snippet.title: The State of Enterprise Operations Security: Our Interview with Rob Lee
snippet.description:
Rob Lee touches on the difference between enterprise IT Security and OT (operations technology) Security during our interview at RSA Conference 2020, yet underscores the importance of uniting the two -- not bifurcating the industry. Lee explains the far-reaching touchpoints of OT security and the potentially catastrophic situations that industrial security faces as a result of our increasingly connected world. He cautions that in light of all of this we shouldn't over-regulate to correct for this.

Rob Lee is a SANS Institute fellow and founder, and CEO at Dragos, Inc.

snippet.title: Humans are Resilient and Adaptive: Our Interview with Bruce Schneier
snippet.description:
Humans are resilient, adaptive, and have a knack for figuring our way out of really bad problems. Bruce Schneier explains why these traits coupled with a security mindset gives us the special ability to make advancements not only to cyber security, but to society as a whole. He theorizes that security professionals have a unique perspective that could -- and should --  influence policy. 

Schneier also shares valuable tips for getting the most out of RSA Conference and all that it offers.

Bruce Schneier is an award-winning author, a world-renowned cryptographer and cybersecurity expert, and an RSA Conference veteran presenter.

snippet.title: The Latest Cyber Attack Techniques to Watch for in 2020: Our Interview with Ed Skoudis
snippet.description:
Ed Skoudis sat down with us at RSA Conference 2020 to talk about deep persistence, attackers "living off the land", and the latest penetration techniques he's seeing. Skoudis also shares with us the two events he looks forward to most every year at RSA Conference, which includes the Cryptographer's Panel.

Ed Skoudis is a SANS Institute fellow and a world-renowned pen-testing expert.

snippet.title: Solving Cybersecurity's Talent Gap | RSAC 2020
snippet.description: The number of unfilled jobs in cybersecurity is expected to reach 4 million by 2022. As our industry faces a critical workforce shortage and talent gap, several experts at RSA Conference 2020 emphasized the need to create a culture of inclusion, as well as where we should be looking to find the cybersecurity experts of tomorrow.

snippet.title: The Future of Supply Chain Security | RSAC 2020
snippet.description: As organizations rapidly change supply chain tactics to meet the demands of evolving global ecosystems, security and risk mitigation need to be top of mind every step of the way. Experts at RSA Conference 2020 weigh in on the state of supply chain security and the vulnerabilities that need our focus.

snippet.title: Preview: Quantum computing's potential is limitless | RSAC 2020
snippet.description:
Steve Grobman, Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer, McAfee, discusses how quantum computing will one day solve some of society's biggest challenges such as a universal vaccine. But it is our current cloud architectures that allow scientists to fight disease and solve many of these challenges, today.

Watch the full keynote here: https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/presentation/time-to-tell

snippet.title: Preview: Designing security to be adopted rather than engineered to be enforced | RSAC 2020
snippet.description:
Wise words from Wendy Nather, Head of Advisory CISOs at Cisco, on engineering security to be adopted vs. enforced.

Watch the full keynote here: https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/presentation/we-the-people-democratizing-security

snippet.title: Preview: Can we build a trustworthy network out of untrustworthy parts? | RSAC 2020
snippet.description:
World-renowned cybersecurity expert, Bruce Schneier, wrestles with the question that results from our global supply chain today. What will it take to build a trustworthy network out of untrustworthy parts? Spoiler alert: more research is needed.

Watch the full keynote here: https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/presentation/how-to-reduce-supply-chain-risk-lessons-from-efforts-to-block-huawei

snippet.title: What SMBs Need to Know to Survive a Ransomware Attack
snippet.description:
Presenters:
Kiersten Todt, President and Managing Partner, Liberty Group Ventures, Managing Director, The Cyber Readiness Institute
Tanya Janca, Founder, Security Trainer and Coach at SheHacksPurple.dev

Ransomware is disruptive and costly and can be catastrophic for some businesses…but it doesn’t have to be. In this webcast, focused on the cybersecurity needs for small to medium-sized businesses, industry leaders will walk you through the steps you can take (regardless of your budget) to ensure that your business survives a ransomware attack.

https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/webcast/42-smb-ransomware

snippet.title: Presenting Virtually? Here’s How to Do It Right.
snippet.description:
Presenters:
Ron Woerner, Cybersecurity Professor, Bellevue University
Lesley Carhart, Principal Threat Hunter, Dragos

With more conferences going virtually, speakers are having to dip their toes into unchartered waters. But, whether you’re new to presenting virtually, have some experience or are well versed in all things external cameras, microphones and lighting, there’s much to learn about delivering a better virtual presentation. Take a quick break from your day to listen to tips from Dr. Ron Woerner, Cybersecurity Professor, Bellevue University and Lesley Carhart, Principal Threat Hunter, Dragos, Inc.

https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/webcast/41-presenting-virtually

snippet.title: RSA Conference 2020 | Highlights from the West Stage: Democratizing Security and the Human Element
snippet.description:
The West Stage at RSA Conference always draws large crowds for some of the most anticipated keynotes of the week. Many of this year's keynotes emphasized the importance of democratizing cybersecurity, collaboration and investing in the human element.

"Security should be designed to be adopted rather than engineered to be enforced."

https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/video/2020-keynote-highlights-west-stage-democratizing-security

snippet.title: RSA Conference 2020 | Keynote Highlights from the South Stage: The Next Frontiers of Cybersecurity
snippet.description: The South Stage hosted some of the most memorable and inspiring keynotes at RSA Conference 2020. It was the predictions and conversations about the next frontiers of cybersecurity that really stole the spotlight on the South Stage this year.

snippet.title: Running Sensitive Workloads on Untrusted Hosts: Project Enarx
snippet.description:
Presenter: Mike Bursell, Chief Security Architect, Red Hat

How fully can you trust the host you run your applications on—not just the software stack, but the sysadmins, BIOS, firmware and more? This webcast will show you how Enarx, a Red Hat open-source project, uses trusted execution environments to allow you to run sensitive applications on fundamentally untrusted hosts.

https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/webcast/40-running-sensitive-workloads-on-untrusted-hosts

snippet.title: The Hugh Thompson Show with Penn & Teller | RSAC 2020
snippet.description: What are the parallels between magic and cybersecurity? Penn & Teller share their thoughts on human behavior when it comes to disinformation, deep fakes, deception, and understanding the art of illusion at the close of RSAC 2020, in a conversation with Hugh Thompson.

snippet.title: 2020 Election and Cybersecurity | Highlights from RSAC 2020
snippet.description:
Voting security and the unique challenges that social networks and cyber threats pose to our democracy, where topics addressed throughout this year’s RSA Conference, as the U.S. looks ahead to the 2020 Presidential Election.

One common thread throughout these discussions is the importance of more resources and training and for us all to come together in solidarity.

snippet.title: My Botnet Always Beats Yours: A Honeypot to Massive Bot Fight Scenes
snippet.description:
Tan Kean Siong, Security Researcher, Independent

The IoT botnet universe is always the fascinating one. This session will share interesting threat hunting stories from a single honeypot to uncover various dramatic fight scenes of IoT botnet herders in the dark, such as botnet operators takeover and wipe out other's botnets, shared backdoored exploit scripts to their peers, constantly develop bots with evolving bot killing capabilities, etc. Pre-Requisites: General understanding of honeypot concept, botnet and IoT.

snippet.title: “I'm Still Standing,” Says Each Cyber-Resilient Device
snippet.description:
Nivedita Aggarwal, Firmware Engineer, Intel
Abhilasha Bhargav-Spantzel, Principal Engineer, Intel

The goals of this talk will be to visit the key aspects of a resilient computer system, provide some industry standard examples, and highlight key learnings from multiple engineering disciplines to rethink resilience in the cyberworld. The hypothesis is that it will allow a path forward to combat the increasing number of cyberthreats that have a high impact on our computer solutions and services. Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of Cryptography and general familarity with Platform Firmware (BIOS, Embedded controller etc.) as well as standards bodies such as NIST.

snippet.title: Dr. Peggy Whitson: Breaking Records and Life at NASA | RSAC 2020
snippet.description: Dr. Peggy Whitson, a veteran astronaut with NASA and the first woman to command the International Space Station, humbly shares the value of diverse teams, how the human element makes every team stronger and how a "farm kid from Iowa" became an accomplished astronaut, who has completed the most spacewalks of any female astronaut and spent the most time in space of any American (665 days).

snippet.title: Tracy Edwards: What It Took to Race Around the World | RSAC 2020
snippet.description: The act of sailing is one of adventure and perseverance. Tracy Edwards, world-renowned sailor and subject of the 2019 documentary, Maiden, shares her harrowing journey of leading the world's first all-women sailing team to circumnavigate the globe. Tracy draws parallels and lessons for the cybersecurity industry. Among them: the value of diverse teams.

snippet.title: RSA Conference 2020: The Highlights
snippet.description: Highlights from RSA Conference 2020 in San Francisco

snippet.title: The Human Element at RSA Conference 2020
snippet.description: This year’s theme – The Human Element – was inspired by the humans that make cybersecurity possible. See the many people that inspired us at RSAC 2020, which took place February 24-28 in San Francisco.

snippet.title: The Hugh Thompson Show, featuring Dr. Lorrie Cranor
snippet.description:
Dr. Lorrie Cranor, Director and Bosch Distinguished Professor, CyLab Security and Privacy Institute, Carnegie Mellon University
Hugh Thompson, Program Committee Chair, RSA Conference

Humans. We're each different, but we have a lot in common, too. We can be predictable, gullible, and deceived. Why? Mystery and magic intersect with human behavior analysis on the Hugh Thompson Show, with security fallibility from renowned expert Dr. Lorrie Cranor.

snippet.title: “We’re Trending!!” When Traffic Is Spiking, How Do You Know It’s Legit?
snippet.description:
Gilit Saporta, Head of Fraud Intelligence, Simplex

How do you identify and mitigate trendy items fraud? This talk will cover examples for hot-items fraud trends from the last decade (from Zhu Zhu Pets 2009, through airlines/travel 2016, to Bitcoin 2019). 
The talk will use an interactive game to decide if traffic spikes are fraud or legit, then share methods for mitigating trendy items fraud to ensure that your system is ready for any type of volatility.
Pre-Requisites: Prior knowledge of ecommerce/fraud.

snippet.title: SIMs, eSIMs and Secure Elements: Dynamic Security for Connected Devices
snippet.description:
Mike Strock, General Secretary, Trusted Connectivity Alliance

SIMs and Secure Elements are well-proven hardware components, enabling various devices to be connected and trusted across multiple applications such as payment, travel and authentication, for example. Global manufacturers, IoT service providers, MNOs and automotive companies are now deploying these technologies to deliver flexible control over a connected object’s lifetime.
Pre-Requisites: General understanding of SIMs and Secure Elements as well as IoT security challenges.

snippet.title: How Generational Psychology Impacts Your Security Strategy
snippet.description:
Ben Smith, Field CTO (US) and Principal Sales Engineer, RSA

Not every generation is alike, nor should they be treated the same way. This session will discuss the importance of understanding how multigenerational psychology and attitudes impact your security strategy. You will learn about best practices to address vulnerabilities, risks, privacy concerns, policies, security controls and communication strategies for each unique generation.
Pre-Requisites: Understanding of security and risk polices and strategies.

snippet.title: Designing Trustworthy AI: A UX Framework
snippet.description:
Carol Smith, Senior Research Scientist, Emerging Technology Division, Carnegie Mellon

Artificial intelligence (AI) holds great promise to empower us with knowledge and scaled effectiveness. To harness the power of AI systems, we can—and must—ensure that we keep humans safe and in control. This session will introduce a new user experience (UX) framework to guide the creation of AI systems that are accountable, de-risked, respectful, secure, honest and usable.
Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of artificial intelligence and machine learning.

snippet.title: Malware and Misconfigurations—The 2nd Annual RSAC SOC Report
snippet.description:
Jessica Bair, Senior Manager, Advanced Threat Solutions, Cisco Security
Percy Tucker, Senior Manager, RSA
Neil Wyler, Principal Threat Hunter, RSA

In this session presenters will share their experience monitoring the RSAC network for stability, security and stats of interest, exploring trends and sharing stories. If you’d like to see what a network looks like when its users know security, know its challenges, should know better and choose to ignore all of that anyway, join us for the always informative RSAC SOC report.

snippet.title: Breaking Password Dependencies: Challenges in the Final Mile at Microsoft
snippet.description:
Lee Walker, Principal Architect, Microsoft
Alexander Weinert, Director of Identity Security, Microsoft Corporation

You must break free of password vulns but the reality is legacy auth woven into the org in various stages of technical debt. Large enterprises may close 95 percent of the holes while attackers find the remaining 5 percent. This session will describe the dangers and the surprises of Microsoft’s journey toward 100 percent remediation with practical guidance to help with yours.
Pre-Requisites: General understanding of core IAM concepts, logging, analytics, and application of MFA concepts.

snippet.title: Equifax Canada Multiclient Collaborative Cybersecurity Audit
snippet.description:
Arif Hameed, Senior Director, Client Security, Equifax

An overview of Equifax Canada’s experience in convincing multiple clients to participate in a single client cybersecurity audit, developing the scope and benefits to both clients and vendor.
Pre-Requisites: Some knowledge around 3rd Party/Supplier Risk.

snippet.title: You Can Stop Stupid
snippet.description:
Dr. Tracy Celaya Brown, President, Go Consulting International
Ira Winkler, Lead Security Principal, Trustwave

Currently when a user causes a loss, it is considered an awareness failing. The reality is that it is a failure of the system that allowed an action to result in loss. Applying safety and counterterrorism sciences, presenters will provide a strategy for creating an environment around users that prevents the initiation of losses, and then mitigates losses should a user make a potentially harmful action.
Pre-Requisites: While any security professional will be able to learn a great deal from this session, professionals with an experience in governance and security strategy will be able to get the most out of it.

snippet.title: Mercedes-Benz and 360 Group: Defending a Luxury Fleet with the Community
snippet.description:
Yuankai Chen, Security Researcher, 360 Technology Group Co., Ltd.
Guy Harpak, Head of Product Security, Mercedes-Benz R&D Tel-Aviv, Daimler

The worldwide Mercedes-Benz community creates and nourishes a mindset which is the foundation for how the company understands, develops and lives cybersecurity. For securing a diverse fleet, it is essential to leverage the power and skills of the security community. The session will include a presentation of the Mercedes-Benz security approach and research done by 360 Group on Mercedes-Benz vehicles.

snippet.title: API Abuse through Mobile Apps: New Attacks, New Defenses
snippet.description:
Skip Hovsmith, Principal Engineer, CriticalBlue

Planning on introducing a mobile app into your product mix? Expect new attacks on your API infrastructure.  Help Shipfast and ShipRaider battle for control of a driver delivery app by exploiting API keys, OAuth2 user authorization, TLS certificate pinning, HMAC call signing, app shielding/hardening, app attestation and more. Overview the unique challenges of API security with mobile clients.
Pre-Requisites: Understanding of basic API request/response operation in HTTP environments. Any exposure to REST, GraphQL, gRPC, streaming, or pub-sub communication is sufficient. Conceptual familiarity with user authentication, API keys, call authorization, and TLS concepts will help.

Detailed understanding of Android, iOS, or backend server programming is NOT required.

snippet.title: You’ll Be Shocked When You See These 10 Tips from Former Industry Analysts!
snippet.description:
John Pescatore, Director, SANS
Greg Young, Vice President, Trend Micro

John Pescatore and Greg Young, who have over 25 years of experience as cybersecurity analysts between them, will present their top 10 tips for how to use your company’s subscription to industry analyst services to your advantage in driving support for changes and enhancements to security processes, architectures and controls. Audience interaction will be maximized—come with questions.
Pre-Requisites: Basic cybersecurity knowledge, some level of management responsibility and experience, some familiarity with industry analyst reports.

snippet.title: How Threat Sharing Hones Your Competitive Edge
snippet.description:
Michael Daniel, President and CEO, Cyber Threat Alliance

The cybersecurity community has discussed intelligence sharing for 30 years, but progress has been slow. One impediment is the idea that sharing threat intelligence gives away an advantage. However, sharing actually enhances your competitive advantage, because no company can detect every cyberthreat all the time. This talk will provide real-world examples of beneficial intelligence sharing.

snippet.title: Data Ethics and Privacy Engineering in Cybersecurity
snippet.description:
Michelle Dennedy, Chief Executive Officer, DrumWave
Lourdes Turrecha, CEO, PIX, LLC
Hilary Wandall, SVP of Privacy Intelligence, TrustArc

What is data ethics? How can we use data ethics, company values, and stakeholder and societal expectations to fuel privacy engineering and create better security products? The panelists will share their vision of a world in which data ethics and privacy engineering are the norm and discuss use cases and takeaways from their experience as privacy leaders in the cybersecurity industry.
Pre-Requisites: General understanding of privacy engineering.

snippet.title: #Psybersecurity: Mental Health Impact of Cyberattacks
snippet.description:
Ryan Louie, Psychiatrist, Vituity

What happens to a person’s mental health during a cyberattack? This session will discuss the impacts on victims and first-responders. Attendees will gain an understanding of mental health conditions that can be caused by cyberattacks. Utilizing this knowledge of psybersecurity, attendees will learn ways to build more resilient mental security networks for better incident response and cyberdefense.

snippet.title: Scaling Key Management: Thousands of Clients, Trillions of Operations
snippet.description:
Yaron Sheffer, Director, Security Technologies Product Development, Intuit

Intuit safeguards financial information for millions of people, and encryption is one of the main tools to protect this data. Learn how Intuit developed a secure and scalable system to manage encryption keys for thousands of internal applications. This session will dive into the system architecture and how it combines a unique-but-conservative cryptographic approach to form a highly scalable solution.
Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of cryptographic terms: encryption, keys etc.

snippet.title: I Find Your Lack of Security Strategy Disturbing
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Merlin Namuth, Program Manager, Tenable

Panelists:
Deborah Blyth, CISO, State of Colorado
Kyriakos Lambros, CEO and Founder, RockCyber, LLC
Matthew Sharp, CISO, Logicworks

Strategy is “a plan of action to accomplish a major goal.” Companies have a large number of security tools, but only a few of them are fully implemented and utilized. Some security leaders can’t obtain enough budget to build out their security program. A strong strategy can solve these. This panel of seasoned security leaders will discuss the different aspects of a strong strategy and results.
Pre-Requisites: Experience running a security program.

snippet.title: Integrating Our DevSecOps Product Pipeline with Software Security Standards
snippet.description:
Altaz Valani, Research Director, Security Compass

Learn how to manage the dynamic nature of both security standards and DevOps technologies in our product development pipeline. Learn to leverage automation of DevOps tools for rapid reaction to standards changes, work with standards groups to introduce risk concepts and tie your innovation pipeline through early stage telemetry, and tightly coupling standards maps with product releases.

snippet.title: Genomics: A New Frontier for Privacy and Security
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Rajeev Chand, Partner and Head of Research, Wing Venture Capital

Panelists:
Dr. Patrick Courneya, Chief Medical Officer, Kaiser Permanente
Kathy Hibbs J.D., Chief Legal and Regulatory Officer, 23andMe
Sharon Terry, President and CEO, Genetic Alliance
Michael Wilson, SVP and Chief Security Officer, Molina Healthcare

As genomics becomes mainstream, what are the opportunities and implications for companies and societies? How do we ensure consumer privacy and protection? What are the security risks? And what does the new frontier mean for the potential for bias? This session will cover the opportunities and challenges in an interactive roundtable discussion with the foremost leaders in the genomics industry.

snippet.title: Hacking your security culture for the cloud
snippet.description:
Brian Riley, Senior Director, Global Cyber Risk Management, Liberty Mutual Insurance

If infrastructure is code, security needs to be code too -- but that reality has tremendous implications on a security team. How can a security team adapt its culture, build the necessary skills, recruit the right talent, and transform itself to support cloud adoption?

snippet.title: Play Smart and Automate the Self-Defense Using AWS Lamda
snippet.description:
Sapna Singh, Senior Security Specialist, Deloitte

Are you and your cloud security team drained of managing noisy security alerts? Live easy, don’t let your cloud environment fall in the hands of cyber criminals. In this talk, the presenter will show how automation of incident response workflow improves the cyber-health by utilizing Lamda function and through various demos.
Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of Cloud and AWS.

snippet.title: Your Democracy Needs You: Taking On Digital Dictatorships
snippet.description:
Brittan Heller, Counsel, Corporate Social Responsibility, Foley Hoag, LLP
Ben Nimmo, Director of Investigations, Graphika

Democracy is under attack and it needs smart defenders. This panel will describe the human cost of repressive regimes’ digital warfare, how threat actors coordinate and hide their activity, the research methods used to expose them, and the limitations of current research. Come connect cybersecurity with human rights and learn how you can protect users against would-be digital dictators.

snippet.title: PSD2 Preparedness? Research Reveals FinTech Risks
snippet.description:
Feike Hacquebord, Senior Threat Researcher, Trend Micro

With the advent of open banking in 2019, banks will have to provide APIs to share customers’ banking data with third parties. Hear the results of our research into the challenges of protecting the larger attack surface created by open banking and the potential security issues associated with APIs, banking apps and protocols.
Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of data sharing, APIs, OFX protocol; Screen scraping.

snippet.title: Follow the Money: The Link between Passwords and Terrorism
snippet.description:
Frank Abagnale, CEO, Abagnale and Associates
Ori Eisen, Founder, Trusona

This co-speaker session will lead the audience on an exploration of motivations behind breaches and what actually happens to the money that nefarious actors gain by exploiting compromised credentials. It is common knowledge that compromised credentials are responsible for the majority of high impact breaches.  A realm that is less known is what do the bad guys actually do with this money.
Pre-Requisites: General interest in Cyber Security

snippet.title: Parlez-Vous Policies? Translate Policies into Powerful Development Tools
snippet.description:
Jen Trahan, Senior Director of Application Security, Discovery Inc.

Corporate security policies are a key component to any business, but unfortunately, by design, they read like legal documents. Are any of your project managers, creatives or engineers reading the policies? And if they are, do they know what it all means? Learn how to make product development teams excited and empowered about security by translating corporate policies into product-focused standards.

snippet.title: Beating Security Inertia with Actionable KPIs
snippet.description:
Harshil Parikh, Sr. Director of Security, Medallia, Inc.

Easy to understand KPIs are very powerful in not just measuring progress but also in encouraging action. Learning from fitness trackers and gaming leaderboards, Medallia built security KPIs for the business to drive measurable (positive) change. This talk will discuss how the team built actionable security KPIs (with examples) and saw increased ownership, accountability and data driven decision making.
Pre-Requisites: Some experience as a security practitioner.

snippet.title: How to Implement a World-Class IAM Program Driven by Access Analytics
snippet.description:
Vishu Mandalika, Director, Information Security, CVS Health

Identity and access management (IAM) plays a key role in enterprise security. This session will present the success story of Aetna, a CVS Health company, in building a world-class IAM program that leverages identity and access data analytics to understand risk and drive the enterprise IAM using a risk-based approach.
Pre-Requisites: General understanding of Identity and Access Management, and Access Provisioning.

snippet.title: First Do No Harm
snippet.description:
Mary Ann Davidson, CSO, Oracle

“Launch nuclear weapons? There’s an app for that,” said no one—yet.  Security geeks enjoy ever-increasing job security as technology-induced risk is all too often band-aided with more technology, without ever asking, “Why does my refrigerator need a firewall?” We need a Hippocratic Oath—“first, do no harm”—especially for security geeks who know all too well, “What could possibly go wrong?”

snippet.title: Implementing the Perfect Travel Laptop Program
snippet.description:
Brian Warshawsky, Manager of Export Control Compliance, University of California Office of the President

Large organizations ignore international travel as a risk. Impenetrable core facilities provide a false sense of security if the weak link crated by border crossings is not controlled. This session will present a case study for implementing a travel laptop program to mitigate this risk.
Pre-Requisites: Understanding of mobile and end-point security as it relates to international travel and border crossing for large organizations.

snippet.title: Collaborating to Improve Open Source Security: How the Ecosystem Is Stepping Up
snippet.description:
Mark Russinovich, Chief Technology Officer, Microsoft Azure

Learn about efforts across industry and open source communities to improve open source security across discovery and notification, fuzzing and other tools, and better review. Mark Russinovich will cover projects focused on a software bill of materials, sharing metadata and tools, securing package managers and source code repositories, and best practices for consumers and producers of software.

snippet.title: Prioritizing the Top 20 on a Shoestring
snippet.description:
William Bailey, VP Information Security, Police & Fire FCU

The “Top 20” controls provides three tiers of 20 security controls that organizations should implement, but even with that, the top 20 controls can be daunting for an organization to achieve. Each control often includes multiple aspects. Where does an organization start when they have a limited budget? The session will highlight where the controls are directly related to various industry breaches.
Pre-Requisites: Understanding of industry terms such as encryption, DLP, but not product specific.

snippet.title: Crushing Biases: Why the Digital Identity Industry Needs Diversity
snippet.description:
Janelle Allen, Board Director, ID Pro
Pamela Dingle, Director of Identity Standards, Microsoft

We may be unknowingly and unwittingly influenced by our own biases. By having people with differing points of view on our teams, we can avoid building products with blind spots. Including people with diverse backgrounds building digital identity products can lead to providing the gift of an identity to forgotten individuals and give them a voice and power.
Pre-Requisites: Some understanding of the digital identity technology, facial recognition, biometrics, authentication etc. would be beneficial.

snippet.title: SDLC and 62443: Build It In, Don’t Bolt It On
snippet.description:
Shoshana Wodzisz, Global Product Security Leader, Rockwell Automation

Successfully building security directly into the product life cycle and having the resulting processes certified to IEC 62443 demands a shift in how you think about security both culturally and technically. In this session, you will learn the do’s and don’ts to effectively implement changes and enable your company to take a more collaborative approach to product security.

snippet.title: First Line of Open Source IAM: Just Sudo That!
snippet.description:
Peter Czanik, Open Source Evangelist, One Identity

Sudo is open source IAM installed everywhere, but still mostly known as a prefix for administrative commands. Learn how to create the building blocks of your first line of IAM in a Linux/UNIX environment via lesser known functions, like checksum verification, session recording, plugins and more—and how to log and alert on critical events in real time using built-in tools and syslog.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of Linux administration and security.

snippet.title: Securing the Genome: The Intersection of Genomics, Cloud and Big Data
snippet.description:
Brian Castagna, Chief Information Security Officer, Seven Bridges
Brandi Davis-Dusenbery, Chief Scientific Officer, Seven Bridges

Our genomes represent unchangeable personal information about ourselves. Yet within these genomic datasets are secrets that can unlock new medical therapies. The scale, velocity and complexity of genomic datasets make cloud the best place for this work. The adoption of cloud by pharma has lagged due to security concerns. This talk will explore the security and compliance of genomic data in the cloud.

snippet.title: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure: You’ve Come a Long Way, Baby
snippet.description:
Katie Moussouris, Chief Executive Officer, Luta Security
Chris Wysopal, Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer, Veracode

Examples abound of clashes between security researchers and companies over disclosing software flaws, yet there is little quantifiable data delving into vulnerability disclosure. With the help of new research data on coordinated disclosure, this presentation will focus on the views of security researchers and organizations alike to highlight behaviors, preferences and established practices.
Pre-Requisites: Understanding of vulnerability disclosure processes and policies.

snippet.title: Solving for DevOps Auditors with Automated Compliance
snippet.description:
Shannon Lietz, Director, Intuit
Michelle Nikulshin, Director, Information Security, Intuit, Inc.

Automated compliance when it comes to DevOps? It wasn’t what we expected either, until we found ourselves solving DevSecOps challenges with auditors in unique ways. We realized that code could be used to assert and evaluate controls as just another part of a software stack. Come join the discussion as we talk about how to code security controls and check them as part of a securability score.

snippet.title: Does Artificial Intelligence Need a General Counsel?
snippet.description:
Alan Brill, Senior Managing Director, Kroll
Stacy Scott, Managing Director, Cyber Risk, Kroll

AI and deep learning systems operate within a series of laws, regulations and user expectations. Some may not be top of mind to development technicians but can represent significant risk to an organization. This session will focus on risks where law, regulations and litigation intersect with AI/deep learning systems. Through case studies, learn how to focus on these risks in your AI projects.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of artificial intelligence.

snippet.title: The Age of Economic Warfare: What to Expect in This New Reality
snippet.description:
Galina Antova, Co-Founder, Claroty

The world runs on industrial control systems, and they are valuable targets for attackers seeking to advance geopolitical agendas. This session will address the scenarios of economic warfare leveraging cyberattacks on infrastructure, what it means in terms of potential impact to your organization, common pitfalls from the field and how to avoid them.
Pre-Requisites: Understanding of network security fundamentals and Industrial Control System fundamentals.

snippet.title: Chronicle of the Supply Chain Attack and Two Attack Strategies
snippet.description:
Byeongjae Kim, Malware General Researcher, Korea Internet and Security Agency (KISA)
Taewoo Lee, Malware Researcher, Korea Internet and Security Agency (KISA)

The attacker group involved in ASUS incident is actively targeting companies in specific countries as well as global companies. KrCERT analyzed various supply chain attacks targeting Korean companies, and confirmed artifacts, malware code similarities. In addition, the team identified two strategies for supply chain attack (SW development environment penetration, update server penetration).

snippet.title: The Modus Operandi of EV Certificates Fraudsters: Findings from the Field
snippet.description:
David Maimon, Professor, Georgia State University

New research results show the prevalence and value of SSL/TLS certificates on the dark web, including availability, packaging, pricing and purchasing process.  Digital transformation has increased our reliance on encryption, but cybercriminals now use encryption SSL/TLS certificates in attacks. Learn about the established SSL/TLS certificate marketplace on the dark web that enables these attacks.
Pre-Requisites: General understanding of the role of encryption in security and privacy and the use of SSL/TLS certificates in encryption.

snippet.title: Advanced Persistence Threats: The Future of Kubernetes Attacks
snippet.description:
Ian Coldwater, Lead Platform Security Engineer, Salesforce
Brad Geesaman, Security Consultant, DARKBIT

As Kubernetes grows in popularity, the sophistication of attackers will improve, and security by obscurity will no longer be sufficient. What could an attacker who understands Kubernetes at a deep level be capable of? Let’s explore the dark corners of clusters and shine a light on several new advanced attacks on Kubernetes, and learn how to detect and prevent them using practical, proven methods.Pre-Requisites: Familiarity with Linux and networking fundamentals, containers and Kubernetes.

snippet.title: Augmenting Intelligence: Machines as Super Assistants for Security Experts
snippet.description:
Matteo Dell'Amico, Senior Principal Researcher, NortonLifeLock

How to deal effectively with security data? It’s way too much for humans to handle, and automation has important limitations. Luckily, virtues of humans and machines are complementary: people can be genuinely creative and insightful, while computers easily sift through huge data. The session will discuss a vision of systems where ML complements human expertise rather than replacing it.Pre-Requisites: General background on security.

snippet.title: Air-Gapping Is Overrated: Pressing a Red-Button via a Multifunction Printer
snippet.description:
Ben Nassi, Ph.D. Student/Security Reseacher, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev

This session will show how attackers can exploit the light sensitivity of a multifunction printer for infiltrating commands to a malware installed on an isolated organization. It will demonstrate the attack on a real organization using (1) a laser attached to a tripod stand; (2) a laser carried by a drone; and (3) a hijacked smart bulb.

snippet.title: Cyber-Hygiene for All: An Introduction to the CIS Controls
snippet.description:
Phyllis Lee, Senior Director Controls, Center for Internet Security

The CIS Controls are one of the most popular cybersecurity standards in the world, used by auditors, CISOs and security professionals like you. This session will explore the CIS Controls and highlight the free tools, techniques and guidance CIS provides to overcome pitfalls and barriers to adoption in your organization.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of IT terminology.

snippet.title: Securing the Budget You Need! Translating Security Risks to Business Impacts
snippet.description:
Jim Mirochnik, Senior Partner, CEO, HALOCK Security Labs

Securing the right budget is often harder to do than performing the project requiring the budget.  If your goal is to secure the budget you need vs. prioritizing into the budget you’re given, then you need a different approach than what you’ve been using.  Learn how an industry-proven methodology (DoCRA) can help you communicate to the C-Suite in a new way and receive the budget you truly need.Pre-Requisites: An appreciation for the difficulty in justifying technical projects in business terms is a plus.

snippet.title: Suricata: 10 Years Strong Bringing the Best in Network Threat Detection
snippet.description:
Eric Leblond, Suricata Developer, The Open Information Security Foundation (OISF) / Suricata
Peter Manev, CSO, Stamus Networks, LLC

Suricata is a 10-year-old open source network threat detection engine used worldwide by global Fortune 100 companies. This talk will illustrate Suricata’s as a critical point for SOOC practitioners by spotlighting use cases of its versatility and the latest features such as datasets, XDP and lua used to maximize demanding deployments scenarios.

snippet.title: Clearing the Clouds: Incident Response in AWS (Isn’t as Bad as You Thought)
snippet.description:
Kristy Westphal, VP, CSIRT, Union Bank

As you dive deeper into AWS, you realize that the architecture and various components consist of a jungle of new terms and products uniquely Amazon.  However, your approach to security incident response isn’t necessarily as unique. Yes, new skills are needed, but the session will also demystify the approach by looking at detailed use cases of how to respond to AWS-specific security incidents.
Pre-Requisites: Some understanding of AWS, incident response principles, security analysis techniques. This session will participate in polling. To participate please be sure to download the RSA Conference app prior to the session.

snippet.title: The 5 Most Dangerous New Attack Techniques and How to Counter Them
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Alan Paller, Research Director and Founder, SANS Institute

Panelists:
Heather Mahalik, Senior Instructor and Director of Digital Intelligence, SANS Institute and Cellebrite
Ed Skoudis, Instructor, SANS Institute
Johannes Ullrich, Dean of Research, SANS Technology Institute

What are the most dangerous new techniques attackers are employing? How do they work? How can you stop them? What’s coming next and how can you prepare? This fast-paced briefing features three people best positioned to provide answers: the nation’s top expert on mobile forensics, the director of the Internet Storm Center and the top hacker exploits expert in the US. Panelists will also answer audience questions.

snippet.title: On The Edge Of Something Big: Security’s Next Frontier
snippet.description:
Ken Xie, Founder, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, Fortinet

The convergence of physical and digital worlds is triggering an era of hyperconnectivity, creating billions of edges and attack vectors.  With the Internet becoming integrated in our lives and the emergence of 5G and SD-WAN, security must be woven into every transaction. It will operate as part of the network, adapting in real-time to network changes, ensuring new devices, configurations, or data paths don’t introduce risk or compromise compliance. As ML and AI are woven into the security network environment, events can be managed autonomously, saving critical resources and enabling focus on strategic concerns.

snippet.title: Rives: Declaration of Independence
snippet.description: John Rives opens the Thursday afternoon keynote session at RSA Conference 2020 in San Francisco with his spoken word, "Declaration of Independence".

snippet.title: Hacking Stress in Cybersecurity Operations
snippet.description:
Dr. Celeste Paul, Researcher, National Security Agency

Anyone in this business knows the excitement of working information security also comes with an emotional and physical cost. We are just now learning how to talk about mental health in the information security community. The Hierarchy of Hacker Needs will help frame the discussion of stress in the information security environment that leads to job dissatisfaction and burnout.Pre-Requisites: General knowledge about the information security community.

snippet.title: The Industrial Cyberthreat Landscape: 2019 Year in Review
snippet.description:
Robert Lee, CEO, Dragos, Inc.

The industrial cyberthreat landscape is constantly changing with new adversaries, new vulnerabilities and new attacks as well as lessons learned from incident response cases. This presentation will reveal new cases, threats, and lessons learned with the annual Dragos Year in Review reports from the industrial control system (ICS) community. Participants will leave with actionable recommendations.Pre-Requisites: General familiarity with ICS/industrial environments. Does not require a deep  technical knowledge. It's a ""technical"" session in that it discusses technical topics but anyone in info sec at all would benefit from this session.

snippet.title: Geopolitical Risks, Elections and Cybersecurity
snippet.description:
Juliette Kayyem, Professor, Harvard’s Kennedy School of Government
Admiral James Stavridis, Retired Four-Star Officer, US Navy

Admiral James Stavridis, US Navy (Ret.), Fmr. NATO Supreme Allied Commander, PreVeil board member, 12th Dean of Tuft’s Fletcher School and chief international diplomacy and security analyst for NBC News, will join Prof. Juliette Kayyem from Harvard’s Kennedy School, former Asst. Sec. at DHS and CNN security analyst, in conversation on cyberthreats to US national security, democracy and industry.

snippet.title: Assessor versus Assessed: Debates on PCI DSS Topics
snippet.description:
Jacob Ansari, Senior Manager, Schellman & Company, LLC
Todd Aument, Head of Data Security Governance, Square

PCI DSS compliance, despite, or perhaps because of its maturity and extent, presents a number of complex challenges to a variety of organizations. This session will present the perspectives of both an experienced assessor and experienced GRC lead on issues such as segmentation, managing user credentials, and scanning and vulnerability management.
Pre-Requisites: Working knowledge of PCI DSS requirements. Networking basics to understand nuances of scoping discussion.

snippet.title: Election Info Ops: Stories from the Social Media Frontlines
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Donie O’Sullivan, Reporter, CNN

Panelists:
Camille Francois, Chief Innovation Officer, Graphika
Toni Gidwani, Analyst Lead, Threat Analysis Group, Google
Nathaniel Gleicher, Head of Cybersecurity Policy, Facebook
Yoel Roth, Head of Site Integrity, Twitter

Since the 2016 US presidential election, information operations trolls have been refining their techniques on audiences in the US and around the world. In this panel, hear from the experts in the trenches from Facebook and Twitter, to Graphika and Stanford’s Internet Observatory who are monitoring and defending against disinformation campaigns in the run-up to the 2020 elections.

snippet.title: Do Investors Care about Cyber-Risk?
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Jacob Olcott, Vice President, BitSight

Panelists:
Derek Bingham, Vice President, Global Investment Research, Goldman Sachs
Derek Vadala, CEO, Moody’s Cyber Risk Assessments
Dr. Chenxi Wang, General Partner, Rain Capital

Investors are increasingly concerned about the financial impact of cyber-incidents on their investments. How do investors factor cyber-risk in their decisions? What challenges do they face in obtaining security data? Can companies become better investments by demonstrating strong security? Join some of the world’s leading investors and financial analysis firms to hear their perspectives. This session will participate in polling. To participate please be sure to download the RSA Conference app prior to the session.

snippet.title: Challenges in Android Supply Chain Analysis
snippet.description:
Łukasz Siewierski, Reverse Engineer, Google

Android supply chain is a complex ecosystem of software and hardware companies, which include SoC manufacturers, OEMs, carriers and more. The result of this is an Android system image. This talk will show real-world examples of where assumptions can go wrong and common pitfalls when looking at Android system images as opposed to the analysis of an independent application.
Pre-Requisites: General understanding of application-based malicious software and security concepts like sandboxing or attack surface. Ability to read decompiled Java code.

snippet.title: How to GRC Your DevOps
snippet.description:
Susan Allspaw Pomeroy, Technology Compliance Manager, Fastly, Inc.

DevOps practices have helped businesses think differently about building systems in more reliable and resilient ways for 10 years.  Standard GRC approaches haven’t quite evolved to complement DevOps concepts. The speaker will talk about ways to calibrate GRC and DevOps needs so that they can work in reciprocal ways that benefit each other and not just meet their own goals in disconnected ways.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of GRC concepts and the different frameworks that that exist.

snippet.title: Shadow IT and Shadow Remote Access. How to Find It (for free!)
snippet.description:
John Strand, Owner, Black Hills Information Security

From the TeamViewer attack to the Nuance attack, we are just now beginning to see how often vendors have direct access to our networks. And many times, they never asked, it was just baked into the product or service they provide.

snippet.title: Untangling SaaS Security in the Enterprise
snippet.description:
Rehman Khan, Director Cloud and Data Security, TD Ameritrade
Brajesh Moni, Senior Cloud Security Consultant, TD Ameritrade

Organizations continue to move business capabilities and critical business information to SaaS applications.  Learn about TDA’s controls framework that aligns with security policies and vendor management processes.  Attendees will learn about integration patterns that provide specific security controls to protect data. Cover business use cases and solutions that solve BYOD challenges.
Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of SaaS applications and cloud security, risk management and security governance. Technical knowledge of CASB and Identity Management solutions.

snippet.title: Preventing an Enterprise Win10 Rollout Being Remotely Controlled and Ransomed
snippet.description:
Murray Goldschmidt, Chief Operating Officer, Sense of Security Pty Ltd

A case-study for static and dynamic testing of Win10 enterprise rollout images. How this saved an organization from deploying an image that would have resulted in 10,000+ machines being remotely controlled by an adversary for ransom. Hardening reviews, configuration management, app whitelisting effectiveness, encryption recovery, and the ability to detect and defeat sleeper malware are described.

snippet.title: The First 6 Months as a CISO Determines Success or Failure
snippet.description:
Michael Coates, CEO, Altitude Networks

Setup your new CISO role for success. Learn from the former CISO of Twitter and Mozilla. First, the importance of a restraining from action and embarking on a “listening tour,” the fallacy of CISO accountability for all data breaches, how to build your strategic security roadmap and gain executive support, and the core essences of team building in a negative unemployment security market.Pre-Requisites: Attendees should have experience leading security divisions and programs and an understanding of challenges balancing technical, organization, and governance risks. Best suited for those with a desire to be a successful CISO.

snippet.title: The Most Memorable Moments From RSAC 2020 USA
snippet.description:
Britta Glade, RSA Conference, Director, Content and Curation
Hugh Thompson, RSA Conference, Program Committee Chair

What were some of the standout moments and most buzzworthy topics from RSAC 2020? Find out as Britta Glade and Hugh Thompson weigh in during this podcast that was recorded in the midst of all the Conference action.

snippet.title: Test or Be Tested: Adversary Emulation with Atomic Red Team
snippet.description:
Chris Rothe, Chief Product Officer, Red Canary

Whether it’s the result of a misunderstanding or a misconfiguration, security software doesn’t always work as expected. Red Canary built Atomic Red Team to validate assumptions about the telemetry produced by EDR tools. Since 2017, more than 80 individuals have contributed to the project, growing it from a humble set of basic tests to a robust framework with atomics for nearly 160 ATT&CK techniques.
Pre-requisites: General understanding of information security, detection and red teaming.

snippet.title: Human Dimensions of Active Defense
snippet.description:
Leonard Bailey, Head of Cybersecurity Unit/Special Counsel for National Security, U.S. Department of Justice

Active defense is typically only discussed as technical operations. This session will instead focus on human-directed countermeasures involving intelligence gathering and reacquisition of stolen data. Using real-world examples and new guidance from DOJ, it will identify legal red lines and policy considerations when gathering information from criminal sources and reacquiring stolen data online.
Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of the policy debates surrounding active defense. While this presentation will include legal concepts, no prior familiarity of those is required.

snippet.title: Third-Party Code: Where Data Breaches, Election Meddling, Ad Fraud Converge
snippet.description:
Mark Grantz, Supervisory Special Agent, US Secret Service
Chris Olson, CEO, Founder, The Media Trust

The presenters will examine a recent case to show how fraudsters and foreign adversaries use phishing redirects, payload drops, crypto-mining, keylogging and bloatware to infiltrate social media, apps and news sites. The goal is to underscore the urgent need to hold to account third-party code suppliers, who know our and our children’s behaviors, preferences, and other sensitive information.
Pre-Requisites: Understanding of website operations. DevSecOps and app/sec experience helpful.

snippet.title: Test and Learn: Securing Connected Products and Services
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Bree Fowler, Multimedia Content Creator, Electronics, Consumer Reports

Panelists:
Betsy Cooper Director, Aspen Institute, Aspen Tech Policy Hub
John Dickson, Principal, Denim Group
Ben Moskowitz Director, Consumer Reports, Digital Lab

With ongoing threats to data and security, the need for solutions is essential. Consumer Reports launched the Digital Lab to expand testing of smart products (i.e., routers and TVs) and delve into transparency, accountability and choice. The session will explore output from the lab: how to compare products based on privacy and security, improve privacy policies and hold bad actors responsible.
Pre-Requisites: An understanding of IoT security techniques and the specific security threats targeting IoT devices.

snippet.title: Analyst View: Cybersec/Risk/Governance Jobs, Skills, Pay Review and Forecast
snippet.description:
David Foote, Chief Analyst, Foote Partners, LLC

Hear the latest from tech labor market guru analyst David Foote on how tech professionals in these four areas are being compensated in salary and skills/certifications pay, how these jobs will evolve over the next three years, and what’s working in managing these pros in an environment of disruption and new innovative technologies. How do we compete for and manage these practitioners?

snippet.title: Going Beyond the Basics: An Advanced Privileged User Management Program
snippet.description:
Kurt Lieber, CISO, Aetna

This session will look at bringing a risk-based approach to managing privileged access, including using machine learning to identify anomalous behavior and making real-time access control decisions based on risk instead of static credentials.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of access recertifications, authentication, password management, and/or provisioning.

snippet.title: Understanding and Disrupting Offensive Innovations
snippet.description:
Dmitri Alperovitch, Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer, CrowdStrike
Jason Healey, Senior Research Scholar, Columbia University School of International and Public Affairs

Which innovations have given attackers the most advantage over defenders, at the greatest scale and least cost? Cyberattackers have had the advantage over defenders for decades. To change this, defenders need to understand important innovations, how they evolve, and identify which ones are easiest to disrupt. This talk will discuss recent research to disrupt the systemic advantage of attackers.
Pre-Requisites: Basic cybersecurity knowledge.

snippet.title: Aviation Cybersecurity: Technology and Teamwork
snippet.description:
Pete Cooper, MD, Aerospace Sandbox
Patrick Kiley, Principal Security Consultant, Rapid7
Ken Munro, Partner, Pen Test Partners

The aviation industry is digitized, interlinked and interdependent. The technology used is similar to many other sectors so what does that mean for the vulnerabilities on that technology? This presentation will introduce you to some of the technical challenges facing the aviation industry, the efforts and partnerships to manage those challenges, and what other sectors can learn from that journey.

snippet.title: What Really Happens When Hackers Attack Medical Devices
snippet.description:
Michael Kijewski, CEO, MedCrypt

This session will review a hack on healthcare delivery organizations, with emphasis on medical devices as entry points. FDA guidance and evolution will then be reviewed to learn how medical devices are regulated. Closing with a live demo of a hacker attacking an HDO network and giving attendees a chance to interact with code that could be implemented on a device and how it works to ensure data integrity.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of how product security relates to a broader networked ecosystem.

snippet.title: How Smart Cities Become Wise
snippet.description:
Gary Hayslip, Director of IT Security, CISO, Softbank Investment Advisors

The movement to make cities smarter transforming municipal governments worldwide into disparate ecosystems of cutting-edge technologies are also making cities unique targets for cybercriminals. To manage these threats requires security professionals who are comfortable managing risk across both legacy and smart technologies to create security programs that allow innovation safely amid the chaos.Pre-Requisites: General knowledge on the rise of smart cities, various new smart projects and technologies and how these initiatives are supposed to serve their citizens and enable them to be more engaged with their government and the community, including converged infrastructures and the risks these new ecosystems pose to cities. Some knowledge on the roles of a CISO and how they would approach managing traditional enterprise risk and how risk management on this scale will require efforts that are not in traditional risk management frameworks.

snippet.title: The Value of Human-Centered Research in Identity and Access Management
snippet.description:
Juliette Hainline, UX Researcher, Google
Charlotte Massey, UX Researcher, Google
Keita Wangari, Senior UX Researcher, Google

We know that products are most effective when they’re both useful and usable for real people in real contexts. Presenters will share success stories that demonstrate the value of user-experience research in the enterprise identity, access and security space, and discuss practical ways to incorporate user research into your product development life cycle so you can identify critical user needs.

snippet.title: When Privacy Meets Populism: How People Are Influencing the Data Debate
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Julie Brill, Corporate Vice President, Microsoft

Panelists:
Helen Dixon, Commissioner for Data Protection, Data Protection Commission Ireland
Alastair Mactaggart, Founder and Chair, Californians for Consumer Privacy

RSA gathers in a city that banned facial recognition technology and the state with the most advanced privacy law in the US. These laws might be just the start. Experts debate the effectiveness of privacy activity in the US and Europe, how the world is responding to the privacy movement, and what populism and the desire to “take down” big tech could mean for enhanced privacy protections.Pre-Requisites: General knowledge and interest in data privacy and politics.

snippet.title: Automotive/IoT Network Exploits: From Static Analysis to Reliable Exploits
snippet.description:
Jonathan Brossard, CEO, Moabi

Moabi just reported CVE-2016-10743 and CVE-2019-10064, which are not public. The first one relates to an accidental fix in Hostapd 2.5; the second one is current and affects all versions of Hostapd including the current ones (there is no patch). Both relate to the fact that Hostapd is relaying on PRNGs from the libc to generate various cryptographic keys, while never actually seeding those PRNGs.
Pre-Requisites: Technical experience in Reverse Engineering and a working knowledge of everything ranging from assembly to C auditing to compiler mitigations and exploits writing.

snippet.title: Over the Top Security!
snippet.description:
Daksha Bhasker, Principal Cybersecurity Architect, Comcast NBC Universal

Over the top (OTT) solutions are proliferating rapidly, along with global Internet penetration that has reached almost 4.4 billion people. With access to vast reserves of consumer and business information across the globe, that is attractive to scammers, security designs and architectures for OTT solutions, are quite distinct from traditional “walled garden” architectures. Over the top security is here!Pre-Requisites: Understanding of security fundamentals and the basics of security design and architecture.

snippet.title: 20 Years In: Security’s Grand Challenges, Then and Now
snippet.description:
Andy Ellis, Chief Security Officer, Akamai Technologies, Inc.

Spoiler: It’s not the user’s fault. Security’s grand challenges have evolved significantly since the 1990s, when security professionals mostly needed intelligence, scale and layered solutions. Today’s teams struggle with an overabundance of implicit trust, know their businesses are over reliant on passwords, and face skills gaps for managing architectures assembled from third-party sources—creating exposure, especially as they deal with cloud migration under shared-responsibility models. Akamai CSO Andy Ellis will show how security’s grand challenges have shifted, discusses his experiences mitigating advanced threats—and provides insight into evolving future threats.

snippet.title: Tricky Issues and Practical Guidance in Medical Device Cybersecurity
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Jami Vibbert, Partner, Venable LLP

Panelists:
Steven Christey, Principal Cybersecurity Engineer, The MITRE Corporation
Andrea Coravos, CEO, Elektra Labs
Jeff Dunifon, Privacy Counsel, Zimmer Biomet

In this session, hear from FDA’s Suzanne Schwartz and a global privacy officer of a med device company on how to effectively and practically protect medical devices through a robust cybersecurity program.  Panelists will discuss FDA’s pre- and post-market guidance on cybersecurity management, the Joint Security Plan for Medical Devices and Health IT, and how to handle implementation challenges.

snippet.title: Supply Chain Security in the Software Era
snippet.description:
Beau Woods, Cyber Safety Advocate, I Am The Cavalry

Software has eaten the world and its supply chain gives us heartburn. Recent incidents have revealed risks in the sprawling, opaque web of code components that make modern organizations run. This presentation will outline a framework for understanding supply chain risks and provides concrete recommendations for policy makers and company executives based on real-world examples.

Pre-Requisites: Understanding of technology drivers, innovation, procurement, general security issues, or other related topics would be helpful.

snippet.title: Evolution of AIOps to Watch Over Smart City IoT
snippet.description:
Darren Bennett, Deputy Director, Chief Information Security Officer, City of San Diego
Thomas Caldwell, CTO, Techniche

In light industry including physical infrastructure, more smart devices are being connected to networks. Smart cities are abundant with sensors, video cameras and facility assets. Monitoring these assets for availability, performance and cybersecurity is a challenge. AIOps, including AI-Bots can leverage AI/ML for operational automation and to analyze cross-domain context and alerts in seconds.Pre-Requisites: Knowledge of operational system management including cybersecurity.

snippet.title: Beyond the Ballot Box: Securing America’s Supporting Election Technology
snippet.description:
Aaron Wilson, Senior Director of Election Security, Center for Internet Security

How are we securing the election systems no one is talking about, yet are the most at risk components of our election infrastructure? Come hear from the Center for Internet Security on how their recommendations are being used to secure and verify America’s Internet-connected election technology. Results from their verification pilot project will be shared and discussed.
Pre-Requisites: General awareness of the security risks to democratic elections from nation state and other actors. General understanding of web application architecture concepts and the threats posed to various parts of the technology stack. General understanding of how system verification processes are typically structured and executed.

snippet.title: Secure Your Code from Open Source Vulnerabilities
snippet.description:
Megha Dixit, Technical Program Manager Security, Salesforce

Developers are the “smart” community; they would like to churn out the features faster. In the quest of making the feature work as expected and with so much of lucrative options available from the open source world, it has become one of the most popular ways to get the feature working. Unless deeply reviewed and monitored, it has even enabled the “hacker” community to find easy ways to hack system.Pre-Requisites: Basic development, security and devops knowledge and an understanding of security tools.

snippet.title: How to Harness Dev and Their Native Tools to Accelerate DevSecOps
snippet.description:
Cindy Blake, Sr. Security Evangelist, GitLab

This step-by-step view through the developers’ workflow will show exactly where application security can be embedded. A case study will show what can be achieved and a brief demo of an actual developer pipeline will help the audience see exactly how app sec can become iterative, automated and embedded into the automated DevOps processes.
Pre-Requisites: Knowledge of the methodologies and tools their development teams use is helpful but not required.

snippet.title: How to Build Engaging, Low Cost Awareness Videos
snippet.description:
Jill Barclay, Cybersecurity Awareness and Communications Lead, CommonSpirit Health

Video is a great marketing tool used to educate an audience about cybersecurity best practices, which is often perceived as too technical and complex or not a real threat to everyday life. Learn how to create relatable and engaging videos that deliver a better understanding of cybersecurity risks. The speaker will break down the process for creating fun, consumable and budget-friendly awareness videos.

snippet.title: Hunting Linux Malware for Fun and Flags
snippet.description:
Marc-Etienne M.Léveillé, Senior Malware Researcher, ESET

Server-side Linux malware is a real threat now. Unfortunately, as for its Windows counterpart, most system administrators are inadequately trained to analyze and understand the threats that their infrastructures are facing. This tutorial aims at creating an environment where Linux professionals have the opportunity to study such threats safely and in a time-effective fashion.

snippet.title: Proactive Directory: Practical Counterdefenses to Securing Active Directory
snippet.description:
Matthew McWhirt, Senior Manager, FireEye Mandiant

This talk will focus on the pillars of Active Directory topologies, privileged accounts and endpoint hardening—to educate the audience on the practical and proven Active Directory configurations that will harden an environment, and prevent against techniques that attackers leverage to compromise enterprise environments.
Pre-Requisites: Working understanding of Active Directory, Threat actor tactics and methods, Group Policy, Authentication Silos and
Identity and Authentication services.

snippet.title: Measuring Vulnerability Remediation Strategies with Real-World Data
snippet.description:
Dr. Wade Baker, Partner and Co-Founder, Cyentia Institute
Dr. Benjamin Edwards, Senior Data Scientist, Cyentia Institute

How do you assess a vulnerability management program? This talk will outline four data-driven measures that give a holistic view of vulnerability management: coverage, efficiency, velocity and capacity. Presenters will compare these measures across several hundred organizations, highlight practices of exceptional programs, and demonstrate how any organization can apply these measures to their program.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of various approaches to vulnerability management. A basic understanding of statistics.

snippet.title: Using Automation for Proactive Cloud Environment Incident Response
snippet.description:
Benjamin Potter, Global Security Lead, Well-Architected, Amazon Web Services

How can cloud customers outsmart well-funded, automated adversaries? Are you aware of how to employ canaries that will trigger automated investigation and response processes? Can cloud provide material advantages for thwarting an advanced persistent threat (APT)? Come to this technically deep session to learn about cloud incident response automation concepts, including real life examples with demos.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of how cloud providers expose API's for customers to use.

snippet.title: Build Your Own IDaaS: Lessons from Year One
snippet.description:
Sean Farrell, Lead Identity Engineer, Thomson Reuters
Jon Lehtinen, Principal Identity Engineer, Thomson Reuters

Build or buy? Do we have the staff, talent and budget to operate a new security service if we decide to build? In this talk, the presenters will deconstruct the myth that you need large teams and expensive software to run cloud-native identity-as-a-service platforms for your enterprise by sharing their experience building their own at Thomson Reuters and posting big annual savings along the way.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of docker, AWS, containerization, YAML & orchestration platforms.

snippet.title: How FIDO2 and WebAuthn Stop Account Takeovers
snippet.description:
Jen Tong, Security Advocate, Google

User authentication is hard. It’s a constant struggle between ease of use and effectiveness. User education has not been sufficient. Fortunately, better options already exist. U2F has proven effective over the years, and its successor, WebAuthn, is even better. This talk will discuss how FIDO2 and WebAuthn provide strong auth, using them to protect yourself, and how to add your own support.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of password based authentication and  public key cryptography.

snippet.title: Her Story: A Journey to Cybersecurity Leadership in the Middle East
snippet.description:
Dr. Reem Al-Shammari, CISO, Team Leader Information Security, Kuwait Oil Company

Dr. Reem Al-Shammari will share her journey to leadership in Kuwait in business and the community. From developing a strategy to bringing organizations together to collaborate, she has tremendous experience speaking and getting heard as a cyber leader who always thrives to aspire and inspire.

snippet.title: What’s in Your Risk Assessment?
snippet.description:
Steve Reznik, Director, Operational Risk Management, ADP
Allison Seidel, Senior Risk Specialist, PNC Bank, PNC Bank

Industry guidelines, standards and regulations often recommend or require a “risk assessment.” However, not all assessments are created equal. Many methods, although compliant, are not useful for running the business. This session will accelerate your risk assessment approach to keep up with the evolving regulatory landscape, while meeting stakeholder demand for higher quality decision data.
Pre-Requisites: Some experience with “risk assessment” would be helpful. This session will participate in polling. To participate please be sure to download the RSA Conference app prior to the session.

snippet.title: The Future of Transportation Relies on Strong Cybersecurity
snippet.description:
Mary T. Barra, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, General Motors Company

General Motors’ vision is to create a world with zero crashes, to save lives; zero emissions, so future generations can inherit a healthier planet; and zero congestion, so customers get back a precious commodity—time. Technology is a key enabler to achieving this vision by developing connected, electrified and autonomous vehicles that will help us get there. General Motors’ Chairman and CEO Mary Barra will discuss why it’s important for the automotive industry to work together to secure a strong enterprise-wide cybersecurity posture and why STEM education and careers will be even more critical in the coming years.

snippet.title: Rives: Buttons Five Years
snippet.description: John Rives opens the Thursday morning keynote session at RSA Conference 2020 in San Francisco with his spoken word, "Buttons Five Years".

snippet.title: IoT Bug Hunting: From Shells to Responsible Disclosure
snippet.description:
Shaun Mirani, Security Analyst, Independent Security Evaluators
Ian Sindermann, Associate Security Analyst 2, Independent Security Evaluators

Internet of things (IoT) have always been vulnerable. This study proved that security controls put in place by device manufacturers are insufficient against attacks carried out by remote adversaries. This talk will summarize some of the best stories from the research project aimed to uncover and leverage new techniques to circumvent these new security controls in embedded devices.Pre-Requisites: General familiarity with what IoT devices are and a cursory understanding of HTTP, network traffic analysis, *NIX shell command execution, DNS resolution, and basic web application vulnerabilities.

snippet.title: Hacking Society
snippet.description:
Bruce Schneier, Security Technologist, Researcher and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School

A computer security mindset is essential to understanding the security of complex technological systems. As we move into a world where all social, economic and political systems are to some extent technological, we need to extend this way of thinking. Come learn how to hack—and then defend—society’s core systems: elections, the market economy, lawmaking, tax policy, journalism and more.

snippet.title: On the CANT Bus, No One Can Hear You Scream
snippet.description:
Tim Brom, Managing Senior Security Researcher, GRIMM

Bit-level attacks against the CAN bus were described in ICS-ALERT-17-209-01, but what are the practical implications of these attacks, and what hardware is required to perform these attacks? What might this attack method mean for CAN Intrusion Detection and Intrusion Prevention systems? Come see the CANT tool perform this attack and hear discussion of how to defend against these attacks.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of automotive networking and CAN bus would be helpful, but not required.

snippet.title: Hey Google, Activate Spyware! When Google Assistant Uses a Vulnerability as a Feature
snippet.description:
Erez Yalon, Director of Security Research, Checkmarx

This talk will highlight serious security findings in Android smartphones, enabling attackers to remotely control, take, and retrieve photos, videos, and geolocation from victims’ phones without the victim knowing, even if the phone is locked or the screen is turned off. Join us to see how one team chained several weaknesses and features to create a fully weaponized rogue spy-application.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of application security, vulnerability exploitation and remediation

snippet.title: Industry Standards to Support Supply Chain Risk Management for Firmware
snippet.description:
Lawrence Reinert, Computer Systems Researcher, National Security Agency
Monty Wiseman, Principal Engineer, Cybersecurity, GE Research

Supply chain risk management requirements include determining trust of the platform’s boot firmware. TPM-enabled platforms record the firmware provide it to verifiers. Verifiers compare these measurements against a set of expected values from the platform supplier. The speakers will present the industry standards for both measurements and expected “golden” values verifiers use to make trust decisions.Pre-Requisites: General knowledge of keys and certificates and TPM.
