snippet.title: Same Thing We Do Every Few Minutes, Pinky – Try to Take Over All Your Subdomains!
snippet.description:
Alun Jones, application security engineer, Starbucks Coffee Company

A year ago, if you searched the web for subdomain takeover, you’d find pages relating to Starbucks rewarding bounties on that issue. Come and listen to the steps Starbucks has taken to reduce the occurrence of new pages citing the company as examples of subdomain takeover vulnerability, including education, detection, prevention, engagement and hardening.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of DNS and Cloud/Web applications.

snippet.title: Revisiting Public-Private Collaboration: Asian and Global Perspectives
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Dr. Allan Friedman, Director of Cybersecurity, NTIA / US Department of Commerce

Panelists:
Dr. Chaichana Mitrpant, Deputy Executive Director, Electronic Transactions Development Agency
Dr. Kondo Reiko, Director, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
John Yong, Director, Cyber Security Group, InfoComm Development Authority (IDA), Singapore Government

Public-private partnerships and policies can differ globally, and continue to evolve. While not new in the US and EU, Asian governments are still exploring potential models of collaboration. Government officials will share progress towards working with industry in several Asian countries, identify what works and what doesn’t, and offer insight on how industry stakeholders around the world can engage.Pre-Requisites: Familiarity with some of the basic forms of public-private partnerships.

snippet.title: The Ghost in the Machine: Reconciling AI and Trust in the Connected World
snippet.description:
Sam Curry, Chief Security Officer, Cybereason
Dr. Alon Kaufman, Co-Founder and CEO, Duality Technologies

The adoption of advanced data technologies is one of the defining characteristics of the connected world. From ML to AI, we are getting a smarter, more personal world. The dystopic view is that not only Big Brother but many parties can monitor, control and manipulate us. What are the implications for trust? The need for privacy enforcing technologies is now, not after the ghost is in the machine.

snippet.title: RSAC Security Scholar Poster Pitch-Off
snippet.description:
Theresa Payton, CEO and President, Fortalice Solutions LLC
General (Ret.) Keith Alexander, Founder and Co-CEO, IronNet
Ann Johnson, Corporate Vice President, Cybersecurity Solutions Group, Microsoft Corp.
Ben Jun, CEO, HVF Labs

Learn about the cutting-edge research coming out of top universities as three selected RSA Conference Security Scholars pitch to government, research and cybersecurity veterans. Then listen in as these respected experts provide feedback and insights to the scholars on how to make their topics more relevant to different perspectives and industries.

snippet.title: Secure Software Development Framework: An Industry and Public Sector Approach
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Adam Sedgewick, Senior IT Policy Advisor, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

Panelists:
Donna Dodson, Chief Cybersecurity Advisor, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
Steven Lipner, Executive Director, SAFECode
Tommy Ross, Senior Director, Policy, BSA | The Software Alliance

NIST, SAFECode and BSA will discuss a new NIST document that presents a framework of practices aimed at helping regulated industries mitigate the risk of software vulnerabilities. The document is based on industry secure software development practices and targets software producers and consumers. International and industry sector-specific policies, regulations and mandates are highlighted.

snippet.title: Air Gap Hopping with Musical Fans: Proving a False Sense of Security
snippet.description:
Aaron Rosenmund, Author, Evangelist and Researcher: Incident Response, Pluralsight

Proof of concept demonstration of exfiltrating data across air-gapped systems using fan speeds and how this chain of compromise could be interrupted with the correct monitoring and alerting. Leveraging this example, the session will examine various other side-channel attacks that threaten networks wherever they live including supply chain interdiction, spinning hard drive attacks and more.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of general defense-in-depth methodologies including continuous monitoring and air-gapped networks.

snippet.title: Forget the Kids! Did Alexa Just Use Your Credit Card?!
snippet.description:
Daniel Cohen, Director, Anti-Fraud Strategy & Products, RSA Security
Gregory Dicovitsky, Field CTO, RSA Fraud and Risk Intelligence, RSA

As open banking gains traction driven by consumer demand and regulation, the likes of PSD2, FinTechs and traditional banks are developing new ways for end users—and their devices—to gain automated access to payment information. Fraudsters are going to have a field day! This session will provide anti-fraud practitioners strategies they can deploy today to prevent tomorrow’s financial consumer fraud!
Pre-Requisites: Knowledge of the financial consumer fraud space,
anti-fraud tools, practices and policies.

snippet.title: Peel Back the Layers of Your Enterprise and Make Your Adversaries Cry
snippet.description:
Doug Burks, CEO, Security Onion Solutions, LLC

Security Onion is a free and open source platform that contains best of breed open source components for enterprise visibility. It was created by defenders for defenders who may not otherwise have the resources for comprehensive visibility. If we can give defenders better visibility, then they can detect their adversaries more quickly and interrupt them before they achieve their objectives!
Pre-Requisites: General understanding of Intrusion Detection, Network Security Monitoring, Log Management, Incident Response.

snippet.title: Privacy by Design Lessons from Beyoncé
snippet.description:
Ayana Miller, Technical Program Manager, Privacy and Data Governance, Pinterest

As we approach the second anniversary of GDPR, it’s a great time to reflect on the state of privacy by design and what’s in store for the future of privacy. We’ve seen an increase in privacy engineering commitments from large tech companies, an outpouring of vendors promising privacy compliance solutions and more policies like the California Consumer Privacy Act. What would Beyoncé do?Pre-Requisites: General understanding of privacy regulations including the European General Data Protection Regulation, California Consumer Privacy Act, and US Privacy Shield. Understanding of basic privacy engineering best practices and approaches.

snippet.title: Creepy Leaky Browsers
snippet.description:
Daniel Ayoub, Director Product Management, ThreatMetrix - Lexis Nexis Risk Solutions
Dean Weinert, VP Product Management, ThreatMetrix - Lexis Nexis Risk Solutions

Are you concerned about privacy on the Internet? If so, your browser may be leaking a creepy amount of data that can be used to identify you. This session will explore some of the most popular web browsers available today and compare/contrast the amount of data that is leaked.Pre-Requisites: No programming experience is required. General understanding of how modern web browsers operate, what javaskript is (how it works), and the privacy implications of revealing  too much data should be sufficient.

snippet.title: Top 10 List for Securing Your IT/OT Environment
snippet.description:
Dawn Cappelli, VP Global Security and Chief Information Security Officer, Rockwell Automation
Roy Gundy, Head of OT Cyber Security, Johnson & Johnson

US-CERT’s most recent statistics show manufacturing as the most targeted sector, accounting for 22 percent of all cyberattacks. ICS attacks use multiple vectors: compromise IT and move into OT, compromise OT directly, insider threats and supply chain. A holistic security strategy for converged IT and OT is imperative. Use this Top 10 list from leading CISOs to benchmark your IT/OT security strategy.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of operational technology as well as the high level concepts covered in the NIST CSF.

snippet.title: Case Files from 20 Years of Business Logic Flaws
snippet.description:
Chetan Conikee, Chief Technology Officer, ShiftLeft, Inc.

What do Citibank, First American Financial, McDonald’s, Nordstrom and Signet/Jared Jewelers have in common? Each company suffered from a type of vulnerability that eluded code analysis tools: business logic flaws. Chetan Conikee will present “case files” of each company along with a full set of taxonomies of business logic flaws coupled with scenarios and exploitative patterns.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of and experience in application security and DevOps.

snippet.title: You, Me and FIPS 140-3: A Guide to the New Standard and Transition
snippet.description:
Ryan Thomas, CST Laboratory Manager, Acumen Security

On March 22nd, 2019, FIPS 140-3 was officially signed. After years of waiting, the new standard based on ISO/IEC 19790 and ISO/IEC 24759 will succeed FIPS 140-2. Find out what’s new in FIPS 140-3. What are the key differences between FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3? Learn about the planned transition timeline and what will happen to current FIPS 140-2 certificates.
Pre-Requisites: Understanding of cryptographic techniques, symmetric and asymmetric encryption, hashing, digital signatures, random number generation, authentication.

snippet.title: NPK: High-Powered, Open Source Hash Cracking Tool
snippet.description:
Brad Woodward, Director, Coalfire Labs, Coalfire

The cloud is highly enabling—yet, organizations should understand their degree of risk from weak passwords. NPK, a new open source tool, finally enables high-powered hash cracking without the high price tag. This mostly serverless, distributed hashing platform leverages the exceptionally powerful GPU instances in AWS, providing user control on instance/price limitations for optimal results.

snippet.title: Hacking the Unhackable: Pwning the Bitfi Crypto Wallet
snippet.description:
Ken Munro, Partner, Pen Test Partners

Don’t call your device unhackable. Don’t choose the wrong hardware to build your devices on. Don’t ignore secure coding standards. Don’t trash your brand by being publicly combative with security researchers. Don’t rubbish claims when presented with irrefutable advice. Don’t snort bath salts.

snippet.title: Scaling IAM Rules with ML-Based Risk Analytics? You Don’t Need to Be a Ninja
snippet.description:
Sudarsan Kannan, Consultant, RSA
Alex Zaslavsky, Senior Principal Data Scientist, RSA

Are you in the process of developing or deploying an ML-based risk analytics engine to prevent identity theft and abuse? Want to better understand what specific ML models do for such use-cases, associated benefits and challenges? Come learn how to define and approach technical and operational requirements based on lessons learned through enterprise experience.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of IAM specific technical controls, identity specific attacks and risk analytics.

snippet.title: “Cramming for FISMA”: How to Launch a NIST 800-53 Moderate System in 180 Days
snippet.description:
Johannes Wiklund, VP of IT and Cyber Security, Somos

What do you do when a federal agency asks your company to build a new system in 180 days and throws in “FISMA compliance” as a requirement? Based on real-world experience from the trenches, this session will cover potential pitfalls in deploying a system that must meet the NIST 800-53 security controls, and give actionable advice on how to overcome challenges and be ready for a FISMA Assessment.
Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of of AWS service architecture and compliance frameworks and a high-level knowledge of system architecture and operations.

snippet.title: Putting Access Management for the Internet of Things into Practice with MUD
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Eliot Lear, Principal Engineer, Cisco - Enterprise Chief Technology Office

Panelists:
L. Jean Camp, Professor, Indiana University
Drew Cohen, Chief Executive Officer, MasterPeace Solutions Ltd
Mudumbai Ranganathan, Computer Engineer, National Institute of Standards and Technology
Darshak Thakore, Principal Architect, CableLabs

The panel will summarize public and private sector activities for documenting and applying best security practices for IoT. It will describe industry collaborations, including describing and showing proof of concept implementations of the Manufacturer Usage Description (MUD) Specification (RFC 8520) for controlling access to IoT devices. Lessons learned and implementation issues will be explored.Pre-Requisites: Awareness of internet protocols and access management in networks. This session will participate in polling. To participate please be sure to download the RSA Conference app prior to the session.

snippet.title: At What Point Does DevSecOps Become Too Risky for the Business?
snippet.description:
Altaz Valani, Research Director, Security Compass
Hasan Yasar, Technical Director, SSD Division at Software Engineering Institute, Carnegie Mellon University

This session will cover the implementation of an automated, continuous risk pipeline that demonstrates how cyber-resiliency and compliance risk can be traced to and from DevSecOps teams working in the SDLC program and project levels. It will include integration of asset management, DevSecOps tooling, policy-to-procedure platform and risk management platform.
Pre-Requisites: Working knowledge of Risk and Compliance Management. This session will participate in polling. To participate please be sure to download the RSA Conference app prior to the session.

snippet.title: Going Cyber-Nuclear: Is It Time for a Big Red Button?
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Stanley Lowe, Global Chief Information Security Officer, Zscaler, Inc.

Panelists:
Tony Cole, CTO, Attivo Networks
Michael Daniel, President and CEO, Cyber Threat Alliance
Anne Marie Zettlemoyer, Vice President of Security Engineering and Business Security Office, Mastercard

It wouldn’t be an actual button (although that would be cool). But the impact would be near-instant: The United States of America’s Internet would be cleaved off from the rest of the world, isolating US network traffic from outside bad actors. Yes, it’s extreme. And it may not even be possible. Its time to start a blunt, serious conversation.Pre-Requisites: Curiosity about how the intersection of cyber security, internet and economics is critical to our national & economic interests.

snippet.title: What Was Once Old Is New Again: Domain Squatting in 2020
snippet.description:
Jeremy du Bruyn, Practice Manager, Sense of Security
Willem Mouton, Head of Research, Sense of Security

In this session the presenters will demonstrate how old school domain squatting can be modernized to include OSINT gathering and the delivery of weaponized documents using email messages. The result is scarily accurate corporate relationship and supply chain mappings, as well as re-purposing actual business documents into spear-phishing attacks.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of email protocols such as SMTP and DNS, spear-phishing and supply-chain attacks.

snippet.title: Dude, You’re Getting a Dell: Organizational Culture Shift to SDL Maturity
snippet.description:
Mohit Arora, Software Security Architect, Dell
Richard Tonry, Firmware Security Architect, Dell

Dell is an organization of 157,000 employees that ships millions of PCs, devices and software products every year. An organization of this size presents challenges in getting people to shift their security mindset. This talk will discuss the challenges, changes and lessons learned on the journey towards a security-focused culture within Dell’s PC business unit and alignment with the rest of the company.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of security processes, SDL and vulnerability response.

snippet.title: Save Your (Cyber) Bacon: Personal Liability for CISOs and Infosec Pros
snippet.description:
Aravind Swaminathan, Global Co-Chair, Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe’s Cyber
Mark Weatherford, Global Information Security Strategist, Booking Holdings

Information security professionals have increasingly come under intense scrutiny, facing criminal and civil legal proceedings and becoming the targets of regulators, plaintiffs, the media and even their own companies. Join this session to learn about the personal liability risks to CISOs and CIOs and how to protect yourself, both prior to an incident and during response activities.

snippet.title: Dynamic Defense: Security Operations Transformation
snippet.description:
Garrettson Blight, Director of DarkLabs, Booz Allen Hamilton
Adam Langford, Senior Associate, Booz Allen Hamilton

With the proliferation of new technologies, adversarial sophistication and an increase in publicly announced breaches, SecOps organizations must transform. The dynamic defense model modernizes SecOps by utilizing a proactive, intelligence-driven and continuous loop approach containing five key sub-functions: incorporate data sources, collaboration, orchestration, AI and KPI.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of security operation center principles.

snippet.title: Extracting Secrets from Locked Password Managers
snippet.description:
Adrian Bednarek, Senior Security Analyst, Independent Security Evaluators

Are your secret entries kept safe by your password manager? Even when you log out of it and place it in a locked state? This session will dive into what happens to your master password and the secrets it guards when you unlock a password manager and more importantly what happens when you log out or lock it. Password Managers covered: 1Password, Dashlane, KeePass, LastPass.

snippet.title: Insights from Kara Swisher
snippet.description:
Kara Swisher, Co-Founder and Editor-at-Large, Recode

Don’t miss this keynote session where Kara Swisher will address the role of social media in our current political landscape, with a focus on greater accountability in the tech industry.

snippet.title: RSAC Launch Pad - Soluble
snippet.description:
Richard Seiersen, Founder and CEO, Soluble
Theresia Gouw, Founding Partner, aCrew Capital
Enrique Salem, Bain Capital
Ted Schlein, Partner, Kleiner Perkins

RSAC Launch Pad offers three selected early-stage startups a chance to pitch leading security venture capitalists Theresia Gouw, Enrique Salem and Ted Schlein to gain advice, interest and maybe…investment.

snippet.title: Rives: Buttons Now
snippet.description: John Rives opens the Wednesday morning keynote session at RSA Conference 2020 in San Francisco with his spoken word, "Buttons Now".

snippet.title: Find Your Voice and Your Confidence
snippet.description:
Lynn Terwoerds, Executive Director, Executive Women’s Forum

You have expertise and a reputation – learn how to submit a winning abstract and deliver a compelling talk. The session includes a hands-on exercise to jump start your next speaking engagement.

snippet.title: Why Your People Are Still Your Best Cyber-Defense
snippet.description:
Ann Johnson, Corporate Vice President, Cybersecurity Solutions Group, Microsoft Corp.

As organizations digitally transform, access to artificial intelligence and machine learning powered by the cloud will mean the difference between struggle or success for organizations, as bad actors look to AI to do their dirty work. While cybersecurity and operational resilience should be complementary disciplines, the one thing many organizations who recover quickly from a cyberattack possess is also the one thing many attackers don’t take into account. The human spirit. Ann Johnson, CVP Cybersecurity Solutions Group, Microsoft, will share how to create a culture where people are your best defense.

snippet.title: How to Reduce Supply Chain Risk: Lessons from Efforts to Block Huawei
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Craig Spiezle, Founder, Agelight Advisory and Research Group

Panelists:
Katie Arrington, Cyber Information Security Officer of Acquisitions, US Dept of Defense / OUSD for Acquisitions
Donald (Andy) Purdy, Chief Security Officer, Huawei Technologies USA
Bruce Schneier, Security Technologist, Researcher and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School
Kathryn Waldron, Fellow, R Street Institute

There has been intense scrutiny on Huawei, ranging from their software development processes to allegations of backdoors. While it may be debated if Huawei is a pawn in a trade war or a national security risks, it reinforces the importance of knowing one’s ecosystem. This session will use Huawei as a case study for best practices to assess risk and provide transparency to all stakeholders.

snippet.title: Navigating Privacy in a Data-Driven World: Treating Privacy as a Human Right
snippet.description:
Jules Polonetsky, Chief Executive Officer, Future of Privacy Forum

Privacy risks are in the news and regulators are advancing new regulations and moratoriums on certain technologies. Browsers and mobile OS are adding consumer controls, blocking cookies and setting new rules on tracking. Companies see new uses of data as the key to new services. How can brands change the narrative to support trusted uses of personal data? Which technologies will create the greatest risks in the next 10 years and which will advance data protection?

snippet.description:
Hugh Thompson, RSA Conference, Program Committee Chair
Theresia Gouw, Founding Partner, aCrew Capital
Enrique Salem, Bain Capital
Ted Schlein, Partner, Kleiner Perkins

RSAC Launch Pad offers three selected early-stage startups a chance to pitch leading security venture capitalists Theresia Gouw, Enrique Salem and Ted Schlein to gain advice, interest and maybe…investment.

snippet.description:

Theresia Gouw, Founding Partner, aCrew Capital
Enrique Salem, Bain Capital
Ted Schlein, Partner, Kleiner Perkins

RSAC Launch Pad offers three selected early-stage startups a chance to pitch leading security venture capitalists Theresia Gouw, Enrique Salem and Ted Schlein to gain advice, interest and maybe…investment.

snippet.description: John Rives opens the Wednesday afternoon keynote session at RSA Conference 2020 in San Francisco with his spoken word, "2020 Twenty Questions".

snippet.title: RSAC Launch Pad - Welcome & Introduction
snippet.description:
Hugh Thompson, RSA Conference, Program Committee Chair
Theresia Gouw, Founding Partner, aCrew Capital
Enrique Salem, Bain Capital
Ted Schlein, Partner, Kleiner Perkins

RSAC Launch Pad offers three selected early-stage startups a chance to pitch leading security venture capitalists Theresia Gouw, Enrique Salem and Ted Schlein to gain advice, interest and maybe…investment.

snippet.title: ICS Village: RSAC Talk with Chris Krebs
snippet.description:
Bryson Bort, Founder & CEO, SCYTHE
Chris Krebs, Director, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency

The Director of CISA and Co-Founder of the ICS Village will discuss the vision for community engagement, training and partnership to provide interactive simulated control systems environments.

snippet.title: Kr00k: How KRACKing Amazon Echo Exposed a Billion+ Vulnerable WiFi Devices
snippet.description:
Robert Lipovsky, Senior Malware Researcher, ESET
Stefan Svorencik, ESET, Senior Detection Engineer

Initially discovering that some Amazon Echoes and Kindles were vulnerable to attacks against WPA2 (KRACK), ESET then found that a related attack, which could enable adversaries to decrypt wireless network packets, affects WiFi chipsets used in over a billion devices including some by Apple, Google, and Samsung. 

Pre-Requisites: A basic understanding of WPA2 (including the four-way handshake) is beneficial.

snippet.title: Next-Gen IoT Botnets 3: Bad Implementations of Good Cloud Platforms
snippet.description:
Alex Jay Balan, Chief Security Researcher, Bitdefender

With most IoTs moving towards cloud platforms, it seemed appropriate to look at their implementations. And boy did the team hit “insecurity gold”! Authentication bypasses, device tampering and RCE. And the beauty of it is that it’s no longer needed to iterate the IP space and find open ports since one bad cloud implementation allows attackers to interact with all devices from the vendor.Pre-Requisites: Strong networking skills and understanding of tampering with APIs, MQTT, AWS S3. While not mandatory, it would help if  the audience had some knowledge of buffer overflows, ROP and command injection for the RCE demos.

snippet.title: What’s in the Box? Software Bill of Materials for IoT
snippet.description:
Dr. Allan Friedman, Director of Cybersecurity, NTIA / US Department of Commerce

Devices are opaque—how do we trust them? In addition to security standards, transparency of SW components can be a key driver of trust and quality. This talk will share details on industry consensus around “software bill of materials” and present an initial playbook and tools for IoT vendors to share their third-party dependencies, and how enterprise customers can use this to make risk decisions.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of SW development for IoT. NB: can still be understood by policy / business folks to understand the existence/importance of SBOM, template contract language, etc.

snippet.title: Why Is Securing Elections the Hardest Problem in IT Security?
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Mary Hanley, Associate Director, University of Chicago Harris Cyber Policy Initiative

Panelists:
Harri Hursti, Founding Partner, Nordic Innovation Labs
Philip Stark, Professor and Associate Dean, University of California, Berkeley
Dan Webber, Managing Partner, Nordic Innovation Labs

As the 2020 election looms, the US election system faces innumerable threats both foreign and domestic, yet lags behind on even basic industry standards for cybersecurity. This talk will go beyond the voting machines in exploring the unique security challenges faced in elections both in the US and abroad.

snippet.title: ICS OSINT: An Attacker’s Perspective
snippet.description:
Amy Bejtlich, Director of Intelligence Analysis, Dragos, Inc.
Selena Larson, Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst, Dragos

Destructive ICS attacks generally require specialized skill and resources, but initial reconnaissance to plan an attack requires little advanced capabilities. Learn how defenders can decrease their attack surface and increase adversary friction by developing an awareness of ICS-specific open source intelligence (OSINT) techniques and the type of freely available data adversaries use in attacks.

snippet.title: Evaluation Criteria and Tactics Amidst an Expanding Landscape of Solutions
snippet.description:
Dara Such, VP and Publisher, Security Networking and IoT, TechTarget

Between new threats, resource constraints and ever-expanding vendor landscape, services and frameworks, security professionals have their work cut out for them. Learn from industry veterans and more than 2,000 security projects globally what their key selection criteria was for recent purchases, how they approach evaluating security tools and what essentials steps made the process easier.

snippet.title: Losing Our Reality: How Deepfakes Threaten Businesses and Global Markets
snippet.description:
Alyssa Miller, Application Security Advocate, Snyk, Ltd.

As a result of continuing advancements in AI, deepfake media has become increasingly convincing and easy to produce. Experts have warned of the impact this could have on elections and personal security. However, the threats that deepfakes pose to businesses and global markets are often overlooked. This session will analyze those threats and present defense strategies business must consider.Pre-Requisites: Knowledge of market factors and influences would be helpful but not required.

snippet.title: Product Security Meets Human Life: Inoculating Medical Devices
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Adam Brand, Managing Director, PwC

Panelists:
Sara Bohan, Senior Information Security Analyst, Mayo Clinic
Tara Larson, Chief Security Architect – Product Security Director, Abbott
Scott Nichols, Director, Global Product Privacy and Cybersecurity, Danaher/Beckman-Coulter

How do you secure a product when insecurity can mean death or injury? How do you do this for low-processing-ability devices on a potentially hostile network that may be used for a decade? In this technically focused panel conversation, product security leaders from leading device manufacturers and a leading health system discuss the latest challenges and approaches to inoculating critical devices.Pre-Requisites: Knowledge of product security concepts such as secure design, SOUP, and coordinated disclosure will be helpful to following the panel discussion.

snippet.title: SCADA/ICS Inherited Insecurity: From Nuclear Power Plants to Oil Rigs
snippet.description:
Aleksander Gorkowienko, Managing Consultant, Spirent

Attacking SCADA/ICS could leave a country without electricity, lead to huge financial losses and, what’s worst, could cost lives. The speaker will discuss his research on SCADA/ICS security and show examples of vulnerabilities from previously conducted penetration tests. The talk will include a review of practical exploitation techniques and a live demonstration of simulated attacks on the power grid.Pre-Requisites: General knowledge of hacking and IT security, knowledge of TCP/IP, industrial protocols. At least basic programming knowledge (C, Python) will be a plus.

snippet.title: Enhancing Aviation Cybersecurity Capacity or How I Learned to Love a Hacker
snippet.description:
Steve Luczynski, CISO, T-Rex Solutions, LLC

Loss of the flying public’s trust in reliable, safe and trustworthy air travel could impact national security. While the US government and the aviation industry are working hard, individually and cooperatively, an untapped resource remains. By dispelling hacker myths, trust among these communities can increase their collective ability to contribute more effectively to bolstering safe air travel.

snippet.title: Practical Use of the MUD Specification to Support Access Control in the IoT
snippet.description:
Dr. Parisa Grayeli, Manager, NCCoE MUD Laboratory, Mitre/NCCoE
Blaine Mulugeta, Cyber Security Engineer, Mitre/NCCoE

The presentation will demonstrate how the National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence’s proof of concept implementations of the Manufacturer Usage Description (MUD) Specification (RFC 8520) can be used in controlling access to IoT devices. Lessons learned and implementation issues will be explored.Pre-Requisites: Elementary understanding of networking.

snippet.title: Cyber-Litigation 2020: Recent Cases in the Courts and Agencies
snippet.description:
Professor Richard Aldrich, Cybersecurity Policy and Compliance Analyst, Booz, Allen, Hamilton/DOD OSD
Julia Bowen, Senior Vice President and General Counsel, The MITRE Corp.

Attendees will be briefed on a number of the most recent and impactful Supreme Court and Federal Circuit court decisions and supporting fact patterns, along with pending agency decisions likely to result in litigation. Cases from areas including cyber-insurance, cyber-conflict, encryption controls for national security purposes and tech-based border searches will fill this year’s docket.Pre-Requisites: No formal legal training or experience required, but maximum benefit will be derived by attendees who understand both the facts leading to the disputes and the legal concepts being discussed. General familiarity with concepts such as ""contract"" ""agreement"" ""warranty"" ""and the substantive issue in each case, such as encryption tools will make participation more meaningful.

snippet.title: Implications of the Global Push to Ban End-to-End Encryption
snippet.description:
Dr. Andrea Little Limbago, Chief Social Scientist, Virtru
Professor Lesley Seebeck, Professor, Australian National University, Cyber Institute

The majority of the world’s population currently live under governments that have already implemented, or are considering, bans on encryption. These encryption bans have significant implications for privacy and security as well as the global decline in democracy. Presenters will discuss current and impending policies that weaken encryption, and contrast them with the nascent privacy-preserving movement.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of encryption and its role in data protection. Minimal background in global affairs and cybersecurity trends.

snippet.title: Nudging through Numbers
snippet.description:
Sahil Bansal, AVP, Information Security, Genpact

With the increasing threat landscape, security training cannot be a one-size-fits-all. Based on existing data points, Genpact categorized users based on the risk they pose. Genpact defined acceptable behaviors and as the risk increased, the threshold for this behavior went higher. Users can now look up their individual scores, see what is contributing to it and are nudged to improve it.Pre-Requisites: An experience/interest in running security awareness and training initiatives.

snippet.title: A Sherlock Holmes Mystery: AI-Powered Behavioral Forensics
snippet.description:
Erin Englund, Sr. Threat Analyst, BioCatch
Uri Rivner, Chief Cyber Officer, BioCatch

Sherlock Holmes would have been proud: advances in AI enable the profiling of hackers based on the specific behavioral and cognitive DNA traces left by the attacker at the crime scene. This series of case studies will build a strong forensic case against individual hackers and see how seemingly unconnected hacks are all done by the same mysterious criminal.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of fraud fighting principals such as detection vs. FP and alert rate, digital signals (device, location, behavior), link analysis, common attack methods such as Account Takeover, RAT, Bot, Social Engineering.

snippet.title: All That Glitters? Debunking Fool’s Marketing of ML and AI
snippet.description:
Diana Kelley, Cybersecurity Field CTO, Microsoft
Dr. Char Sample, Cybersecurity Research Fellow, Idaho National Laboratory

Tired of the glittery hype about how AI and ML will solve for cyber? Confused about general vs. narrow AI? Supervised vs. unsupervised ML? Reinforcement learning? Wonder who’s accountable if a model fails? Worried sentient bots are going to take over the planet? A scientist and a technologist debunk the myths around ML and AI.Pre-Requisites: A desire to debunk!

snippet.title: No CISSP, No Problem: Growing the Cyber-Talent Pool
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Lisa Monaco, Partner / Co-Chair, O'Melveny & Myers / Aspen Cyber Security Group

Panelists:
Marene Allison, Chief Information Security Officer, Johnson & Johnson
Barbara Massa, Executive Vice President & Chief of Business Operations, FireEye
Nick Peach, Senior Vice President, Bank of America

Despite the persistent skills gap in cybersecurity, the talent is there if companies look in the right place. Along with leading employers across multiple sectors, the Aspen Cybersecurity Group is working to scale the adoption of practices that broaden the cyber-recruitment pool. In this session, attendees will hear how major companies are reimagining where we find cybersecurity talent.

snippet.title: The Past Is Not the Future: Practical Ethics for Algorithms
snippet.description:
Behnam Dayanim, Partner, Global Chair of Privacy & Cybersecurity Practice, Paul Hastings LLP
Mike Kiser, Global Security Advocate, Office of the CTO, SailPoint

Who was the real Tara Simmons? A court was forced to decide whether she was a convicted felon (her past) or a respected lawyer (her future). Algorithms that use the past to predict the future are common but can cause great harm. Via the story of Simmons and others like her, presenters will develop a practical ethical standard (with currently available tools) for evaluating and comparing algorithms.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of Python and machine learning would be helpful; content would apply to anyone with a basic association with artificial intelligence.

snippet.title: Enemies at the Gate: Protecting American Democracy in 2020
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Theresa Payton, CEO and President, Fortalice Solutions LLC

Panelists:
Geoff Hale, Senior Cybersecurity Advisor, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
Jennifer Morrell, Former Election Official and Partner, Elections Group
Trevor Timmons, Chief Information Officer, Secretary of State’s Office, Colorado

DHS cyber-experts and election infrastructure partners will outline their work in advance of the 2020 presidential election against threats, including foreign interference, in order to build a more resilient election infrastructure. The panel will highlight efforts to assess risk and improve coordination with partners while spotlighting tools available to increase election security and resiliency.

snippet.title: Monokle: Mobile Surveillanceware with a Russian Connection
snippet.description:
Adam Bauer, Senior Staff Security Intelligence Engineer, Lookout
Apurva Kumar, Staff Security Intelligence Engineer, Lookout

This session will provide a close look at the highly targeted Monokle surveillanceware, how it is most likely deployed by nation-states and how it was attributed to a Russian government contractor. The audience will learn about the latest trends in the development of sophisticated mobile surveillanceware.Pre-Requisites: A basic background on Android and some of its features -- including permissions, how to install and uninstall apps, default Android services such as Accessibility services etc.
An understanding of domains and IP addresses and what those mean in the context of an application sending or receiving data from an internet connection.
Although most terminology will be explained, security terms such as command and control infrastructure may be shortened to ""C2"" or ""C and C"" later in the talk.

snippet.title: API Security Exposure for Gift Card Fraud: A 15-Year-Old’s Guide
snippet.description:
Tanay Deshmukh, Self, High School Student

Adoption of APIs is increasing significantly. Mobile apps and web applications use API to transmit a lot of sensitive information. Many retailers and online platforms that provide subscription-based services use API to allow users to login or check balances on their gift cards. Sophisticated attacks can expose details of gift cards and gift card balances that could be used maliciously.Pre-Requisites: General knowledge of javaskript and fidler.

snippet.title: Demystifying 5G Security through Threat Modeling
snippet.description:
Zhijun Zhang, Lead Security Architect, The World Bank Group

5G promises to bring much faster data rate and many new services. At the same time it has created a lot of concerns around security risks. This talk will walk  through the new technology components in a 5G network and the new services it provides, to comprehensively analyze the risks in this ecosystem through a threat model the World Bank Group developed and to discuss the mitigating controls.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of Threat models such as STRIDE.

snippet.title: Proactive Container Security for the Masses
snippet.description:
Ross Turk, Vice President, Anchore

Linux Containers help DevOps teams hide complexity and reuse work more efficiently. But they can also allow vulnerabilities to spread if images are not created and managed responsibly. In this talk, Ross Turk from Anchore will discuss how open source tools and best practices can help you and your team build secure container workflows.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of basic software development lifecycle (SDLC) concepts and Linux containers.

snippet.title: Tackling Cyber-Enabled Crime at Scale: Moving Enforcement Forward
snippet.description:
Nick Selby, Chief Security Officer, Paxos Trust Company

In 2019, the New York Police Department piloted a strategy led by Nick Selby to address cyber-enabled crimes department-wide. This talk will discuss why this is hard: the challenges of getting the right metrics, training and supporting officers, understanding the demography, and overcoming ad hoc approaches to respond at scale, and some of the NYPD’s surprising findings about victimology.

snippet.title: OpenSSL and FIPS... They Are Back Together!
snippet.description:
Matthew Caswell, Developer, OpenSSL Software Foundation
Ashit Vora, Vice President, Acumen Security

OpenSSL is being FIPS 140-2 validated after a hiatus of seven years. This validation of great importance to the industry since it supports both TLS v1.3 and FIPS in the same release of OpenSSL for the first time. This presentation will cover the architectural changes made to OpenSSL to accommodate the FIPS validation, the scope of the validation, current status and next steps post-validation.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of OpenSSL architecture, FIPS 140-2 requirements and Cryptography.

snippet.title: Nanotechnology, Behavior and Supply Chains: Managing Risk at a Platform Level
snippet.description:
Edna Conway, VP, Global Security, Risk & Compliance, Microsoft Azure
Ophir Gaathon, PhD, CEO/Co-Founder, DUST Identity

The platform revolution triggered a tectonic shift in global supply chains. The proliferation of service platforms has raised a new specter of unaccounted risk: the third-party risk. Exactly who and what are in the value chains of our XAAService providers? The answer is often opaque. This co-presentation will explore how we can close the trust gaps across our expanding third-party network.Pre-Requisites: Background in supply chain and global value chains.

snippet.title: The Impact of Software Security Practice Adoption Quantified
snippet.description:
Larry Maccherone, DevSecOps Transformation, Comcast

This talk will present research quantifying the impact that various software security practices have on security risk outcomes. Comcast has correlated practices like secure coding training, threat modeling, pen testing, SAST/IAST/SCA tool usage, security code review, etc.. with outcome data from 200 different teams in the technologically and process maturity diverse environment inside Comcast.

snippet.title: 'Phoning Home’ Impact on Enterprise Data, Security and Privacy
snippet.description:
Matt Cauthorn, VP of Cybersecurity Engineering, ExtraHop Networks
Jeff Costlow, CISO, ExtraHop

Enterprises seldom know all the ways that vendors send data to their own environments. This lack of awareness can have profound implications. This session will cover four real-world examples of vendors phoning home data without the customer’s authorization or knowledge, the security and regulatory implications of this activity, and the questions you should ask vendors about their data practices.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of the threat of data exfiltration.

snippet.title: A Mapping of GDPR to Common Features
snippet.description:
Matthew Clapham, Director of Cybersecurity, GE Healthcare

GDPR has set developers and companies atwitter with concerns about what it means to them. Lawyers may describe the obligations and penalties for noncompliance. What is needed are practical ways to translate the simple rights under GDPR into actionable feature ideas. A possible mapping of privacy rights to feature sets will help satisfy GDPR and other pending regulations around the globe.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of GDPR and privacy concepts
Knowledge of pending legislation in other regions/municipalities.

snippet.title: Disrupting BEC Attacks Utilizing Kill Chain
snippet.description:
Patrick Peterson, Founder and CEO, Agari
Teresa Walsh, Head, Financial Services Information Sharing and Analysis Center Inc. (FS-ISAC)

In this session, the presenters will share trends in business email compromise (BEC) and ways the financial service industry fights this $26B problem. Learn about (a) BEC criminal gangs tactics, techniques and procedures, (b) BEC intelligence gathering/disruption and (c) FS-ISAC ground breaking fraud ntelligence sharing.

snippet.title: Nanny State to Invisible Hand: What’s the Proper Role for Regulation?
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Gib Sorebo, Security Consulting Senior Manager, Accenture

Panelists:
Kathryn Coburn, Partner, Murphy Cooke Kobrick LLP
John Gregory, General Counsel, Retired, Government of Ontario, Canada
Lauren Topelsohn, Member, Mandelbaum Salsburg P.C.

Getting people to do the right thing is never easy, particularly when costs are high, and the benefits are often elusive. This session will explore the various ways governments have tried to regulate or otherwise incentivize better cybersecurity behaviors through fines, lawsuits and public shaming. Panelists will examine what has worked and what hasn’t and discuss how we can do better.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of risk management regulatory landscapes.

snippet.title: Next Steps for the Cyber-Moonshot
snippet.description:
Moderator:
John Carlin, Chair, Cyber & Technology Program, The Aspen Institute

Panelists:
John Davis, VP Public Sector, Palo Alto Networks
Tom Patterson, Vice President and Chief Trust Officer, Unisys
Bobbie Stempfley, Director, Software Engineering Institute, Carnegie Mellon University
Bradford Willke, Assistant Director, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee, and the Aspen Institute are planning several Cyber Grand Challenges related to cybersecurity economics, digital literacy, automation and digital identity. The session will detail final concepts for the grand challenge contests and offer opportunities for industry participation.

snippet.title: Pre-Crime Detection of Active Shooters Using Predictive Policing Systems
snippet.description:
Jeffrey Blatt, Founder, X Ventures

Active shooters intending to cause mass casualties exhibit warning behaviors that are usually not detected by law enforcement prior to an attack. Predictive policing technology utilizing “all source data collection” coupled with AI may be used to monitor social media, government and other data sets to identify a potential active shooter’s pre-crime behavior allowing for early intervention.

snippet.title: Artificial Intelligence Security and Privacy Legal Threats and Opportunity
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Stephen Wu, Shareholder, Silicon Valley Law Group

Panelists:
Kapil Raina, Chair, AI Security Alliance
Winn Schwartau, Founder, SAC
Lucy Thomson, Attorney, Livingston PLC

Artificial intelligence and robots will fundamentally change the world. But AI may fail, invade privacy, cause data breaches and trigger mass disasters. This panel will cover AI privacy and security legal threats and opportunities. Speakers will focus on the work of the AI Security Alliance bringing together companies and individuals in cyber and AI fields to preserve AI privacy and security.

snippet.title: Biometric Data: Power, Promise and Privacy Challenges
snippet.description:
Natalia Belaya, Head of Security Assurance and Compliance, Autodesk
Bret Cohen, Partner, Privacy and Cybersecurity Practice, Hogan Lovells
Alexandra Ross, Director, Global Privacy and Data Security Counsel, Autodesk

Biometric data is becoming more and more ubiquitous in our digital society. Think of the times you’ve used your thumbprint to open your iPhone or your retina scan at the airport customs line. In turn, privacy concerns have led to greater legal restrictions biometric data collection. This session will explore what are the privacy risks and practical approaches to implementing this technology?Pre-Requisites: General understanding of biometric data collection and use.

snippet.title: Humanizing Privacy with Power of User Experience (UX)
snippet.description:
Gary Patterson, Sr. Director, Informatica
Ranjeet Tayi, Senior Manager, User Experience Design, Informatica

Privacy is a fundamental human right and this needs understanding of data. Many companies fail to leverage industry-standard usability principles to make privacy regulations easy for their customers to understand and consume. Looking from both organization and consumer perspectives, this talk will showcase how UX can simplify integration of privacy/security compliance and scale for future regulations.Pre-Requisites: Basic knowledge on privacy and security and enterprise software.

snippet.title: When Cybercriminals with Good OpSec Attack
snippet.description:
Ryan MacFarlane, Supervisory Special Agent, FBI
Liam O'Murchu, Director, Symantec

Investigating career cybercriminals is hard, especially when their paranoia has fostered strong OpSec? The FBI and Symantec spent 10 years investigating such a gang eventually finding cracks just large enough to end the gangs crime spree. This case study will show how to investigate when strong OpSec exists.Pre-Requisites: General knowledge of cyber crimes investigations, minimal traffic analysis and malware analysis.

snippet.title: Incident Response Metrics: Turning Stats into Stories
snippet.description:
Mary Carp, Senior Cybersecurity Engineer, Avery Dennison
Jeremy Smith, Senior Manager of Information Security, Avery Dennison

It’s one thing to collect and chart the raw data from your incident response tools—it’s another to turn that data into a story, and yet another to pair that story with an ask. This session will explain how Fortune 500 manufacturing company Avery Dennison built a layered approach to IR metrics that partially automates the creation of narratives for reporting at all levels of the organization.Pre-Requisites: Experience with or interest in Incident Response processes and tools.

snippet.title: The Network Is Going Dark: Why Decryption Matters for SecOps
snippet.description:
Joshua Northrup, Manager of Monitoring and Automation, Fiserv
Jesse Rothstein, CTO, ExtraHop Networks

Like it or not, TLS 1.3 is coming and will make network traffic opaque to inspection. This session will cover lessons learned from Fiserv’s experience decrypting PFS-encrypted traffic and the various options available, including SSL fingerprinting, proxies and session-key forwarders installed on critical servers. Attendees will be able to formulate a strategy that works for their organization.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of network analysis and the implications of network traffic encryption for monitoring.

snippet.title: I Had My Mom Break into a Prison. Then, We Had Pie.
snippet.description:
John Strand, Owner, Black Hills Information Security

In this presentation John Strand will walk through how his late mother successfully broke into a prison. It will highlight how sometimes the greatest hackers don’t know much about computers. The session will also cover a number of other successful social engineering techniques attackers can use to gain access to some of the most secure places on the planet.

snippet.title: Syncopation in Enterprise IT: Uneven Migration to, and within, the Cloud
snippet.description:
Nick Selby, Chief Security Officer, Paxos Technology Solutions

Enterprise IT security vulnerabilities are being created at an accelerating pace. At first glance, this seems due to asymmetric migration paths, as companies go from lift-and-shift to cloud-native architectures. But generally speaking, the underlying causes of this are not technical. Instead, they are related to how humans view risk as they change how they get things done. This talk will discuss why.Pre-Requisites: CISOs, CIOs, enterprise risk managers, and cloud architects attending this talk should understand the basics of enterprise architecture and of the trend towards cloud migration, as well as Wardley mapping.

snippet.title: Serverless Attack Vectors
snippet.description:
Teri Radichel, CEO, 2nd Sight Lab

Serverless is all the rage in cloud computing. Large-scale applications are being deployed on serverless architectures. What does security look like in this brave new world? What types of attacks might an attacker carry out on in this environment? Come find out in this session that will focus on attacking and defending serverless infrastructure and applications.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of breaches and basic awareness of simple code concepts.

snippet.title: AI Security Engineering—Modeling/Detecting/Mitigating New Vulnerabilities
snippet.description:
Andrew Marshall, Principal Security Program Manager, Microsoft Corporation
Jugal Parikh, Senior Data Scientist, Microsoft
Raul Rojas, Security Assurance Architect, Microsoft Corporation

AI and machine learning present a litany of unmitigated security threats. Research is pivoting from contrived vulns to weaponized exploitation. As a security engineer, how do I protect and defend my services against these threats? As a data scientist how do I even detect them? As a first responder how do I triage? Join this session to go deep on these issues with new research and guidance.

snippet.title: Journey of a CISO
snippet.description:
Dr. Chenxi Wang, General Partner, Rain Capital
Nicole Darden Ford, CISO, Carrier 

Carrier's CISO Nicole Darden Ford sat down with Dr. Chenxi Wang to discuss her training in the US army, and her journey into the Cybersecurity industry. As the CISO for one of the most iconic brands in the US, Nicole's job is not only to protect the assets, brand, and resources for the company but also to lead the company into the next phase of the innovation journey. 

Recorded at RSA Conference 2020

snippet.title: Rethink the Way You Secure Your Organization with Intrinsic Security
snippet.description:
Sanjay Poonen, Chief Operating Officer, Customer Operations, VMware
Carrie Mills, Senior Manager, Cybersecurity, Southwest Airlines
Patrick Morley, SVP/GM, Security Business Unit, VMware

There has never been a more challenging nor exciting time in security. Sophistication of attackers, security threats, breaches and exploits are becoming more prevalent with no end in sight. With the adoption of cloud, new applications, mobile digital workspace, IoT, compute and data at the edge, the problem is only getting harder to solve. But this also represents an opportunity for a new approach. Join this session to hear how making security intrinsic can unlock new advantages and make life easier for security practitioners.

snippet.title: Treating CFIUS: Funding and Exiting When Feds Step In to “Enhance Security”
snippet.description:
Joshua Gruenspecht, Partner, Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati
Ken Mendelson, Senior Managing Director, Guidepost Solutions LLC

Foreign investment is both a source of capital and an exit strategy for tech startups. New legislation has expanded the US government’s authority to review, impose conditions on, and in some cases, block, such investments for security reasons. In this session you will learn about the government’s security concerns and the steps parties can take to mitigate such concerns and close the deal.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of M&A and government regulation. No specific prior knowledge of CFIUS or its processes are necessary.

snippet.title: Hacking Exposed: Global Threat Brief
snippet.description:
Dmitri Alperovitch, Co-Founder, CrowdStrike

In this session, the presenters will cover the most novel attacks in the current global threat landscape, diving into specific, real-time examples of threat actor activity from both nation-states and criminal groups. 
Pre-Requisites: Knowledge of basic attack techniques (preferably from past Hacking exposed presentations)

snippet.title: What You Don’t Know CAN Hurt You!
snippet.description:
Sherry Ryan, Vice President and CISO, Juniper Networks

Cybersecurity risk is a growing concern for organizations and has become a priority for boards. As breach costs increase, companies are taking a closer look at the role of security due diligence in M&A. Unlike other disciplines, the security due diligence process isn’t as well-defined but the stakes can be high, raising costs of the deal, decreasing its value and putting the transaction in jeopardy. Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of Information Security terminology and risk management practices.

snippet.title: Building a Comprehensive IoT Security Testing Methodology
snippet.description:
Deral Heiland, Research Lead, IoT, Rapid7

This presentation will focus on building an effective security testing methodologies for Internet of things (IoT) product ecosystems. IoT is multifaceted, requiring a well-defined and holistic approach in its testing. Learn why a structured and comprehensive testing program is needed in a discussion of the technical details, and challenges around the creation of an IoT testing program.Pre-Requisites: Understanding general security issues and vulnerabilities related to Mobile application, Cloud APIs and Web services, Network communication, Radio Frequency  communication and Electronic components and embedded firmware.

snippet.title: The Magic of Tracking Attack Campaigns Using Data Science
snippet.description:
Vicky Ray, Principal Researcher, Palo Alto Networks

The use of data science techniques is used in cybersecurity products and technologies but not commonly used by cyberthreat analysts or researchers when investigating attack campaigns. This talk will discuss the benefits of using data science when investigating attack campaigns and will cover data science algorithms that can be used to extract patterns and reduce analysis times significantlyPre-Requisites: Understanding of Threat Intelligence, Threat Analysis, and a 
basic understanding of data science concepts.

snippet.title: 8 Million Findings in One Year: Fresh Look at the State of Software Security
snippet.description:
Jay Jacobs, Co-founder and Chief Data Scientist, Cyentia Institute
Chris Wysopal, Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer, Veracode

What can we learn from 8.3 million software security findings? Plenty, and the presenters have the visuals to prove it. Analysis of millions of security flaws across tens of thousands of applications found that not all flaws (or applications) are created equal. This presentation will dive into the state of secure coding practices as observed from over 1 million application security scans.Pre-Requisites: General knowledge of Application Development and application vulnerabilities would be helpful, but not necessary.

snippet.title: Abaddon, the Red Team Angel
snippet.description:
Charles Ibrahim, Senior Information Security Consultant, Wavestone

Red team operations involve miscellaneous skills, last several months and are politically sensitive; they require a lot of monitoring, consolidating and caution.
Wavestone’s red team operations management software, Abaddon, has been designed to make red team operations faster, more repeatable, stealthier, while including value-added tools and bringing numerous reporting capabilities.Pre-Requisites: Global knowledge about modern pentesting techniques and an overall understanding of what red teaming is.

snippet.title: Privacy, Policymakers and the Tech Needed to Protect People
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Lydia de la Torre, Of Counsel, Squire Patton Boggs

Panelists:
Richard Arney, Co-Author, CCPA
Dimitri Sirota, CEO, BigID

The GDPR and CCPA are just the start. More states are following suit and companies are being slapped with massive fines in breach penalties. Compliance will require more than tech. It will require the will, the way, and unlikely partnerships with the people who engineered the policies and humans enforcing them.

snippet.title: Deterrence in Cyberspace
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Deborah Feyerick, Independent Journalist, CNN National Correspondent (Ret.)

Panelists:
Adam Hickey, Deputy Assistant Attorney General, National Security Division, US Department of Justice
Steven Kelly, Chief of Cyber Policy, Cyber Division, Federal Bureau of Investigation
Liesyl Franz, Senior Policy Advisor, Office of the Coordinator for Cyber Issues, US Department of State
Thomas Wingfield, Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy, US Department of Defense

Strategic competitors are increasingly using cyber-capabilities to seek political, economic and military advantage over the US and its allies and partners. This panel of US government experts will explore ways of deterring destabilizing and escalatory cyber-activity, and reinforcing the US framework for stability in cyberspace.

snippet.title: When Application Security “The Wrong Way” Is the Right Thing for Your Organization
snippet.description:
Jennifer Czaplewski, Director, Product Security, Target

What’s a common challenge for application security teams? To drive meaningful change and scale to the pace and size of IT. Target’s experience was no different—so the team switched from enforcer to teacher. This session will describe successes in implementing a “credit score” to measurement practices, building an exclusive(!) security champions program, and changing how to “scan all the things.”Pre-Requisites: An undestanding of white/black/gray box testing tools would be helpful but not required.

snippet.title: Alice Ain’t Home: Detecting and Countering Foreign Hackers on Social Media
snippet.description:
Alex Kobzanets, Special Agent, FBI
Chris Ott, Partner, Rothwell Figg

Hacking operations often involve coordination with false social media profiles for social engineering, foreign influence, as a communications hub, to build hacking infrastructure, to aid in money laundering, and many other tasks. Longtime FBI Special Agent Aleksander Kobzanets and attorney Chris Ott will discuss some of the ways in which false online personas are detected and combated.

snippet.title: Kubernetes Practical Attack and Defense
snippet.description:
Jay Beale, CTO, InGuardians

A rising tide of engineering teams are running Kubernetes clusters. As an infosec professional, you need to understand attacks on Kubernetes and container-based applications.

In this talk, we'll demo Kubernetes attacks on the open source Bust-a-Kube cluster, both manually and via the open source Peirates tool. We'll teach you how to attack and how to break your attacks. Come learn!Pre-Requisites: General understanding of what Kubernetes is and what its purpose is.Working knowledge of a Linux command line and familiarity with standard Linux command line tools.

snippet.title: Understanding and Explaining Post-Quantum Crypto with Cartoons
snippet.description:
Klaus Schmeh, Chief Editor Marketing, cryptovision

Are you an IT security professional, but not a mathematician? This session will explain you how post-quantum cryptography works—with a 100 percent cartoon-based slide show. All cartoon stories presented refer to easy-to-understand analogies. No advanced mathematical skills are required. Among the post-quantum methods covered are NTRU, Google’s “New Hope,” (R)LWE, QUARTZ and SLFLASH.Pre-Requisites: Understanding the concept of asymmetric cryptography
Basic mathematical skills (vectors, matrices, polynomials)

snippet.title: Mobile MFA Madness: Mobile Device Hygiene and MFA Integrity Challenges
snippet.description:
Aaron Turner, President and Chief Security Officer, HighSide
Georgia Weidman, CEO, Shevirah

Mobile authenticator apps have become the overwhelming favorite of organizations to supposedly improve the integrity of digital identities.  Unfortunately, most organizations have not paid attention to the importance of mobile device hygiene to really assure the integrity of those authenticator applications. Come see a demo of how easy it is to compromise mobile authenticator apps.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of mobile operating system basics, knowledge of how MFA systems work.

snippet.title: The Fog of Cloud Security Logging
snippet.description:
Rehman Khan, Director Cloud and Data Security, TD Ameritrade
Matt Lubbers, Cloud Security Architect Consultant, TD Ameritrade

Learn about TD Ameritrade’s approach on their journey to solve cloud security logging across multiple cloud platforms and reduce complexity. What is the human element in deciding which logs are critical for your cloud? Learn about use cases and our agile implementation approach to enable security logging on AWS and Azure to support security incident response and threat management.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of cloud security services such as AWS Cloud Trail, Azure Information protection and audit. 
Mid level understanding of security controls.

snippet.title: Consumer IoT Security: Creating a Baseline Standard
snippet.description:
Jasper Pandza, Development Lead, UK Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS)

HMG will explain why standards and complementary regulation for consumer IoT security are needed. The presenter will provide an update on the UK’s international work, in terms of the steps taken to refine ETSI TS 103 645 and also setting out how its work within specific international forums and standardization bodies is leading efforts to create international alignment on consumer IoT security.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of IoT space.

snippet.title: Secure Sandboxing in a Post-Spectre World
snippet.description:
Jonathan Foote, Principal Security Architect, Fastly
Tyler McMullen, Chief Technology Officer, Fastly

In the pursuit of stronger and more efficient ways to isolate and contain untrusted code, the industry has developed a variety of sandboxing technologies. In this session, you’ll learn more about WebAssembly and newly open-sourced Lucet, the bright lights in secure edge computing with lower resource and performance costs than competing approaches to multi-tenant isolation of native code.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of edge computing.

snippet.title: Logging in the Cloud: From Zero to (Incident Response) Hero
snippet.description:
Jonathon Poling, Managing Principal Consultant, Secureworks

So many logs, so little time. What logs even exist? Which are enabled by default? Which are the most critical to enable and configure for effective incident response? AWS. Azure. GCP. My. Dear. God. Send help! And, help you this presentation shall. This session will walk through the most important logging to enable (and how) in each cloud provider to take you from zero to incident response hero!Pre-Requisites: Basic familiarity operating with the three major Cloud providers: AWS, Azure, and GCP.

snippet.title: Intelligent Threat Intel: “LEAD” Framework
snippet.description:
Filip Stojkovski, Threat Intel Manager, Adobe

“Doing” threat intelligence is important—but doing it right is critical. We have been using threat intelligence for many years as part of the SOC, incident response and threat hunting teams; these are some of the use cases that have mastered it. Applying threat intelligence outside of these use cases is where it can get problematic. This is where the LEAD framework comes in play.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of threat Intelligence concepts and principals, security orchestration and automation. Working 
knowledge of SIEMs architecture,Threat Hunting and Security Operations principals and concepts.

snippet.title: Compromising Kubernetes Cluster by Exploiting RBAC Permissions
snippet.description:
Eviatar Gerzi, Security Researcher, CyberArk

Attackers are increasingly targeting Kubernetes clusters to compromise applications or abuse resources for things like crypto-coin mining. Through live demos, this research-based session will show attendees how. Eviatar Gerzi, who researches DevOps security, will also introduce an open source tool designed to help blue and red teams discover and eliminate risky permissions.Pre-Requisites: Basic experience with Kubernetes and familiarity with docker containers.

snippet.title: Role of the Board in Your Cybersecurity Strategy
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Chris Hetner, Executive Vice President, Moody’s/Team8 Cyber Venture

Panelists:
Nora Denzel, Independent Board Director, AMD, Ericsson, NortonLifeLock and Talend SA
Shawn Henry, CSO and President of Services, CrowdStrike
General (Ret.) Linda Medler, President and CEO, L A Medler & Associates, LLC., Independent Board Member, PNC Financial Services, Inc and PNC Bank National Association, and TransAmerica (AEGON Americas)

This panel and Q&A session, moderated by Chris Hetner who is Executive Vice President of Moody’s/Team8 Cyber Venture and serves as Special Advisor of Cyber Risk for the National Association of Corporate Directors (NACD).  Chris will be joined by CrowdStrike’s President of Services and CSO Shawn Henry and board members of global organizations. They will share real-world insights on board involvement in cybersecurity—strategically and in the wake of a cyberattack.

snippet.title: A Congressional View of Cybersecurity Priorities in the 116th Congress
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Norma Krayem, Vice President, Chair, Cybersecurity and Data Privacy Practice Group, Van Scoyoc Associates

Panelists:
Hope Goins, Majority Staff Director, House Homeland Security, US Congress, House Homeland Security Committee
Jeffrey Rothblum, Staff, US Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs
Michelle Woods, Director, US Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs (Majority)

Capitol Hill remains poised to tackle multiple cybersecurity-related issues this Congress, including legislation that addresses 5G, IoT, critical infrastructure and supply chain. Staff from the key congressional committees of jurisdiction will offer their perspective of where Congress stands on these current issues and the cybersecurity agenda for the remainder of the 116th Congress.Pre-Requisites: Insight into current Federal policy could prove beneficial.

snippet.title: Combatting Cyber Sexual Predators
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Leonard Bailey, Head of Cybersecurity Unit/Special Counsel for National Security, U.S. Department of Justice

Panelists:
Dr. MaryAnne Franks, Professor, University of Miami School of Law
Carrie Goldberg, Attorney and Owner, C.A. Goldberg
Mona Sedky, Senior Trial Attorney, US Department of Justice Computer Crime & Intellectual Property Section

Cyber sexual predators ruin their victims’ lives, causing harm that is different in kind from other cybercrime.  These immense injuries target humans rather than data, and their potential for inflicting harm is amplified by the advent of “deep fakes,” encryption and other tools. Learn about this new form of online sexual violence, how to avoid being a victim and what to do if you are.

snippet.title: NIST Privacy Framework IRL: Use Cases from the Field
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Naomi Lefkovitz, Senior Privacy Policy Advisor, Information Technology Lab, NIST

Panelists:
Timothy McIntyre, Associate General Counsel, Privacy and Product, Okta
Nick Oldham, Chief Privacy and Data Governance Officer, Equifax

The NIST Privacy Framework is here! This voluntary tool for enterprise risk management helps organizations answer a fundamental question: how are we considering the privacy impacts to individuals as we develop systems, products and services? Learn about the framework through two early adopter implementation use cases, hear about the challenges and successes, and get your own adoption tips.

snippet.title: Cloud-Powered Compromise Blast Analysis: In the Trenches with Microsoft IT
snippet.description:
Sarah Handler, Program Manager II, Microsoft
Kristina Laidler, Senior Director, SOC and Incident Response, Digital Security and Risk Engineering, Microsoft

Microsoft’s Identity Security and Protection team protects millions of authentications, but how do they protect their own walls? Learn how Microsoft Identity product team collaborated with Microsoft IT to discover and implement new blast analysis methods for identity compromise, using the power of cloud logs, SIEMs, and advanced telemetry to discover and remediate compromise.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanidng of identity and security. Knowledge of  KQL is helpful but not necessary.

snippet.title: 10 Things I Wish Every Developer Knew about Security
snippet.description:
Christopher Romeo, CEO, Security Journey

Do your developers understand security enough to secure your applications properly? A large number of security issues bury developers. Do you know best how to help them? The answer is to understand the 10 things every developer must know about security. For each item, grasp the risk and proper mitigation. Finish with how to apply security coaching to your program.Pre-Requisites: Knowledge of OWASP Top 10, application security program.

snippet.title: Look Who’s Talking: How Fraudsters Steal Voices and Make Billions
snippet.description:
Vijay Balasubramaniyan, Co-Founder and CEO, Pindrop

Voice is now the most attractive new channel for integrated customer experience and for fraudsters to harvest data and dollars. Find out how voice fraud became a multibillion-dollar industry and the unique threats different industries face. Experience the uncanny voice forgeries that fraudsters can create and learn how to recognize them. Educate yourself on 2020’s newest threat: Synthetic Voice.

snippet.title: How AI Inference Threats Might Influence the Outcome of 2020 Election
snippet.description:
Karel Baloun, Software Architect and Entrepreneur, UC Berkeley
Ken Chang, Cybersecurity Researcher, UC Berkeley
Matthew Holmes, Cybersecurity Student, UC Berkeley

What we have learned from the US 2016 election interfered by Russian. This session will inspect the inference threats on how elections in the international community interfered by inference threats. The session will also analyze the patterns of disinformation and misinformation used in the past elections and how artificial intelligence might be applied to influence the outcome of the 2020 election.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of Data Privacy Engineering concepts and general information technology background interested in inference threats.

snippet.title: Entropy as a Service: A Framework for Delivering High-Quality Entropy
snippet.description:
Ravi Jagannathan, Security Architect, VMware
David Ott, Senior Staff Researcher and Academic Program Director, VMware Research

Weak or poorly designed entropy sources undermine the strength of cryptographic protections in IoT communications and cloud. Entropy as a Service (EaaS), a framework developed in collaboration with NIST, offers a practical and effective solution. We discuss how the solution works to make high-quality entropy widely available to devices or systems lacking robust entropy sources.Pre-Requisites: Prior knowledge of entropy and entropy sources is helpful but not required.

snippet.title: Safety Implications of Medical Device Cybersecurity
snippet.description:
Penny Chase, Information Technology and Cyber Security Integrator, The MITRE Corporation
Margie Zuk, Senior Principal Cybersecurity Engineer, MITRE

It is critical to come to ground truth when high consequence vulnerabilities are discovered in medical devices. The FDA is exploring the development and viability of a Cyber Med Safety Analysis Board to integrate critical patient safety and clinical environment dimensions into the assessment and validation of high-risk/high-impact device vulnerabilities and incidents.Pre-Requisites: Familiarity with medical devices and their use within the clinical environment; familiarity with the medical device regulatory environment.

snippet.title: Recapture of Glory: The Return of Persistent Threat Actors
snippet.description:
Charles Carmakal, SVP, Strategic Services CTO, Mandiant, A FireEye Company
Jibran Ilyas, Director, Mandiant, A FireEye Company

The presenters will share personal experiences of the chess game they play with the aggressive and persistent threat actors who try to regain access to targeted networks. The presentation will provide advanced recommendations on combating subsequent targeted attacks. Presenters will also conduct live demos of the techniques threat actors have been observed using to conduct their intrusions.Pre-Requisites: Intermediate level experience in Incident Response, Red Teaming.

snippet.title: Time to Tell
snippet.description:
Steven Grobman, Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer, McAfee

The sun rises and sets like clockwork, and yesterday’s innovations are gone tomorrow. Except, it appears, in cybersecurity. Cyber-defenses from a generation ago linger front and center, even as the coming wave of quantum computing is poised to reshape the digital world. Steve Grobman, CTO for McAfee, will make the case that our current defenses share far too many traits with legacy immunology practices. It’s time to get smart. To move beyond intelligence, because the way it’s always been shouldn’t always last. It’s time to ask, can we act in time to change the future?

snippet.title: Critical Conversations: Esteemed Leaders Share How They Handle Being Heard When It Matters
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Kelly Jackson Higgins, Executive Editor, Dark Reading

Panelists:
Dr. Reem Al-Shammari, CISO, Team Leader Information Security, Kuwait Oil Company
Cheryl Biswas, Founding Board Member, The Diana Initiative
Joyce Brocaglia, CEO, Alta Associates and Executive Women’s Forum on Information Security Risk Management and Privacy
Bobbie Stempfley, Director, Software Engineering Institute, Carnegie Mellon University

Your voice is a powerful tool for advocating change and communicating critical information. Whether you are presenting to a room of thousands or a board room of ten, you want to ensure your message is heard and remembered. However, delivering important messages takes a different style and approach. Our experienced panel will share their stories and techniques when delivering presentations such as explaining why your company was hacked to the board of directors, talking to your team about a reorganization, or sharing an important need for change to senior leadership. Learn techniques to ensure your message is clear and concise, speaks to your audience in a way they can easily consume, and is actionable.

snippet.title: Power Up Your Personal Pitch
snippet.description:
Alyssa Miller, Application Security Advocate, Snyk, Ltd.
Juliet Okafor, CEO, RevolutionCyber

You have 30-60 seconds to make a first impression. Join this discussion to hear from an expert in building a leadership brand that stands out and is well respected. We’ll share tips and techniques to hone your personal elevator pitch for the board room or a cocktail event – how to use your pitch to advocate for yourself, your business, and your passions.

snippet.title: Using the Hacker Persona to Build Your DevSecOps Pipeline
snippet.description:
Dr. Aaron Estes, Lockheed Martin Fellow, Lockheed Martin
Robin Yeman, Lockheed Martin Sr. Fellow, Lockheed Martin

The requirement to build mission critical capabilities faster while ensuring the capabilities are secure and operate as intended has been an ongoing challenge in government spaces. Lockheed Martin has found that development of hacker personas support building a secure defense-in-depth strategy that enables secure pipelines and capabilities.Pre-Requisites: Basic Knowledge of DevSecOps.

snippet.title: Rocked to the Core
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Donna Dodson, Chief Cybersecurity Advisor, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

Panelists:
Marene Allison, Chief Information Security Officer, Johnson & Johnson
Paul Kocher, Security Entrepreneur and Researcher, -
Phil Venables, Board Director and Senior Advisor Cyber, Goldman Sachs

Over the last few years, significant vulnerabilities have been discovered in basic building blocks of core technologies. Heartbleed. Spectre and Meltdown. Now the news of Windows 10. As each has been discovered, the downstream ripples have been felt for years. How can we create stronger, more secure products? We need to challenge development life cycles and understand and address failure implications.

snippet.title: A Forward Look at the Cyberspace Solarium Commission
snippet.description:
Moderator:
