Mike Montgomery, Executive Director, Cyberspace Solarium Commission

Panelists:
Frank J. Cilluffo, Director, Auburn University McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security
Suzanne E. Spaulding, Senior Advisor, CSIS
John C. (Chris) Inglis, Looker Distinguished Visiting Professor of Cyber Studies, United States Naval Academy

The Cyberspace Solarium Commission is releasing its report in March 2020, and commissioners will discuss the security issues and challenges they examined and made recommendations about. Topics include reforming government structure, promoting resilience, collaboration with the private sector, reshaping the cyber-ecosystem, preserving and employing military power, and strengthening norms.

snippet.title: Fear and Loathing in Cybersecurity: An Analysis of the Psychology of Fear
snippet.description:
Dr. Jessica Barker, Co-Chief Executive Officer, Cygenta

For too long, the cybersecurity industry has attempted to use FUD to engage with the human element. This engaging talk will draw on extensive research in the sociology and psychology of fear, as well as real-world case studies, to explain why we can’t simply scare people into security, but how we can harness human bias to have a more positive impact on cybersecurity awareness, behavior and culture.Pre-Requisites: No prerequisite knowledge is required; this session will be interesting and informative for anyone working in cybersecurity interested in the human element.

snippet.title: Nation-States and Advanced Actors vs. Your Legal Team
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Steve Black, Professor of Law, Texas Tech University School of Law

Panelists:
Cristin Goodwin, Assistant General Counsel, Microsoft
Brian Levine, Managing Director, Transactions Cyber Group, Ernst & Young

Fighting nation-states and advanced actors requires a bigger toolbox, with lawyers and tech teams working together. Panelists Cristin Goodwin, Microsoft’s assistant general counsel for cybersecurity, and Brian Levine, DOJ’s former lead cyber-prosecutor, will discuss inside and outside threats, private vs. government action, and how legal teams can enable clients to defend against advanced actors.

snippet.title: Women Hacker Boss
snippet.description:
Dr. Chenxi Wang, General Partner, Rain Capital
Ning Wang, CEO, Offensive Security

snippet.title: Women in the Boardroom
snippet.description:
Dr. Chenxi Wang, General Partner, Rain Capital
Didi Dayton, Partner, Wing ventures

snippet.title: Hackers and Hackers' Advocate
snippet.description:
Dr. Chenxi Wang, General Partner, Rain Capital
Chloe Messdaghi, VP of strategy, Point3 Security

snippet.title: JavaScript Skimmers, Formjacking and Magecart: All You Need to Know
snippet.description:
Candid Wueest, Threat Researcher, Symantec

JavaScript skimmers (a.k.a. Magecart, formjacking) have become a very popular way to steal profitable data entered into websites by users. We block nearly one million such attacks every month. Learn about the latest tricks attackers use and how to avoid getting compromised and saddled with some heavy fines. This session will walk you through examples, step-by-step, explaining all you need to know.Pre-Requisites: General Understanding of HTTP requests and HTML pages.

snippet.title: Securing the Software Development Life Cycle with Machine Learning
snippet.description:
Scott Christiansen, Senior Security Program Manager, Microsoft
Mayana Pereira, Data Scientist, Microsoft

This session will cover how to identify and track security bugs in the software development life cycle using machine learning and natural language processing, including from basic concepts to handling practical problems such as mislabeled entries in the training datasets, privacy issues and deployment strategies. The talk will be self-contained and aimed at an audience of security practitioners.

snippet.title: Democratizing Security Knowledge and Automating Decisions
snippet.description:
Alex Chantavy, Software Developer, Lyft
Sacha Faust, Manager - Proactive Security, Lyft

The mission of Lyft Security is to empower the company to make informed and automated security decisions. To achieve this, Lyft released Cartography—a tool that consolidates technical assets, and the relationships between them to enable rapid exploration, repeatable decisions and automated workflows.Pre-Requisites: Basic Cloud deployment (AWS) and awareness of challenges of making security prioritization decisions.

snippet.title: Enabling and Reducing the Barriers for Collective Cyber-Defense
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Todd Weller, Chief Strategy Officer, Bandura Cyber

Panelists:
James Murphy, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, Private Sector Lead, Department of Homeland Security
Bill Nelson, CEO, Global Resilience Federation
Kimberly Watson, Technical Director, The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Lab

The concept of collective cyber-defense is gaining momentum. This diverse panel of key threat intelligence sharing experts will discuss collective cyber-defense and its benefits. The panel will also discuss efforts being made to increase the incentives to share threat intelligence and to better enable small and mid-sized organizations to use and share threat intelligence.

snippet.title: Am I allowed to subvert machine learning for fun and profit?
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Ram Shankar Siva Kumar, Data Cowboy, Microsoft/Harvard

Panelists:
Nicholas Carlini, Research Scientist, Google Brain
Betsy Cooper, Director, Aspen Tech Policy Hub, Aspen Institute
Cristin Goodwin, Assistant General Counsel, Microsoft

When your machine learning (ML) system is attacked, what legal remedies can you seek? Has your terms of service even been updated to account for such attacks?  If you’re an attacker, what risks are you assuming? This panel’s goal will be to convey the definitional challenges that attacks on ML systems pose in cybercrime, copyright and product liability law, and their impact on organizations and society.Pre-Requisites: The panel is aimed at policy and legal professionals with little to no understanding of Machine learning. All the pre-reqs are self contained. At the beginning of each section, we go through the attack - and then dissect it.

snippet.title: The CCPA Is Here: What’s Changed and What You Need to Know for Compliance
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Kevin Kiley, Vice President, OneTrust Vendorpedia

Panelists:
Natasha Amlani, Associate, Perkins Coie LLP
Rebecca Beard, Global Senior Privacy Manager, Dropbox

While California’s Consumer Privacy Act became law on Jan. 1 2020, many key amendments only just passed—meaning security and privacy pros may still be scrambling to build CCPA-compliant programs. This session will bring together the top CCPA experts to detail the latest on the law, including key amendments, share case studies and research on CCPA preparedness, and give a roadmap for compliance.Pre-Requisites: Attendees should have an intermediate understanding of the privacy landscape today and it's impact on day-to-day business operations.

snippet.title: Breaking Bad AI: Closing the Gaps between Data Security and Science
snippet.description:
Davi Ottenheimer, Founder, flyingpenguin

For years the security industry has discussed the leap into cloud computing as a paradigm shift. Get ready for another leap, as data platforms are rapidly becoming AI/ML development that requires its own new species of safety validations. This presentation, based on years of field test, will provide a quick intro and practical test list for security teams to comfortably engage data science projects.

snippet.title: Effective (and Agile) Enterprise Risk Management? Yes We Can!
snippet.description:
Vic Bhatia, Consultant – Security Risk and Compliance, A Tech Company

Current enterprise risk management (ERM) programs are geared towards financial institutions, are process-heavy, and take a long time to implement and become effective. This session will cover practical advice (and lessons learned) to quickly stand up an agile, effective, scalable and business-relevant ERM program at some of the world’s top companies.

snippet.title: Google’s Advice on Building Security into Mobile Software Development Cycle
snippet.description:
Jon Markoff, Developer Advocate, Android Security, Google

What does it mean to build a secure product? How do you ensure your product is designed securely? How do you prove it to leaders and external entities such as auditors or regulators? Learn how to produce secure products, get executive buy-in, generate artifacts for compliance and more. Learn vulnerabilities that security researchers find in top apps on Google Play, see how to find them and fix them.

snippet.title: Defending Serverless Infrastructure in the Cloud
snippet.description:
Eric Johnson, Principal Instructor, SANS Institute

Cloud workloads running on serverless infrastructure provide near zero visibility to security teams. Can security professionals inventory, scan and monitor an environment running thousands of functions for only 100 milliseconds? This technical session will examine real-world attacks and teach you how to enable security controls to defend your serverless infrastructure.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of Cloud, Serverless, and DevOps concepts. Awareness of the  OWASP Serverless Top 10 and Cloud security services, such as identity & access management, key management services, cloud networking stacks, and storage services.

snippet.title: Which Developers and Teams Are More Likely to Write Vulnerable Software?
snippet.description:
Anita D’Amico, CEO, Code Dx, Inc.

Are some developers and dev teams more likely to inadvertently introduce vulnerabilities into their code? This talk will describe several human factors—developer, team and environmental characteristics—associated with developers who inadvertently write insecure code. Learn how factors such as disrupted attention, team size, work hours and collaborative code editing correlate to software security.Pre-Requisites: Fundamental knowledge of software engineering practices and application security testing.

snippet.title: Distributed Trust: Is “Blockchain” the Best Approach?
snippet.description:
Charles Kaufman, Security Architect, Dell EMC
Radia Perlman, Fellow, Dell EMC

It is hard to sort through all the hype to know exactly what “blockchain” is. This session will explain the goals of the original blockchain (Bitcoin), why that led to that design and why that design does not actually yield the assumed properties. This session will also discuss “distributed trust” and how that can be achieved with a non-blockchain solution.

snippet.title: 10 Cybersecurity Visibility Gaps Every CISO Must Fill!
snippet.description:
Russell Eubanks, CIO, CISO and Certified SANS Instructor, Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta

The 10 gaps will each be paired with critical questions to help the successful CISO evaluate their level of visibility. This evaluation is simple enough to be finished before returning home from the RSA Conference. The results can quite easily serve as a roadmap to help the CISO effectively close these critical cybersecurity visibility gaps for years to come!Pre-Requisites: A drive for rapid professional growth.

snippet.title: Nowhere to Hide: How HW Telemetry and ML Can Make Life Tough for Exploits
snippet.description:
Rahuldeva Ghosh, Security Architect, Intel Corp
Dr. Zheng Zhang, Principal Engineer, Intel Corp

HW can reveal the execution of even the best concealed malicious code at an instruction level. This talk goes into details of how scalable, deployable, runtime threat and anomaly detection solutions can be built with CPU telemetry and machine learning. Specifics of telemetry sources, feature selection, overhead management and platform domain specific design considerations will be discussed.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of exploits/malwar and machine learning.

Some knowledge of Intel architecture would be helpful but not absolutely required.

snippet.title: Rob, Replicate and Replace: China’s Global Technology Theft and How to Confront It
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Dr. Catherine Lotrionte, Senior Associate, CSIS Technology Policy Program

Panelists:
John Demers, Assistant Attorney General for National Security, US Department of Justice
William Evanina, Director of the National Counterintelligence and Security Center, Office of the Director of National Intelligence
Major General Thomas E. Murphy, Director, Office of the Secretary of Defense

How concerned should we be about the China cyberthreat? Assistant Attorney General for National Security John Demers and the Director of the National Counterintelligence and Security Center William Evanina will describe the nature of this evolving threat, discuss what the private sector can do to mitigate its vulnerabilities and what the government is doing to counter the threat.

snippet.title: DevSecOps State of the Union
snippet.description:
Clint Gibler, Research Director, NCC Group

It’s tough to keep up with the DevSecOps resources out there, or even know where to start. This talk will summarize and distill the unique tips and tricks, lessons learned, and tools discussed in dozens of blog posts and more than 50 conference talks over the past few years, and combine it with knowledge gained from in-person discussions with security leaders at companies with mature security programs.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of the fundamental areas of modern application security programs, including threat modeling, secure code reviews, security training, building security culture/developing security champions, security scanning (static and dynamic analysis tools), monitoring and logging in production, etc.

Understanding of how software generally moves from development to production in agile environments that embrace CI/CD practices.

Basic understanding of the principles of network/infrastructure and cloud security.

snippet.title: Protect Privacy in a Data-Driven World: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning
snippet.description:
Casimir Wierzynski, Senior Director, AI Products, Intel

Combining AI and privacy doesn’t have to be a zero-sum game. An exciting set of emerging techniques known as Privacy Preserving Machine Learning (PPML) enables unlocking the power of AI while maintaining data privacy and confidentiality. These techniques come with higher computation and storage requirements. Recent research has made huge strides in performance and usability.

snippet.title: Consent, Alignment and Cooperation in the Internet Era
snippet.description:
Dr. Paul Vixie, CEO, Farsight Security, Inc.

Much of the spectrum of human action and human custom translates more or less from the real world (meatspace) into the Internet (cyber-space). Yet, some pieces of the human puzzle do not have an obvious place in the Internet game board, and this has wrought unconsidered change to human society. Is this merely the post-Westphalia era or, as many claim, the post-national era?

snippet.title: The Year Nation-State Cyber-Activities Crossed a Threshold
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Dr. Catherine Lotrionte, Senior Associate, CSIS Technology Policy Program

Panelists:
Stewart Baker, Partner, Steptoe & Johnson LLP
Tom Corcoran, Head of Cyber Security, Farmers Insurance Group
Liesyl Franz, Senior Policy Advisor, Office of the Coordinator for Cyber Issues, US Department of State
Ambassador Timo Koster, Ambassador-at-Large, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of the Netherlands

Cyberspace is regularly described as the fifth domain, another realm in which warfare will take place. But do the facts actually bear that out? This panel will review recent events to explore trends in nation-state behavior and whether we have actually crossed a threshold where cyberspace today is equivalent in significance as the other domains of air, sea, land and space.

snippet.title: Continuous Security and Governance in the Cloud Using a Graph-Based CMDB
snippet.description:
Sean Catlett, CISO, Reddit
Erkang Zheng, CISO, LifeOmic

Learn how Reddit utilizes a graph-based CMDB to gain visibility and ensure security governance in their cloud environment. This talk will explore their security journey of implementation and their results. It will also explore the power behind the graph-based approach such as the ability to aggregate configuration data from various sources via API integrations into a centralized database.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of AWS and a general understanding of graph concepts (nodes/edges).

snippet.title: Lessons Learned: 50 Years of Mistakes in Cybersecurity
snippet.description:
Steven Lipner, Executive Director, SAFECode

Over 50 years, Steven Lipner has led a lot of security projects that he thought would change the world. Many of them crashed and burned at great cost in money and reputation. There were common threads including reliance on government claims about the market and on minimal secure systems built from scratch. This talk will describe some failures, some lessons learned the hard way, and how they paid off.Pre-Requisites: Basic knowledge of the security landscape including attacks, security products and problems, and the way that organizations make decisions. Knowledge of historical government initiatives in computer and network security may also be helpful.

snippet.title: Reproducibility: The Life and Risks of a Model
snippet.description:
Celeste Fralick, Chief Data Scientist, McAfee

Analytics are becoming ubiquitous in the ever-increasing world of data. Often, those analytics are implemented without thorough consideration of the life and the risks of the model employed. This session will explore enabling reproducibility and repeatability in data science, the life cycle of a model, what is missing in typical models of today, and how to ensure a healthy and reliable life of a model.Pre-Requisites: General knowledge about security analytics is helpful but not required.

snippet.title: Cryptographic Agility: Anticipating, Preparing for and Executing Change
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Dr. Lily Chen, Project Leader, Mathematician, Cryptographic Technology Group, NIST

Panelists:
Brian LaMacchia, Distinguished Engineer, Microsoft
David Ott, Senior Staff Researcher and Academic Program Director, VMware Research
Zulfikar Ramzan, Chief Technology Officer, RSA

Cryptography is everywhere in our information systems, and anticipated requirements to migrate to post-quantum cryptography have brought the need for crypto agility into sharp focus. The panel will explore how to plan for and begin development of protocols, interfaces and roadmaps for migration to new algorithms and key sizes even before new cryptographic standards become available.

snippet.title: If You Can’t Trust the Phone Company: A Mock Trial
snippet.description:
Lisa Angelo, Cyber Liability and Data Privacy Attorney, Angelo Law Firm PLLC
Hon. Laurel Beeler, United States Magistrate Judge, United States District Court for the Northern District of California
Hoyt Kesterson, Senior Security Architect, Avertium
Julie Lewis, President, CEO and Founder, Digital Mountain
Lauren Topelsohn, Member, Mandelbaum Salsburg P.C.

A confluence of errors—the carrier clones a SMS-token phone; a doctor’s password is compromised; a vulnerability is exposed only to authenticated users of a medical laboratory; ransomware blocks access to critical test results; the ransom is paid but in the turmoil an unnoticed exfiltration of medical records reveals the dire medical condition of a corporate titan. Millions are lost. Whose fault?Pre-Requisites: General familiarity with authentication technologies, web services vulnerabilities, ransomeware, and data breach is useful but explanatory material on the technology will be presented to the presiding judge. These explanations will be tutorial in nature. No programming or design skills needed.This session will participate in polling. To participate please be sure to download the RSA Conference app prior to the session.

snippet.title: Speaking to Executives: Implementing Quantitative Risk in Cyber-Programs
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Emery Csulak, Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)/Deputy CIO for Cybersecurity, Department of Energy

Panelists:
Joe Albaugh, SVP and Chief Security Officer, Vivint SmartHome
Natalie Priani, Strategy and Advisory Lead, Accenture Federal Services
Cody Scott, Chief Cyber Risk Officer, National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)

Cybersecurity professionals struggle to defend budgets and express risk in terms which executives can appreciate. Using Factor Analysis of Information Risk (FAIR), cyber-professionals can build a defensible investment strategy. The panelists will discuss lessons learned building executive buy-in, identifying early wins, messaging quantitative risk results, tailoring and developing the workforce.Pre-Requisites: Familiarity with risk management terminology helpful.

snippet.title: Why Doesn’t the Security Industry Have a Mary Meeker–Style Report?
snippet.description:
Shannon Lietz, Director, Intuit

The security industry has become super complex, and it is difficult to navigate or understand the underlying trends to know what to do next. This talk will provide key information from lots of different data points to help guide the way. With several hundred slides, come learn about this free annual practitioner’s report and how to use it.

snippet.title: Repurposed Malware: A Dark Side of Recycling
snippet.description:
Patrick Wardle, Principal Security Researcher, Jamf

New Mac malware provides insight into the abilities of hackers and nation-states. But to other adversaries, such discoveries provide fully functional capabilities that may be weaponized for their own surreptitious purposes! This session will discuss attackers’ methodology of subverting existing malware and illustrate how such “recycled” threats may remain undetected by traditional detection approaches.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of malware.

snippet.title: Leaders Needed: Preventing the Next Big Breach
snippet.description:
Jamil Farshchi, CISO, Equifax

The roster of companies suffering massive cyber-breaches isn’t slowing down. While every breach is different, there are common elements and understanding what went wrong can help us better prepare, respond or even prevent the next attack. Jamil Farshchi, Equifax CISO, candidly shares his experiences and assessments, providing actionable insights and tactics. Pre-Requisites: A functional business background  and 5 years cybersecurity professional experience.

snippet.title: Deep Dive Analysis of Current Enterprise Network Security Mechanisms
snippet.description:
Dr. Avril Salter, Technologist, Salter & Association

This session will provide a unique perspective on how to compare and contrast how common security mechanisms are used by different security protocols. Enabling the attending an innate understanding of key  security protocols. In this session, Dr. Avril Salter will deep dive into both wireless and wired security protocols, including SSH, IPsec, TLS, 802.1X and EAP.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of key security concepts used to protect networks, including EDH, digital certs, public/private cryptography.

snippet.title: Humane Technology in Hindsight: What We Could Have Done Better
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Mary Berk, Product Management, Bluestreak Product Advisors

Panelists:
Joseph Jerome, Multistate Policy Director, Common Sense Media
Craig Spiezle, Founder, Agelight Advisory and Research Group

This panel of technologists have advocated for ethical products for decades, with mixed results. Hear their experiences—narrow metrics, short-sighted goals, commoditization of consumers, poor ethical reasoning—used to justify problematic practices, and what they could have done differently. They’ll challenge the audience with a path forward that keeps the greater good of humanity in mind.Pre-Requisites: No prerequisite knowledge is required.  Anyone with interest in the current ethical and trust challenges faced by tech in general will be able to follow this discussion with ease.  At the same time, it will offer meaty considerations for seasoned technology professionals.

snippet.title: How to Protect Your Enterprise Data (Tools and Tips)?
snippet.description:
Jeff Streelman, Director, Citi

Today firms need to take a holistic approach to identifying and protecting their sensitive data. Data is everywhere today and so this session will look at protection of data in the enterprise, on the network, in unstructured environments, in the cloud and in applications. There is no single answer to data protection, but in the face of growing privacy regulations, firms must demonstrate compliance.Pre-Requisites: None of the concepts discussed will require deep technical knowledge. A basic understanding of firms security programs would be beneficial, but not required.

snippet.title: SOC Metrics: Discovering the Key to SOC Nirvana
snippet.description:
Ankush Baveja, Presales Engineer, RSA

You can’t manage what you can’t measure. – Peter Drucker
This presentation will be all about practitioner perspective where the presenter will share some of the key actionable metrics for SOC operations. The session will explore metrics related to (1) detection, response and automation; (2) content engineering and agile methodology; (3) hunt and business alignment; and (4) analyst skill development.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of SOC operations.

snippet.title: Standing Up a Successful Product Security Program
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Andre Ristaino, Managing Director, International Society of Automation

Panelists:
Matthew Bohne, VP, Chief Product Security Officer, Honeywell Building Technologies
Paul Forney, Chief Security Architect, Schneider Electric
Nick Ritter, Vice President, Product and Industrial Security, General Electric
Megan Samford, Global Director for Product Security, Rockwell Automation

Learn more about what it’s like to stand up a product security program from leaders in the industrial control systems community who will share their experiences in designing products with security in mind, creating awareness on what product security is and is not, and running large scale response efforts to attacks like Stuxnet, Black Energy and Trisis.

snippet.title: The Security, DevOps and Chaos Playbook to Change the World
snippet.description:
Aaron Rinehart, CTO, Founder, Verica
James Wickett, Sr. Security Engineer, Verica

DevOps and the subsequent move to bring security in under the umbrella of DevSecOps has created a new ethos for security. This talk will highlight security’s place in DevOps and how topics ranging from empathy to chaos to system safety fit in organizations today. The hope is to uncover a new playbook for devs, ops and security to work together.Pre-Requisites: Experience with Development or architecture is helpful.

snippet.title: Break the Top 10 Cloud Attack Killchains
snippet.description:
Shawn Harris, Managing Principal Security Architect, Starbucks Coffee Company
Rich Mogull, CEO, Securosis

As cloud adoption matures, so do cloud attacks. This session will highlight the top 10 cloud kill chains and how to break them. The presenters will lay out each step of the chain, which are the easiest to snap, and which common security defenses work across multiple chains.Pre-Requisites: Basic technical knowledge of public cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP).

snippet.title: Malicious Documents Emerging Trends: A Gmail Perspective
snippet.description:
Elie Bursztein, Security and Anti-Abuse Research Lead, Google

Everyday Gmail defenses analyze billions of attachments to prevent malicious documents from reaching the inboxes of its users whether they are end-users or corporate ones. This talk provides a comprehensive analysis of the malicious documents that target users and corporate inboxes, an in-depth analysis of the latest evasion tactics used by attackers and what Google is doing about it.Pre-Requisites: A general understanding of what malware are. A basic knowledge of what macro, javascript, clustering, ip/asn, packer, droppers, botnets, malware as a service and exploits are. Some notion of what obfuscation is and, a basic familiarity with fud (fully undetectable documents) and adversarial attacks.

snippet.title: It’s All about the States: Navigating the Privacy Thicket
snippet.description:
Behnam Dayanim, Partner, Global Chair of Privacy & Cybersecurity Practice, Paul Hastings LLP

In the wake of Europe’s landmark GDPR and in the face of federal legislative inaction, the states have moved aggressively to the forefront. This presentation will provide guidance on new laws such as the California Consumer Privacy Act and on bills that may soon become law. It will address federal responses and provide a roadmap forward for businesses facing this ever-increasing privacy thicket.

snippet.title: Time to Spell Out Open Source Software Security
snippet.description:
Brittany O’Shea, Senior Manager, Veracode

Join this session to hear direct and concise information on how open source software (OSS) is done, much more than just publishing on public repos. Why and how vulnerabilities on OSS exist and why it’s not the developer’s fault. You will see how to keep up with constant changes and constant new vulnerabilities. An optimistic view of open source that sparks innovation with better and secure code.Pre-Requisites: Experience in application development.

snippet.title: Tales from the Front Lines 2020
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Rob Sloan, Research Director, Dow Jones / Wall Street Journal

Panelists:
Thomas Etheridge, VP of Services, Crowdstrike
Stuart McKenzie, Senior Vice President Mandiant, Mandiant / FireEye
Alex Tilley, Senior Researcher, Secureworks

This session will share the stories behind the headlines. Experts from three of the world’s best-known incident response companies discuss the incidents they worked on, the threat actors they investigated and the damage done. Hear about the true scale and complexity of cyberattacks our community faces and learn what your organization needs to do to secure data and prevent operational disruption.

snippet.title: The Emerging Role of the CPSO
snippet.description:
Stephanie Domas, CPSO and Executive Vice President, MedSec

You need a CPSO. Likely you’re wondering “why? and what’s a CPSO?” That is a problem. Millions of companies sell digital products, and security breaches are the largest monetary and reputation risk many companies face. So why aren’t there more chief product security officers? This session will focus on discussing the role, how it differs from a CSO, why it’s a critical gap, and what skills it takes.

snippet.title: 5G Trust Model: Recommendations and Best Practices for CSPs
snippet.description:
Srinivas Bhattiprolu, Senior Director – Solutions, Nokia Software

The presentation will provide a perspective of security and trust model in the 5G realm, why 5G security requires flexibility? What are the new security paradigms, approaches for 5G, how are they different from 4G ? How are the latest technologies like AI utilized in 5G security? What are the best practices and recommendations towards integration, orchestration and automation. What are the standards?Pre-Requisites: General understanding of network security and the concepts of 5G. Ideally, attendees have interacted/worked with CSPs and should have an understanding of how security is perceived and implemented in CSPs as well as knowledge of various security products and aspects like automation, integration etc.  It will be an added advantage if the attendees are involved in building 5G strategy for their respective organizations. An understanding and appreciation of technology is of paramount importance.

snippet.title: Insider Threats—When Is It Too Late?
snippet.description:
Jacqueline Atiles, Program Director, Department of State
Gregory Collins, Policy Adviser, Department of State

Based on case trends from the last five years, the Department of State’s Insider Threat Program will present an exfiltration example and work backwards, looking at possible points leading up to an event when preventative measures should have intervened. The human element of security starts by building a trusted and mindful workforce, narrowing the pool of potential threats from the inside.Pre-Requisites: Broad understanding of personnel security, human resources, cybersecurity, and insider threat would be useful, however not necessary.  The concepts and principles are beneficial to all levels, however understanding relative government agency and/or private organization structure will allow for greater comprehension.

snippet.title: Open Source Tooling for Threat Analysis and Attack Surface Management
snippet.description:
Rey Bango, Security Advocate, Microsoft
Gabriel Stocco, Senior Software Developer, Microsoft

Open source solutions continue to evolve to meet the challenges of the cyberthreat landscape with top security companies like Microsoft actively contributing and releasing toolsets and code to help defenders better secure their assets. In this session, attendees will look at MYSTICPY for threat hunting with Jupyter Notebooks and Attack Surface Analyzer for attack surface analysis.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of cybersecurity terminology.

snippet.title: Digital Channel Fraud Mitigation: Balancing Risk and Reward
snippet.description:
Julie Conroy, Research Director, Aite Group
Leonard Gusel, Head of Digital Customer Authentication, JPMorgan Chase

Balancing risk with the customer experience is top of mind for FIs and fintechs as they navigate rising account takeover and new risks associated with faster payments, while also trying to ensure risk mitigation does not impede the user experience. Learn about the top pain points in digital channels and FIs’ planned investments to evolve their technology over the next two years.

snippet.title: How to Deploy Secure Technologies to Help Reduce eCommerce Fraud
snippet.description:
William Newhouse, Cybersecurity Engineer, US Gov't Dept of Commerce, NIST, NICE, NCCoE

E-commerce fraud costs businesses billions of dollars each year. Strengthening user authentication can help mitigate these risks. This session will showcase technologies and strategies retailers can adopt to enhance user identity and reduce fraud risks in order to protect their businesses and customers.

snippet.title: Balancing UX and Secure Banking in a Fast Transforming Industry
snippet.description:
Boudewijn van der Valk, Chapter Lead Fraud Prevention, ING

The digital transformation of the financial sector leads to customers expecting an experience as offered by the “big tech” companies, and more non-digital customers being introduced to the digital experience. Presenters will cover new MOs that have emerged due to this and will also discuss the challenges fraud and cybersecurity experts are facing as processes are becoming faster and more efficient.Pre-Requisites: It helps to have a basic understanding of digital banking processes and most common fraud-MOs such as phishing and false account registration.

snippet.title: Cloud Threat Hunting
snippet.description:
Sherri Davidoff, CEO, LMG Security
Matt Durrin, Security Consultant, LMG Security

Cloud threat hunting is critical for proactively detecting and mitigating attacks on cloud and hybrid environments. Hackers leverage orchestration attacks, file synchronization poisoning, cross-tenant attacks, credential stuffing, and flaws in underlying architecture. Join this talk to learn effective cloud threat hunting tactics, including honeyclouds, integrated monitoring and behavioral analysis/AI.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of common cloud architectures will be useful.

snippet.title: How Corporate Boards and Governments Are Collaborating on Cybersecurity
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Larry Clinton, President and CEO, Internet Security Alliance

Panelists:
Stefan Becker, Head of Private Sector Office, German Federal Office for Information Security
Nora Denzel, Independent Board Director, AMD, Ericsson, NortonLifeLock and Talend SA
Daniel Kroese, Acting Deputy Assistant Director, CISA

The US Department of Homeland Security, the German Federal Office for Information Security and the Internet Security Alliance will discuss key principles for corporate board management of cybersecurity laid out in US and German versions of a Cyber-Risk Handbook, and distinctions between the German and US approach and how those differences impact issues such as insider threats and privacy.Pre-Requisites: Understanding of the role and purpose of corporate boards in company decision-making.

snippet.title: Coordinating a Competitive 5G Strategy among Freemarket Democracies
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Christy Wyatt, President and CEO, Absolute

Panelists:
Admiral Dennis Blair, Chairman and Senior Research Fello, Sasakawa USA
Michael Chertoff, Co-Founder and Executive Chairman, Chertoff Group
Arthur Coviello, Venture Partner, Rally Ventures
William Roth, Fellow, Sasakawa USA

Huawei’s potential domination of 5G markets brings with it significant economic and national security risks.  Concerns of unfair trade practices and compromise of 5G networks by China are intertwined. These two problems need to be treated independently. Deter unfair trade practices, but also devise smart industrial policies to encourage 5G and national security review of foreign 5G equipment.Pre-Requisites: Experience in national security, diplomacy, 5G technical and policy issues, technical risk as a policy issue.  Concerns surrounding China's economic policies, including economic espionage.
Executive summary
https://spfusa.org/research/meeting-the-5g-challenge/
 
Full whitepaper
https://spfusa.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/TCSC-National-Security-Strategy-for-5G-Dec-2019.pdf

snippet.title: Open Source: Promise, Perils and the Path Ahead
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Ed Moyle, Partner, SecuirtyCurve

Panelists:
Inigo Merino, CEO, Cienaga Systems
Dr. Kelley Misata, CEO, Sightline Security
Lenny Zeltser, CISO, Instructor, Author, Axonius, SANS Institute
Diana Kelley, Cybersecurity Field CTO, Microsoft

This informative discussion will explore security ramifications and implications of open source tools as well as what needs to be done differently. Have questions about open source issues? Bring them to this interactive panel where open source leaders will engage the audience to discuss the state of the industry and some of the most pressing issues from release strategies and processes to code maintenance.

snippet.title: Hot Topics in Cyber-Law 2020
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Michael Aisenberg, Principal Cyber Policy Counsel, The MITRE Corporation

Panelists:
Catherine Barrett, Cyber Policy Principal, The MITRE Corp
Lucy Thomson, Attorney, Livingston PLC
Stephen Wu, Shareholder, Silicon Valley Law Group

ABA information security leaders kick off the Law Track with the annual panel on critical emerging legal issues. Hot Topics will give attendees a practical snapshot of developments in cyber-law and litigation, policy and industry frameworks. Focus is on emerging issues from crypto-currencies, IOT/CPS, cloud, privacy/civil liberties, cyber-conflict and the international technology marketplace.Pre-Requisites: Basic high school background in Civics/US History (or US naturalization course on the basics of the U.S. Constitution) helpful to understand legal posture of issues (e.g.--difference between a ""bill"" and a ""law/statute""). Non-U.S. persons may derive less benefit from discussions if they are unfamiliar with basics of the U.S. policy/legal system.

snippet.title: The Journey of Cybersecurity in Kuwait’s Oil and Gas Industry
snippet.description:
Dr. Reem Al-Shammari, CISO, Team Leader Information Security, Kuwait Oil Company

The journey of cybersecurity in Kuwait’s oil and gas (O&G) industry encompasses the establishment of Information Security Governance Framework in companies’ sector. This established framework is to develop, implement and manage a security program to achieve strategic alignment among the companies within the oil and gas sector, risk management and value delivery.Pre-Requisites: Basic understanding of ISO 27001 would be helpful but not required.

snippet.title: Cybersecurity Tips, Tools and Techniques: Updated for 2020
snippet.description:
Ron Woerner, Cybersecurity Professor, Bellevue University

This rapid-fire presentation, updated from 2019, showcases apps and sites used in cybersecurity testing, investigations, administration and just day-to-day work. You’ll experience advanced techniques using tools such as Kali Linux, Virtualization, Wireshark, OSSEC, Nikto and Paros proxies, Spiderfoot and many more. You will get many tricks and techniques to optimize their use based on your need.Pre-Requisites: General understanding of technical infrastructures, network functions and systems administration in order to understand the nature of the tools and applications covered in this talk.

snippet.title: Forensic Techniques against Hackers Evading the Hook
snippet.description:
Mike Jankowski-Lorek, Database and Machine Learning Expert, CQURE
Paula Januszkiewicz, CEO, Cybersecurity Expert, CQURE Inc.

Cybercrime is a very lucrative business, because it’s quite easy to get away with it. Even though hackers use techniques to remain on the loose, it is possible by using forensic techniques to gather evidence to demonstrate what actually happened. During this intense session, techniques used by hackers to hide traces and forensic techniques will be demonstrated. Extremely technical session!Pre-Requisites: Experience in the field of cybersecurity or willigness to learn more about hackers' techniques.

snippet.title: Imagining the Future of Security
snippet.description:
Heather Vescent, Senior Researcher, The Purple Tornado

The foresight process can help imagine a range of possible futures and a set of parameters which influence how the future evolves; applying this process to information security threats, vulnerabilities, and controls provides useful insights into where we’re going and how to get there. This session will describe the results of applying the foresight process to today’s security landscape.

snippet.title: New Paradigms for the Next Era of Security
snippet.description:
Sounil Yu, Chief Security Scientist, Cyber Defense Matrix

As we enter the 2020s, we will see the culmination of unrecoverable attacks against our machines, infrastructure and data. In these scenarios, the old security paradigm of confidentiality, integrity and availability (CIA) no longer applies. Instead, we need to consider design patterns that follow new paradigms for the next era of security: distributed, immutable and ephemeral (DIE).

snippet.title: Leading Change: Building a Security Culture of Protect, Detect and Respond
snippet.description:
Lance Spitzner, Director, SANS Institute

Cybersecurity is no longer just about technology; it is ultimately about organizational change. Change in not only how people think about security but also what they prioritize and how they act, from the board on down. This session will enable senior leaders to leverage the two most common change management frameworks, effectively creating a strong security culture with limited time and resources.Pre-Requisites: Keen understanding and appreciation of how security has gone beyond just technology and is now driven by human issues.  This class is designed for more senior leaders who either manage people or interact with people throughout the organization.

snippet.title: Cybersecurity Has a Posse
snippet.description:
Heather Dahl, Executive Director and CEO, Sovrin Foundation
Chris Krebs, Director, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency

Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Director Christopher C. Krebs will participate in a fireside chat to discuss CISA’s expansive role as the Nation’s risk advisor, and how his agency builds partnerships across government and industry to lead the national effort to help improve American cybersecurity.

snippet.title: The Cryptographer's Panel
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Zulfikar Ramzan, Chief Technology Officer, RSA

Panelists:
Whitfield Diffie, Cryptographer and Security Expert, Cryptomathic
Arvind Narayanan, Associate Professor of Comupter Science, Princeton University
Tal Rabin, Head of Research, Algorand Foundation
Ronald Rivest, Professor, Massachusetts Institute of Technology
Adi Shamir, Borman Professor of Computer Science, The Weizmann Institute, Israel

Each year the founders and leaders of the cryptography field take the RSA Conference keynote stage to debate and discuss the most pressing issues facing the cybersecurity industry and our increasingly digital society. And each year, the stakes seem to drive higher; 2020 promises to deliver discussions around election security, individual privacy and the security of digital systems in the future. Join this year's panel to see what's top of mind in 2020.

snippet.title: RSA Conference 2020 Excellence in the Field of Mathematics Award
snippet.description:
Ron Rivest, Professor, Massachusetts Institute of Technology
Professor Joan Daemen, Radboud University Nijmegen, The Netherlands
Professor Vincent Rijmen, KU Leuven, Belgium UiB, Norway

This award recognizes innovation and ongoing contribution to the field of cryptography. The judging committee seeks to acknowledge those nominees who are pioneers in their field, and whose work has applied lasting value. Nominees are affiliated with universities or research labs.

snippet.title: We the People: Democratizing Security
snippet.description:
Wendy Nather, Head of Advisory CISOs, Cisco

The industry is still building security based on an outdated model. Where enterprises used to purchase, issue and manage the means of computing, now we need to distribute security to mobile users globally. How do we adapt? We have to change hearts and minds as well as technologies. Democratizing security means thinking differently about the people we serve. Users are not “the weakest link”; they are powerful industry drivers. We have to give up the beliefs and control we once held as unquestioned. It’s time for radical change.

snippet.title: Reality Check: The Story of Cybersecurity
snippet.description:
Rohit Ghai, President, RSA

It's our stories that make us human. We love a memorable narrative and often exaggerate characters and fudge reality to fit the narrative. The cybersecurity industry has an incomplete and overly simplified view of the characters in our story: the human element. It's time to review the facts and set the story straight. After all, we are only as great as the story we leave behind.

snippet.title: RSAC 2020 Opening with George Takei
snippet.description:
George Takei

Special guest George Takei kicks off RSA Conference 2020 with an inspirational presentation about the RSAC 2020 theme, Human Element, and what makes us, us.

snippet.title: Enterprise Incident Management: How to Get Everyone Ready for a Crisis
snippet.description:
Erin Becker, Director, Target

Erin Becker will talk about how Target built an enterprise cyber-response program, structured the team and learned important lessons along the way. She’ll tell stories about Target’s war games and tabletop exercises—including a surprise war game launched to prepare Target’s leadership team for a cyber-crisis—and hear the three main things Erin learned about building a cyber-response program.Pre-Requisites: Prior experience (from entry to mid-level and senior leaders) in cyber security or incident response.

snippet.title: The Power of Cooperation: Why Cybersecurity Risks Need Public-Private Punch
snippet.description:
Tim Callahan, SVP, Global Chief Security Officer, Aflac
Dick Clarke, Founder and CEO, Good Harbor Security Risk Management

Sophisticated, unrelenting cyberthreats are forcing IT and business leaders to find more effective solutions. Learn from Good Harbor and Aflac experts about the benefits of taking a public-private approach to addressing cyberthreats. Understand the different responsibilities of the Federal Government and corporations and new partnership opportunities to more effectively enhance cybersecurity.Pre-Requisites: More than 5 years of experience and a working understanding of terms and concepts.  Contains instructive demos, management tools, deep process discussions, or similar level of content.

snippet.title: Time to Reboot: The I/O Psychology of Cybersecurity
snippet.description:
Annalea Ilg, Chief Information Security Officer, Involta
Keenan Skelly, President and CEO, Spark Security Solutions, Inc.

Security professionals feel more losses than wins and cultural conflict can be paralyzing. Instead of adopting more tools and technology, we need to dive deep into the “science of behavior” to align professionals with business outcomes. Using a psychological approach to make cyber-teams more versatile is the unexpected answer.

snippet.title: You Feel Me? How Reading Chemistry Can Improve Your Success
snippet.description:
Lisa Lee, Chief Security Advisor, Global Lead for Financial Services, Microsoft

It’s right in front of us every day and impacts all our interactions: chemistry. How can data driven people learn to read personalities and adjust our behavior to maximize our interactions? How can we be more aware of signals and modify our reactions? What if you could turn adversaries to advocates? Consider what data and psychology can teach us and explore personality types, conflict and success.

snippet.title: IOT Monetization Schemes from the Cybercrime Underground
snippet.description:
David Sancho, Senior Threat Researcher, Trend Micro

The session will highlight the results of our investigation into how different criminal underground sites are discussing attacks against IoT infrastructure—both exploitation and monetization schemes. The speaker will discuss the current state of affairs, whether the chatter changes by the language of the underground site, and our predictions as to what the future may look like in this developing field.

snippet.title: Targeted Ransomware: A Potent Threat Begins to Proliferate
snippet.description:
Jon DiMaggio, Sr. Threat Intelligence Analyst, Symantec
Dick O’Brien, Principal Editor, Symantec

The old ransomware menace has reinvented itself and is back with a new twist. Targeted ransomware attacks have grown apace over the past year, with 40 percent more organizations targeted year-on-year. Learn from firsthand experience how the new breed of targeted ransomware attackers infiltrate a victim’s network and gain insights into how to avoid such threats.

snippet.title: Hi-Tech Mass Extortion: Lessons from the SamSam Ransomware Prosecution
snippet.description:
William Hall, Senior Counsel, US Department of Justice, Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section

Technology has transformed garden-variety extortion into a crime capable of causing destruction on a massive scale: ransomware. This session will explore the challenges posed by ransomware and law enforcement’s response to it through the prism of the investigation that led to the charging of two Iranian nationals with executing one of the most notorious ransomware schemes to date, SamSam.

snippet.title: Ransomware Spread through Various Distribution Methods from 2018 to 2019
snippet.description:
Jin Wook Kim, CERT Manager, WINS

The session will explain how the ransomware distribution methods have changed from 2018 to 2019. One of them is GandCrab. It used LNK vulnerabilities in the form of an email message. In addition, Attacker uploaded Gandcrab ransomware disguised as an Adobe Flash Player update in Korean websites that were to be stolen by the attacker.

snippet.title: Lessons from America’s Two Largest Cities on Preparing for Cyberattacks
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Laura Koetzle, Vice President, Group Director, Forrester

Panelists:
Timothy Lee, Chief Information Security Officer, City of Los Angeles, City of Los Angeles
Lieutenant Gustavo Rodriguez, Lieutenant, FBI NY Cyber Task Force, NYPD

Cities are the hottest target for cybercriminals as municipalities of all sizes are increasingly being caught in their crosshairs. The last 20 years have been focused on fortifying our cities against terrorist attacks, but what has been done to deal with cyberattacks? In this panel, hear what America’s two largest cities are doing to better prepare for cybersecurity threats.

snippet.title: Talent Exfiltration: An Insider’s Guide to the Talent Attack Life Cycle
snippet.description:
Deidre Diamond, Founder and CEO, CyberSN

What are you doing to lower the risk of your cybersecurity talent leaving? You will learn how and when cybersecurity talent becomes vulnerable and compromised, how a skilled cyber-recruiter creates reconnaissance and weaponizes it, how a skilled cyber-recruiter creates an opportunity to exploit your talent, at what moment talent compromise occurs, and how to develop talent exfiltration defenses.

snippet.title: I Believe, I Belong, I Matter: Solving the Cyber Risk Talent Gap
snippet.description:
Malcolm Harkins, Chief Security and Trust Officer, Cymatic

Ever wonder how to create lasting employee and management commitments? How to reduce the talent gap plaguing information security organizations? In this talk, Malcolm Harkins will explore how to make smarter empathic decisions, to handle setbacks with resilience, and to create greater team performance. He will share what strategic thinkers do to inspire purpose, passion, and persistence.

snippet.title: Is There a High School Dropout Waiting to Rock Your Hiring Manager?
snippet.description:
Steven Allen, Startup Entrepreneur, Autism Advocate
Winn Schwartau, Founder, SAC

This session will share several best practices that are currently being used by companies like SAP, Microsoft, IBM and DXC to find, assess, train, hire and support individuals with autism. Speakers will discuss why their attempts are not having the numerical success they predicted when they started. The session will also include information on sources of funding available to pilot and support programs.

snippet.title: Practical Cyber Diversity Now: The Adulting Discussion On-Trend In-Motion
snippet.description:
Lisset Diaz Cervantes, Security Management Specialist, SWIFT
Rosanna Kurrer, Managing Director, Cyberwayfinder asbl

Success, errors and archetypes from a European gender inclusion effort pivoting established business professionals into cybersecurity practitioners. In our reality of pervasive cybercrime and hybrid-cyber-warfare with everything under attack, we are still told “learn the language of business and think like a hacker.” We are reversing this and teaching our business colleagues the language of cyber.

snippet.title: Prioritizing Threats: What Would Threat Researchers Do (WWTRD)
snippet.description:
Moderator:
Anthony Nash, Director of Cyber Intelligence Strategy, Anomali

Panelists:
Chris Cochran, Threat Intelligence Lead, Netflix
Jon DiMaggio, Sr. Threat Intelligence Analyst, Symantec
Timothy Gallo, Solutions Architect, Service and Intelligence, FireEye

Thousands of daily headlines, threat bulletins, social media alerts, and bits and pieces of advice inundate everyone who has skin in the security and risk equation. This panel will feature experienced sources with backgrounds in threat research and intelligence, discussing how they view the threat landscape and what they would do if they had to make decisions about prioritizing security.

snippet.title: Ransomware’s Threat Over Critical Infrastructure and Industrial Production
snippet.description:
Daniel Kapellmann Zafra, Technical Analysis Manager, Cyber Physical, FireEye

Since at least 2017, there has been an increase in public disclosures of ransomware incidents impacting industrial production and critical infrastructure organizations. This session will show the bigger picture and illustrate ransomware implications from a holistic perspective that considers impacts both at the enterprise and process level, analyzing the problem both from an IT and OT perspective.

snippet.title: Come for the Mission, Stay for the Culture
snippet.description:
Caroline Wong, Chief Strategy Officer, Cobalt.io

It’s hard to hire infosec teams. It’s even harder to keep teams together. At the same time, it’s never been more important to build and sustain a successful InfoSec organization. This session will propose several strategies for attracting and retaining great infosec talent. It’ll explore mission and culture, and how to create these authentically and use them as tools to support and protect your team.

snippet.title: Deep Fakes Are Getting Terrifyingly Real: How Can We Spot Them?
snippet.description:
Amanda House, Data Scientist, McAfee
Sherin Mathews, Senior Data Scientist, McAfee

Deepfake is a new and significant advancement of deep learning on how bad actors can generate indistinguishable fake text, images and videos. This session will present a demonstration of this emerging threat along with how deepfake content is created, its implications, and strategies on how to detect it.

snippet.title: Making the Leap: Transforming from Techie to Security Leader
snippet.description:
Todd Fitzgerald, CISO, Cybersecurity Leadership Author, CISO SPOTLIGHT, LLC

You have been a techie and developed great security skills. Now you want to move into management. Should you? Will you be happy there? How will your life change? Is this a good move? How will you get there? This session will examine what this career choice really means—and how to move to a CISO/security leader role.

snippet.title: Feds Fighting Ransomware: How the FBI Investigates and How You Can Help
snippet.description:
Joel DeCapua, Special Agent, FBI

It seems that almost every week there is a new report about a ransomware infection impacting a major enterprise. What has the FBI done to combat ransomware? What is the FBI’s strategy moving forward? And how can the security community collaborate with law enforcement? Join us as your friendly neighborhood FBI agent discusses the tools and tradecraft used to investigate ransomware actors.

snippet.title: Protecting Data from Ransomware and Breaches: Demos and Designs
snippet.description:
Michael Ekstrom, Lead Cybersecurity Engineer, MITRE
Mary Yang, Portfolio Manager, The MITRE Corporation

Little is as valuable to an enterprise as its data and protecting it can seem an overwhelming task. Join cybersecurity engineers from NIST’s NCCoE as they demystify data security by demonstrating their latest standards-based guidance on mitigating the impact of ransomware and data breaches using off-the-shelf tools.

snippet.title: Digital Transformation, Deception and Detox: Security Leaders Anonymous
snippet.description:
Elliott Franklin, Director of IT Governance & Security, Loews Hotels

Security leaders are being asked not only to protect companies but also lead their digital transformation and innovation. We now have a seat at the board table and we are passionate about our team and our work.  But we are not taking care of ourselves and our personal relationships. Anxiety, substance abuse, divorce are just a few of the side effects. Let’s discuss how to change this trend!

snippet.title: Ransomware: Partnering for Recovery
snippet.description:
Deborah Blyth, CISO, State of Colorado

2018 was a bad year for the Colorado Department of Transportation when it suffered a ransomware outbreak taking its business operations environment offline for a month, in a very well-publicized event. The CISO for Colorado will talk about the SamSam ransomware outbreak in 2018, lessons learned, improvements implemented, the partnerships that led to recovery, and the health of the security program two years post-SamSam.

snippet.title: Hacking Your Cybersecurity Career
snippet.description:
Ron Woerner, Cybersecurity Professor, Bellevue University

Looking to break into cybersecurity? To get the right job, consider using hacking techniques to break through the hiring process. Here you’ll learn 3 traits of a well-rounded professional, the career triad, and steps for hacking your career including: visualizing your goals, knowing the best path for you, social engineering your next boss, active learning, and keeping your cyber skills sharp.

snippet.description:
Presenters:
Dr. Aaron Estes, Lockheed Martin Fellow, Lockheed Martin Corporation
Robin Yeman, Fellow, Lockheed Martin

The requirement to build mission critical capabilities faster while ensuring the capabilities are secure and operate as intended has been an ongoing challenge in government spaces. Lockheed Martin has found that development of hacker personas support building a secure defense-in-depth strategy that enables secure pipelines and capabilities.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/using-the-hacker-persona-to-build-your-devsecops-pipeline

snippet.title: Quick Look: #Psybersecurity: Mental Health Impact of Cyberattacks
snippet.description:
Presenter: Ryan Louie, Psychiatrist, Vituity

What happens to a person’s mental health during a cyberattack? This session will discuss the impacts on victims and first-responders. Attendees will gain an understanding of mental health conditions that can be caused by cyberattacks. Utilizing this knowledge of psybersecurity, attendees will learn ways to build more resilient mental security networks for better incident response and cyberdefense.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/psybersecurity-mental-health-impact-of-cyberattacks

snippet.title: Quick Look: Case Files from 20 Years of Business Logic Flaws
snippet.description:
Chetan Conikee, Chief Technology Officer, ShiftLeft, Inc.

What do Citibank, First American Financial, McDonald’s, Nordstrom and Signet/Jared Jewelers have in common? Each company suffered from a type of vulnerability that alluded code analysis tools: business logic flaws. Chetan Conikee will present “case files” of each company along with a full set of taxonomies of business logic flaws coupled with scenarios and exploitative patterns.

Pre-Requisites: General understanding of and experience in application security and DevOps.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/case-files-from-20-years-of-business-logic-flaws

snippet.title: Quick Look: Dude, You’re Getting a Dell: Organizational Culture Shift to SDL Maturity
snippet.description:
Presenters:
Mohit Arora, Software Security Architect, Dell Technologies
Richard Tonry, Firmware Security Architect, Dell Technologies

Dell is an organization of 157,000 employees that ships millions of PCs, devices and software products every year. An organization of this size presents challenges in getting people to shift their security mindset. This talk will discuss the challenges, changes and lessons learned on the journey towards a security-focused culture within Dell’s PC business unit and alignment with the rest of the company.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/dude-youre-getting-a-dell-organizational-culture-shift-to-sdl-maturity

snippet.description:
Presenter: Jim Mirochnik, Senior Partner, CEO, HALOCK Security Labs

Securing the right budget is often harder to do than performing the project requiring the budget.  If your goal is to secure the budget you need vs. prioritizing into the budget you’re given, then you need a different approach than what you’ve been using.  Learn how an industry-proven methodology (DoCRA) can help you communicate to the C-Suite in a new way and receive the budget you truly need.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/securing-the-budget-you-need-translating-security-risks-to-business-value

snippet.title: Quick Look: DevSecOps State of the Union
snippet.description:
Clint Gibler, Research Director, NCC Group

It’s tough to keep up with the DevSecOps resources out there, or even know where to start. This talk will summarize and distill the unique tips and tricks, lessons learned, and tools discussed in dozens of blog posts and more than 50 conference talks over the past few years, and combine it with knowledge gained from in-person discussions with security leaders at companies with mature security programs.

Pre-Requisites: General understanding of the fundamental areas of modern application security programs, including threat modeling, secure code reviews, security training, building security culture/developing security champions, security scanning (static and dynamic analysis tools), monitoring and logging in production, etc. Understanding of how software generally moves from development to production in agile environments that embrace CI/CD practices. Basic understanding of the principles of network/infrastructure and cloud security.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/devsecops-state-of-the-union

snippet.title: Quick Look: Consent, Alignment and Cooperation in the Internet Era
snippet.description:
Dr. Paul Vixie, CEO, Farsight Security, Inc.

Much of the spectrum of human action and human custom translates more or less from the real world (meatspace) into the Internet (cyber-space). Yet, some pieces of the human puzzle do not have an obvious place in the Internet game board, and this has wrought unconsidered change to human society. Is this merely the post-Westphalia era or, as many claim, the post-national era?

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/consent-alignment-and-cooperation-in-the-internet-era

snippet.title: Quick Look: Deep Dive Analysis of Current Enterprise Network Security Mechanisms
snippet.description:
Presenter: Dr. Avril Salter, Technologist, Salter & Association

This session will provide a unique perspective on how to compare and contrast how common security mechanisms are used by different security protocols. Enabling the attending an innate understanding of key  security protocols. In this session, Dr. Avril Salter will deep dive into both wireless and wired security protocols, including SSH, IPsec, TLS, 802.1X and EAP.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/deep-dive-analysis-of-current-enterprise-network-security-mechanisms

snippet.title: Quick Look: The Age of Economic Warfare: What to Expect in This New Reality
snippet.description:
Presenter: Galina Antova, Co-Founder, Claroty

The world runs on industrial control systems, and they are valuable targets for attackers seeking to advance geopolitical agendas. This session will address the scenarios of economic warfare leveraging cyberattacks on infrastructure, what it means in terms of potential impact to your organization, common pitfalls from the field and how to avoid them.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/the-age-of-economic-warfare-what-to-expect-in-this-new-reality

snippet.description:
What topics are expected to be front and center at RSAC 2020? From converged IT and AI to the Human Element, find out what will be generating the most buzz as the RSA Conference 2020 Advisory Board shares their annual Conference preview.

snippet.description:
Presenter: Jeffrey Blatt, Founder, X Ventures

Active shooters intending to cause mass casualties exhibit warning behaviors that are usually not detected by law enforcement prior to an attack. Predictive policing technology utilizing “all source data collection” coupled with AI may be used to monitor social media, government and other data sets to identify a potential active shooter’s pre-crime behavior allowing for early intervention.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/pre-crime-detection-of-active-shooters-using-predictive-policing-systems

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/algorithmic-policing-based-on-behavioral-threat-indicators-should-we

snippet.title: Quick Look: The Impact of Software Security Practice Adoption Quantified
snippet.description:
Presenter: Larry Maccherone, DevSecOps Transformation, Comcast Business

This talk will present research quantifying the impact that various software security practices have on security risk outcomes. Comcast has correlated practices like secure coding training, threat modeling, pen testing, SAST/IAST/SCA tool usage, security code review, etc.. with outcome data from 200 different teams in the technologically and process maturity diverse environment inside Comcast.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/the-impact-of-software-security-practice-adoption-quantified

snippet.title: Quick Look: Leading Change: Building a Security Culture of Protect, Detect and Respond
snippet.description:
Presenter: Lance Spitzner, Director, SANS Institute

Cybersecurity is no longer just about technology; it is ultimately about organizational change. Change in not only how people think about security but also what they prioritize and how they act, from the board on down. This session will enable senior leaders to leverage the two most common change management frameworks, effectively creating a strong security culture with limited time and resources.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/leading-change-building-a-security-culture-of-protect-detect-and-respond

snippet.title: Where Law and Tech Will Collide in 2020
snippet.description:
Presenters:
Angelique Carson, Editor, IAPP
Rita Heimes, GC & Chief Privacy Officer, IAPP
Cathy Scerbo, VP, Chief Information Officer, IAPP

The acceleration of “tech disruption” across all industries is exacerbating privacy risks to consumers globally. In response, 2020 will bring laws increasingly requiring that tech solutions be built with privacy by design, or face potential—and steep—fines. In addition, under California’s Consumer Privacy Act, companies will be exposed to class-action lawsuits for data breaches. Meanwhile, NIST has released draft privacy controls, providing guidance for companies to manage privacy risks. In this webcast, experts in the privacy and technology fields will discuss where technology and the law might find friction in 2020, including how the growing use of disruptive technologies risks exposing consumer data.

https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/webcast/37-law-and-tech-collide

snippet.description:
Presenter: Daksha Bhasker, Principal Cybersecurity Architect, Comcast Business

Over the top (OTT) solutions are proliferating rapidly, along with global Internet penetration that has reached almost 4.4 billion people. With access to vast reserves of consumer and business information across the globe, that is attractive to scammers, security designs and architectures for OTT solutions, are quite distinct from traditional “walled garden” architectures. Over the top security is here!

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/over-the-top-security

snippet.description:

The presentation will provide a perspective of security and trust model in the 5G realm, why 5G security requires flexibility? What are the new security paradigms, approaches for 5G, how are they different from 4G ? How are the latest technologies like AI utilized in 5G security? What are the best practices and recommendations towards integration, orchestration and automation. What are the standards?

snippet.description:
Presenter: Behnam Dayanim, Partner, Global Chair of Privacy & Cybersecurity Practice, Paul Hastings LLP

In the wake of Europe’s landmark GDPR and in the face of federal legislative inaction, the states have moved aggressively to the forefront. This presentation will provide guidance on new laws such as the California Consumer Privacy Act and on bills that may soon become law. It will address federal responses and provide a roadmap forward for businesses facing this ever-increasing privacy thicket.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/its-all-about-the-states-navigating-the-privacy-thicket

snippet.title: Quick Look: The Past Is Not the Future: Practical Ethics for Algorithms
snippet.description:
Presenter: Mike Kiser, Global Security Advocate, Office of the CTO, SailPoint
Presenter: Behnam Dayanim, Partner, Global Chair of Privacy & Cybersecurity Practice, Paul Hastings LLP

Who was the real Tara Simmons? A court was forced to decide whether she was a convicted felon (her past) or a respected lawyer (her future). Algorithms that use the past to predict the future are common but can cause great harm. Via the story of Simmons and others like her, presenters will develop a practical ethical standard (with currently available tools) for evaluating and comparing algorithms.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/the-past-is-not-the-future-practical-ethics-for-algorithms

snippet.title: Quick Look: The Industrial Cyberthreat Landscape: 2019 Year in Review
snippet.description:
Presenter: Robert Lee, CEO, Dragos, Inc.

The industrial cyberthreat landscape is constantly changing with new adversaries, new vulnerabilities and new attacks as well as lessons learned from incident response cases. This presentation will reveal new cases, threats, and lessons learned with the annual Dragos Year in Review reports from the industrial control system (ICS) community. Participants will leave with actionable recommendations.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/the-industrial-cyberthreat-landscape-2019-year-in-review

snippet.title: Quick Look: You, Me and FIPS 140-3: A Guide to the New Standard and Transition
snippet.description:
Presenter: Ryan Thomas, CST Laboratory Manager, Acumen Security

On March 22nd, 2019, FIPS 140-3 was officially signed. After years of waiting, the new standard based on ISO/IEC 19790 and ISO/IEC 24759 will succeed FIPS 140-2. Find out what’s new in FIPS 140-3. What are the key differences between FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3? Learn about the planned transition timeline and what will happen to current FIPS 140-2 certificates.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/you-me-and-fips-1403-a-guide-to-the-new-standard-and-transition

snippet.title: Quick Look: Cybersecurity Tips, Tools and Techniques: Updated for 2020
snippet.description:
Presenter: Ron Woerner, Cybersecurity Professor, Bellevue University

This rapid-fire presentation, updated from 2019, showcases apps and sites used in cybersecurity testing, investigations, administration and just day-to-day work. You’ll experience advanced techniques using tools such as Kali Linux, Virtualization, Wireshark, OSSEC, Nikto and Paros proxies, Spiderfoot and many more. You will get many tricks and techniques to optimize their use based on your need.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/cybersecurity-tips-tools-and-techniques-updated-for-2020

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/personal-professional-development-for-all-career-stages

snippet.title: Quick Look: How to Harness Dev and Their Native Tools to Accelerate DevSecOps
snippet.description:
Presenter: Cindy Blake, Senior Security Evangelist, GitLab

This step-by-step view through the developers’ workflow will show exactly where application security can be embedded. A case study will show what can be achieved and a brief demo of an actual developer pipeline will help the audience see exactly how app sec can become iterative, automated and embedded into the automated DevOps processes.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/how-to-harness-dev-and-their-native-tools-to-accelerate-devsecops

snippet.title: Quick Look: Designing Trustworthy AI: A UX Framework
snippet.description:
Carol Smith, Sr. Research Scientist - Human-Machine Interaction, Carnegie Mellon University, SEI, Emerging Technology Center

Artificial intelligence (AI) holds great promise to empower us with knowledge and scaled effectiveness. To harness the power of AI systems, we can—and must—ensure that we keep humans safe and in control. This session will introduce a new user experience (UX) framework to guide the creation of AI systems that are accountable, de-risked, respectful, secure, honest and usable.

https://www.rsaconference.com/usa/agenda/designing-trustworthy-ai-a-ux-framework

snippet.title: The 5 Most Dangerous New Attack Techniques: Are They Evolving?
snippet.description:
Moderator: Alan Paller
Panelist: Ed Skoudis
Panelist: Heather Mahalik
Panelist: Johannes Ullrich

Each year at RSA Conference, SANS Institute provides the authoritative summary of the most dangerous new attack techniques. Their 2019 list included accurate predictions of smartphone attacks, DNS manipulation, domain fronting, cloud-on-cloud attacks and CPU flaws. Learn more about their 2019 list, see new data about how these attacks have evolved and get up to speed on how to defeat them.

https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/webcast/36-five-most-dangerous-attacks-evolving

snippet.title: New Paradigms for the Next Era of Security
snippet.description:
As we enter the 2020s, we will see a significant increase in the number and severity of unrecoverable attacks against our machines, infrastructure and data. Under this form of threat, the old security paradigm of confidentiality, integrity and availability (CIA) no longer applies. Instead, we need to consider a new paradigm that focuses on resiliency rather than security. In this webcast, we’ll explore new design patterns supported by three principles: distributed, immutable and ephemeral (DIE).

https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/webcast/35-new-paradigms-for-the-next-era-of-security

snippet.title: Leading Change for CISOs: Embedding a Secure Culture
snippet.description:
Presenter: Lance Spitzner, Director, SANS Security Awareness

There was a time when cybersecurity was strictly a concern for IT departments, but those days are long gone. In today’s far-reaching threat environment, cybersecurity needs to be baked into the very fabric of a company—a move that necessitates organizational change.

In this webcast, we’ll look at how organizations—starting at the CISO level and branching out companywide—can leverage organizational change models for an all-inclusive culture of security. Learn the common missteps to avoid, and how appealing to emotion rather than statistics can help drive results.

https://www.rsaconference.com/industry-topics/webcast/leading-change-for-cisos

snippet.title: RSAC Unplugged 2019 Sydney: Panel: Regulation and Legislation
snippet.description:
Moderator:
 -  Leonard N. Kleinman, Chief Cyber Security Advisor, RSA International (APJ and EMEA) 

Panelists:
 -  Narelle Devine, CISO, Australian Government Department of Human Services
 -  Tony Kitzelmann, General Manager & CISO, Information Technology and Cyber Security Branch, Infrastructure Operations Division, Australian Digital Health Agency

The field of cybersecurity has seen enormous change in regulations in the last few years. There is greater emphasis on privacy, security and directives towards safeguarding IT systems. A patchwork of rules and regulations have developed in response to the evolving cyber threat but what does this mean for organisations and leaders of business? How do you keep pace? We are only beginning to see the potential extent of fines companies could face for non-compliance to regulation and what are some of the un-intended consequences and impact?
