snippet.title: Building Security Processes for Developers and DevOps Teams
snippet.description:
Ainsley Braun, CEO, Tinfoil Security

Agile development has changed our technological world. Code is pushed weekly, daily and even hourly, and security has a hard time keeping up. Security can only be achieved through multidisciplinary teams that handle development and security within themselves. Learn to bridge the communication gap between operations, security, and development, and break down those walls.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the way developers test applications to date.2: Learn new techniques to coordinate communication between ops, development and security teams.3: Start thought process of automating tools into the dev process to reduce stress on security teams.

snippet.title: Your Data’s Integrity: Protect and Respond to Ransomware and Critical Events
snippet.description:
Anne Townsend, Lead Cybersecurity Engineer, NIST/NCCoE – MITRE

At RSA18, we shared ways to quickly recover from an event that alters or destroys data. This year, we’re back with an entire suite that organizations can deploy to effectively identify, protect, detect and respond to data integrity events. These solutions are follow-on projects to the highly publicized NIST Special Publication (SP) 1800-11, Recovering from Ransomware and Other Destructive Events.Learning Objectives:1: Understand easy-to-implement data security methods.2: Learn how to build a data security architecture with commercially available technologies.3: Gain line-by-line guidance and how-to directions to build this solution in your own organization.

snippet.title: Mobile Security and the Post-Perimeter World: 10 Years of Mobile Threats
snippet.description:
Apurva Kumar, Security Intelligence Engineer, Lookout

Michael Murray, Chief Security Officer, Lookout

The first decade of widespread use of smartphones and mobile operating systems saw a constant evolution of the attack landscape. Using a decade of data around mobile threats and vulnerabilities, the presenters will show the trends and principles that will drive the direction of the future of risk management, particularly as mobile platforms increasingly operate outside traditional perimeters.

snippet.title: Studies of 2FA, Why Johhny Can’t Use 2FA and How We Can Change That
snippet.description:
L Jean Camp, Professor, Indiana University

Sanchari Das, Doctoral Researcher, Indiana University

Why do people fail to adopt 2FA? Reasons for resistance include usability, acceptability and risk perception. What usability failures stop enrollment? What are common avoidance behaviors and their motivations? What type of interactions can mitigate these? The presentation will include methods and tools to evaluate sources of resistance as well as strategies and resources to change these.

snippet.title: The Digital Risk Dilemma: How to Protect What You Don’t Control
snippet.description:
Nick Hayes, VP of Strategy, IntSights Cyber Intelligence

More of your attack surface resides on web infrastructure you don’t own or control. To protect your digital assets and thwart malicious lookalikes on everything from social networks to criminal marketplaces, you must shift security priorities from prevention to detection and remediation. This session will outline tools, tactics and best practices to safeguard your entire digital footprint.Learning Objectives:1: Understand why security priorities must shift from prevention to active detection and remediation.2: Understand how to align activities to three core steps of digital risk protection: map, monitor and mitigate.3: Take away practical tools and techniques, like sample classifications and decision-tree diagrams.Pre-Requisites:High-level knowledge and interest in security strategy, threat intelligence and process design.

snippet.title: 2028 Future State: Long Live the Firewall?
snippet.description:
Harry Sverdlove, CTO and Founder, Edgewise Networks

Jennifer Minella, VP of Engineering & Security, Carolina Advanced Digital, Inc.

Marcus Ranum, Consultant, Independent

Adam Shostack, President and Consultant, Adam Shostack & Associates

The threat landscape has changed since the invention of the firewall 30 years ago, but not because threat actors or their motivations have changed; our networks and how we need to protect them have changed. Not only do we need to start developing tools that adapt to the threats of today, but we need to threat model in a more sophisticated way and ask more questions about what can go wrong.Learning Objectives:1: Understand what the firewall of 2028 will look like, and if it will even exist as we know it today.2: Examine the commercial tools market to see what best adapts to shifts in attack tactics and surface.3: Learn how to adapt threat modeling to accommodate the actual threat landscape.Pre-Requisites:Basic understanding of the security landscape.

snippet.title: The Metrics Manifesto
snippet.description:
Richard Seiersen, President, M-Cubed

Learn to make metrics like a pro using predictive analytics. Walk away inspired to apply these approaches to security operations as well as board presentations. Some things you will hear here and nowhere else at RSA include decision science, empirical and subjective Bayes, probabilistic programming, quantitative risk management and much more.Learning Objectives:1: Learn the basics or predictive analytics for security.2: Learn how to measure attack surface.3: Learn how to present advanced security metrics to the board.

snippet.title: Cybersecurity Rubicon: Is US Domestic and Foreign Cyber-Policy on Track
snippet.description:
Sam Curry, Chief Security Officer, Cybereason

Mieke Eoyang, Vice President for the National Security Program, Third Way

Chris Painter, Commissioner, Global Commission on the Stability of Cyberspace

Ari Schwartz, Managing Director, Venable

Kiersten Todt, President and Managing Partner, Liberty Group Ventures, Managing Director, The Cyber Readiness Institute

US cyber-policy has faced a significant set of challenges in the last two years. How the country responds to the growing threats will shape its diplomatic, military and economic power. With the stakes this high, is the US getting it right? Join a panel of experts who have worked within the DoD, NIST and White House on these issues to discuss where policy is headed and its success rate.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the efficacy of currently policy efforts.2: Experience the conflicts of interest when policy is discussed.3: Learn the factors that have led to the current state of play.Pre-Requisites:Basic understanding of US policy in cyberspace. Knowing the main institutions involved and their responsibilities will make following the conversation easier.

snippet.title: Building Security In—DevSecOps
snippet.description:
Noopur Davis, SVP, Chief Product and Information Security Officer, Comcast

Many believe that better security comes from robust independent gating, but DevOps has proven that you can safely deploy orders of magnitude faster without human gating. Comcast uses a DevSecOps approach which focuses on automation, speed and team ownership of end-to-end product security lifecycle. It’s agile and developer-focused. It’s about building security in rather than bolting it on.Learning Objectives:1: Learn our six-part approach, including executive sponsorship, craftsmanship, SDL, tooling and more.2: Understand how and why to focus on DevOps teams, while not leaving others behind.3: Find out why security is not just the right thing to do, but how it’s critical to make it the easy thing to do.

snippet.title: Hacking the Human: Special Edition
snippet.description:
Lorrie Cranor, Director, CyLab Security and Privacy Institute, Carnegie Mellon University

Lujo Bauer, Associate Professor, Electrical & Computer Engineering + Computer Science, Carnegie Mellon University

Apu Kapadia, Associate Professor of Computer Science and Associate Director, Security Program, Indiana University Bloomington

Emilee Rader, Associate Professor and AT&T Scholar, Department of Media and Information, Michigan State University

It has been said that humans are the weakest link and a primary attack vector. Why can’t we solve this age-old problem? Join leading researchers who will present a sampling of key discussions from Monday’s focused seminar, discussing fascinating detail on behaviors and mental models, exploring tools that humans can actually use, and examining emerging threats that surface as humans adopt new technology.

snippet.title: New Rules: Comparing the CA Consumer Privacy Act and EU GDPR—What Every Security Professional Ne...
snippet.description:
John Carlin, Partner, Morrison & Foerster LLP

Snir Ben Shimol, Director, Global Cyber Security, Varonis

Lisa Monaco, Former White House Homeland Security, WestExec Advisors

Current and former high-ranking US and cybersecurity experts discuss the similarities and differences between the EU GDPR and the recently enacted California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, the trends that they signal for the global regulatory landscape, and key considerations for companies seeking to remain ahead of the curve.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the similarities and differences between the GDPR and the California Act.2: Learn practical steps that companies can take to avoid regulatory scrutiny.3: See how to predicting the next “domino” to fall—what regulatory developments are on the horizon?Pre-Requisites:None, general knowledge with less than one year of security experience can attend.

snippet.title: Blockchainification of Cyber-Supply Chain Risk: Hype vs. Hope
snippet.description:
Celia Paulsen, Cybersecurity Researcher, National Institute of Standards and Technology

The buzz around blockchains can be exciting, bewildering and, at times, troubling. Get to the bottom of fact and fiction as an NIST researcher discusses how various blockchain technologies are or could be used, focusing on cyber-supply chain risk management.Learning Objectives:1: Discover what problems in cyber-supply chain risk management blockchains may possibly help address.2: Realize some of the limits of blockchain technology as we know it.3: Develop ideas on how blockchains can or can’t be used for cyber-supply chain risk management.Pre-Requisites:Understanding of supply chain management. Understanding of blockchains, hashchains, smart contracts and distributed ledgers.

snippet.title: DevOps’ Seven Deadly Diseases
snippet.description:
John Willis, Founder, Botchagalupe Technologies

DevOps is officially 10 years old. What have we learned? Although prescriptive practices like lean, agile, SAFE and even DevOps may be necessary for IT acceleration, in most cases they aren’t sufficient for long-term systemic improvement. The key to long-term improvement lies in an understanding where human capital interconnects with technology. Come learn how to uncover the diseases in your organization.

snippet.description:
Bret Hartman, VP and CTO, Security Business Group, Cisco

Jyoti Verma, Technical Leader, Cisco Systems

Picture this. You’re presenting to corporate management when suddenly a message pops up on your screen. Your company is on the brink of a security crisis. This can’t be put on hold. You have to act, now. In a real-time, real-world demo featuring a complex supply chain attack fueled by rapid internal lateral movement, this session will address one of today’s most challenging attacks.Learning Objectives:1: Understand supply-chain malware attacks, and why they are so difficult to detect and stop.2: Learn how analytics of server behavior can be used to detect malicious lateral movement.3: Explore how to contain and remediate advanced attacks with automated enforcement.Pre-Requisites:Knowledge of mechanisms for worm propagation, C&C and lateral movement. Understanding of vulnerabilities exploited by worms, such as SMB. Knowledge of mechanisms for logical server segmentation.

snippet.title: Evolution of AI-Bot Swarming Intelligence with Robots
snippet.description:
Thomas Caldwell, President, CTO, League of AI

A new breed of intelligent robot is emerging to augment enterprise and public environments to ensure cyber-and physical safety for offices, parking lots, smart cities. Robots will leverage AI-bot swarming intelligence to team with virtual AI-bots and humans. Robots are a mobile pod of IoT “sensors and video” to enable mobile roaming telepresence/monitoring and become a member of your security team.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the convergence of AI-bot cybersecurity with robotics.2: Learn how AI is evolving to leverage robots into our security framework.3: Find out about new privacy issues that face us with robot IoT sensors and video.

We work with psychologists, social workers and security practitioners to bring the latest research—what we’ve observed and what we’ve heard from kids and teens, and interpretation of that research. This seminar will arm you with the knowledge and tools to help teach children how to better recognize and resist online challenges.

Jessica Payne, Security Person, Microsoft

David Westgard, Lead Engineer, Cyber Security, Target

MITRE’s freely available ATT&CK knowledge base has increasingly become “the language” for describing adversary behavior. This panel will feature experts from organizations that use ATT&CK in their operations, products and services, discussing what works, what doesn’t and how to achieve measurable improvements in your security posture through the use of adversary knowledge.Learning Objectives:1: Understand how to use the adversary behavior described in ATT&CK in your cyber-defense operations2: Learn how other organizations use ATT&CK and what lessons they’ve learned in the process.3: Be able to quickly apply adversary understanding in your organization.Pre-Requisites:Attendees should have a firm grasp of IT security principles and ideally some basic understanding of what adversary behavior is.

snippet.description:
Catherine Yun, Software Engineer, Chain

In this fast-moving seminar, leading experts will guide attendees through the core elements of bitcoin, distributed systems and smart contracts. Technology and legal practitioners—the front line—look for pockets of crypto opportunity, design for scale and craft for regulatory approval. Participants will see how the dark side of today’s attacks and scams has already changed operational security, the regulatory landscape and legal considerations.

snippet.title: Calling All Fear Mongers: Raising Security Awareness Without Creating CyberHysteria
snippet.description:
Diana Kelley, Cybersecurity Field CTO, Microsoft
Kelley Misata, Founder and CEO, Sightline Security

DDoS, Ransomware, honeypots, breaches, encryption—common words used by information security professionals that can strike fear into the hearts of end users and executives. Too much FUD leads to confusion, bad choices and inaction. This talk will illustrate how language is used in security and how it can be used to spur action or create hysteria and paralysis.

snippet.title: Google on BeyondCorp: Empowering Employees with Security for the Cloud Era
snippet.description:
Jennifer Lin, Director, Security, Google Cloud

Google protects billions of users across the globe with a “security-first” approach. Its “BeyondCorp” framework assumes “Zero Trust”—treating all networks as untrusted—to allow employees to easily work from any device, anywhere without a VPN. Jennifer Lin will discuss considerations for companies adopting a similar approach, BeyondCorp in cloud era, and how the cloud is changing security.

snippet.description:
Gen. Keith Alexander (Ret.), Founder, IronNet
Nadav Zafrir, Co-Founder and CEO, Team8

Both Keith Alexander, former NSA director, and Nadav Zafrir, former commander of Israel’s 8200 Intelligence Unit, will share what they miss about their previous roles in the public sector, their strategy for building security companies in the private sector, what keeps them up at night, and what are they hopeful about in the world of cyber.Learning Objectives:1: Learn about leadership in complex environments.2: Get insight into talent philosophy in the face of talent shortage reality.3: Understand public-private collaboration ideas.

snippet.description:
Window Snyder, Chief Security Officer, Fastly, Inc.

If you deploy more security products, is your organization more secure? Does what you do really work, or is your security spend on products just driving complexity and a false sense of security? Acknowledging there is no one size fits all, Fastly CSO Window Snyder will draw from a diverse set of industries and a unique background to explore models and principles that drive good, risk-based decisions and effective security.

snippet.title: Incorporating Security Practices into Business Processes
snippet.description:
Dr. Tracy Celaya, President and Principal Consultant, Go Consulting International
Ira Winkler, President, Secure Mentem

When people fail from a security perspective, everyone seems to blame the users. Part of the consistent failing is that organizations expect users to do their job, and somehow know what security to implement into the process on their own. This presentation will talk about how to build security behaviors into organizational policies and procedures and therefore practice.Learning Objectives:1: Learn how current awareness programs focus on the wrong things.2: Understand why practices should be embedded into procedures and guidelines.3: Learn how to embed security practices into business processes.

snippet.title: Hacking Healthcare Live: Bits and Bytes Meet Flesh and Blood
snippet.description:
Dr. Christian Dameff, Emergency Physician and Clinical Informatics Fellow, University of California San Diego
Josh Corman, CSO/Founder, PTC / I am The Cavalry 
Dr. Jeff Tully, Anesthesiologist and Pediatrician, University of California Davis

Healthcare cybersecurity is in critical condition. Join Josh Corman and physician hackers Christian Dameff and Jeff Tully as they take you to the frontline of efforts to save lives threatened by ransomware and runaway pacemakers. Watch a live simulated medical device hack as an unsuspecting doctor faces the reality of practice in a brave new world of insecure technologies and vulnerable patients.Learning Objectives:1: Understand how recent attacks and device vulnerabilities threaten patient lives.2: Explore the recommendations of the Healthcare Industry Cybersecurity Task Force.3: Witness a doctor undergo a live clinical simulation of a hacked medical device.

snippet.title: Bug Bounty Buzzword Bingo—Deep Dive under a Jumped Shark
snippet.description:
Katie Moussouris, Founder and CEO, Luta Security, Inc.

Bug bounties are booming, but what are they really accomplishing? The market for bugs and what cash incentives create may make organizations look busy and responsive when it comes to securing their products and services, but are we irrevocably choosing to create perverse global incentives? Has bug bounty virtue signaling won over real security improvement? Join a leading expert to explore tough, timely challenges.

snippet.title: GDPR Essentials: Closing Remarks
snippet.description:
Ilias Chantzos, Symantec
Laura Koetzle, VP, Group Director, Forrester

The GDPR is the first major change in EU privacy regulation in more than two decades and has far-reaching implications for worldwide organizations that touch the data of any EU citizen. In other words…fundamentally every medium- and large-sized company is impacted. With May 25, 2018, as the go-live date, many are struggling to be ready and wondering what the consequences really will be—and how fast the penalties will be imparted. This seminar will cover GDPR in depth, exploring fundamentals such as what’s allowed with customer profiling and how to approach the 72-hour mandated breach notifications and security requirements, providing tangible guidance on pitfalls to avoid. It also ponders if this is just the beginning of what looks to be a groundswell of international privacy and security regulation.

snippet.description:
Stuart McClure, CEO, Cylance
Paul Mehta, Research Scientist Staff, Cylance
Brian Wallace, Lead Security Data Scientist, Cylance

While hacking techniques rarely change or evolve, we have seen numerous hacks in 2017 be extremely successful. This session will look at the year’s headline hacks and offer likely explanations of each, how they worked and what went into each of them to make them so successful. Also participants will discuss and demonstrate the potential for AI techniques to be used against the defenders. Learning Objectives:1: Understand the latest hacks in the media and beyond.2: Observe detailed demonstrations of the hacks.3: Understand the simplicity of the hacks and the countermeasures.

snippet.title: The Rise of Confidential Computing
snippet.description:
Mark Russinovich, Chief Technology Officer, Azure, Microsoft

Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) implement safe data processing environments inside untrusted or compromised computers. They can be used for confidential data processing in public clouds where they protect encrypted code and data from malicious administrators and hackers. This talk will describe architectures, runtimes, compilers and tooling for the creation of confidential computing services using TEEs.

snippet.title: Hacking Exposed: Melting Down Memory
snippet.description:
Dmitri Alperovitch, Co-Founder and CTO, CrowdStrike
George Kurtz, CEO and Co-Founder, CrowdStrike
Elia Zaitsev, Director, Sales Engineers, CrowdStrike

Real-world case studies of advanced modern-day intrusions, including attacks on Linux, IOT and machine-learning evasions. In the typical raw Hacking Exposed style, the session will demonstrate these attacks and provide relevant countermeasures for detection and response. Reprising their appearance again this year are also the must-see Adversary Oscars. Learning Objectives:1: Learn about latest attacks happening today and those that are upcoming.2: Gain insight into new adversary TTPs.3: Gain a better view into countermeasures that can protect you against these threats.

snippet.title: POTUS Is Posting: Social Media and National Security
snippet.description:
James Foster, CEO, ZeroFOXKenneth Geers, Senior Research Scientist, Comodo Group

Russian involvement in the 2016 US election and President Trump’s arsenal of tweets barely hint at the ways in which social media now plays a role in our national security. Nation-state spheres of influence extend far and wide through social media, and their tactics are devious and diverse. This talk will show how social media is a platform for crime, espionage, propaganda, terrorism and war.Learning Objectives:1: Learn about the weaponization of social media by nation-state actors.2: Understand how senior US government officials were compromised via social media.3: Learn how best to protect social media accounts, even from advanced hackers.

snippet.title: Hacking the Vote: How to Get Your Candidate Elected in a Few Simple Steps
snippet.description:
Dr. Hugh Thompson, RSA Conference Program Chair, RSA Conference
Kim Zetter, Freelance Journalist

One of the most critical elements of a democratic society is the integrity of its elections. Ensuring outcome integrity isn’t possible in many parts of the US, where vulnerable election systems provide numerous ways to subvert results. Join journalist and author Kim Zetter, who has written about the security of election systems, to discuss how elections can be hijacked and how we arrived at this state of insecurity.

snippet.title: Cyberwar Game: Behind Closed Doors with the National Security Council
snippet.description:
Dmitri Alperovitch, Co-Founder and CTO, CrowdStrike / Jason Healey, Senior Research Scholar, Columbia University SIPA / John Carlin, Partner and Chair, Global Risk & Crisis Management, Morrison & Foerster LLP / Eric Rosenbach, Co-Director, Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs, Harvard Kennedy School / Joan O'Hara, Acting National Security Advisor, Vice President of the
United States/ Suzanne Spaulding, Senior Adviser, Homeland Security Program and International Security Program, Center for Strategic and International Studies

The country is under a serious cyber attack with national consequences, an attack possibly launched by a hostile nation. The president needs to understand the danger and options to consider. Are we at war? Should the military be in charge? How should the government respond and how can it help the private sector? What are our options? This session will give you an insider’s view of a national-level crisis response.

snippet.title: Security Orchestration and Incident Response
snippet.description:
Bruce Schneier, CTO, IBM Resilient, IBM Security

In this hyper-connected world, organizations are more at risk than ever, having to now focus on new areas that they never asked for. Bruce Schneier will explore how to achieve cyber-resilience in an uncertain world of security attacks. Security teams need an orchestrated approach, integrating both human expertise and big-data/machine-learning capabilities, to achieve resilient security.

snippet.title: GDPR Essentials: GDPR: The Future of International Regulation? Panel
snippet.description:
Moderator: Ilias Chantzos, Senior Director EMEA & APJ Global CIP and Privacy Advisor Government Affairs, Symantec
Panelists:
Rogier Holla, Deputy Head of CERT-EU, CERT-EU
Terrell McSweeny, Commissioner, Federal Trade Commission
Richard Watson

The GDPR is the first major change in EU privacy regulation in more than two decades and has far-reaching implications for worldwide organizations that touch the data of any EU citizen. In other words…fundamentally every medium- and large-sized company is impacted. With May 25, 2018, as the go-live date, many are struggling to be ready and wondering what the consequences really will be—and how fast the penalties will be imparted. This seminar will cover GDPR in depth, exploring fundamentals such as what’s allowed with customer profiling and how to approach the 72-hour mandated breach notifications and security requirements, providing tangible guidance on pitfalls to avoid. It also ponders if this is just the beginning of what looks to be a groundswell of international privacy and security regulation.

snippet.title: Virtual Session: How to Perform Ransomware Analysis
snippet.description:
Stephen Sims, Fellow, SANS Institute

According to an April 2nd ZDNet article, some 96 percent of Singapore companies admitted to experiencing a security breach in the past year, of which 28 percent said ransomware was the most frequently used attack mode.

In this presentation, we will take a look at various types of ransomware and affected 
organizations. Demonstrations will be performed showing a ransomware infection and ways to perform behavioral analysis, as well as code analysis. This demonstration comes from the SANS SEC501: Advanced Security Essentials - Enterprise Defender course.

snippet.description:

Alan Paller, Research Director and Founder, SANS Institute
 
Ed Skoudis, Instructor, SANS
 
Heather Mahalik, Director of Forensics Engineering at ManTech and Mobile Forensics Course Director, SANS Institute

Johannes Ullrich, Dean of Research, SANS Technology Institute

snippet.title: RSA Conference is a Game Changer
snippet.description:
Security professionals travel to RSA Conference every year to learn about the latest advances in the industry. Attendees comment on the value of the conference and what they take back to their organizations -- from networking, to new insights on the latest trends across the cybersecurity industry.

www.rsaconference.com

snippet.description: John Rives opens the Thursday afternoon keynote session RSA Conference 2019 in San Francisco.

snippet.title: Rives: Q&A
snippet.description: John Rives opens the Thursday morning keynote session RSA Conference 2019 in San Francisco.

snippet.title: Rives: The Better Box
snippet.description: John Rives opens the Wednesday afternoon keynote session RSA Conference 2019 in San Francisco.

snippet.title: Cybersecurity Insights into the APJ Region: Vishal Salvi
snippet.description:
Vishal Salvi, CISO & Head of Cybersecurity Practice, Infosys

Industry expert provides commentary on the cybersecurity threat landscape in the APJ region.

https://www.rsaconference.com/videos/cybersecurity-insights-into-the-apj-region-vishal-salvi

snippet.description:
Rachael Falk, Chief Executive Officer, Cyber Security Research Centre

Industry expert provides commentary on the threat landscape in the APJ region

https://www.rsaconference.com/videos/insights-into-the-apj-region-rachael-falk

snippet.title: Virtual Session: Behavior and Misbehavior: The First Ever RSAC SOC Report
snippet.description:
Jessica Bair, Senior Manager, Advanced Threat Solutions, Cisco Security
Neil Wyler, Threat Hunter, RSA
Percy Tucker, Senior Manager, RSA

In this session we share our experience monitoring the RSAC network for stability, security, and stats of interest. We'll talk about what changes we've seen over the years, informative and comical experiences from the trenches, and what we think it means for our industry going forward. So if you'd like to see what a network looks like when its users know security, know its challenges, should know better, and choose to ignore all of that anyway; join us for the RSAC SOC report.

https://www.rsaconference.com/videos/virtual-session-behavior-and-misbehavior-the-first-ever-rsac-soc-report

snippet.title: A Conversation with Tina Fey, Writer, Actress and Producer
snippet.description: Hugh Thompson sits down for an insightful conversation with the multitalented Tina Fey.

snippet.title: A Conversation with Donna Brazile and Mary Matalin
snippet.description: For over three decades, Matalin and Brazile have maintained an intense philosophical commitment to their respective politics, along with a deep, mutual admiration and respect for each other on both the personal and professional levels. Together, the pair provides insightful, inspiring and informative commentary, as well as a welcome reprieve to the often-overwrought modern political landscape.

snippet.title: Securely Deploying Micro Services, Containers and Serverless PaaS Web Apps
snippet.description:
Murray Goldschmidt, Chief Operating Officer, Sense of Security Pty Ltd

From blockchain to distributed ledger to self-sovereign identity, this panel will shed light on technology and governance concepts around blockchain-based identity. This panel will explore the business, legal and technical issues that sit in the messy space between blockchain technology’s promise and its current reality to gain a better understanding of blockchain’s ability to solve real-world needs.Learning Objectives:1: Understand what blockchain-based identity means in practice.2: Explore applied research to break through preconceptions.3: Separate blockchain-based identity promise from reality to reduce uncertainty toward adoption.Pre-Requisites:Identity management basic concepts must be understood. Blockchain and distributed ledger concepts must be understood. Governance, risk and compliance practices for information assurance should be understood.

snippet.title: Engineering Trust and Security in the Cloud Era, Based on Lessons from the Early Internet
snippet.description:
Quentin Hardy, Head of Editorial, Google Cloud
Suzanne Frey, Vice President, Engineering, Google Cloud
Amin Vadhat, Google Fellow and Networking Technical Lead, Google

Trust was implicit in much of the design of the early Internet, creating challenges that still impact us today. Now, in the cloud era, trust isn’t assumed; it’s built (or at least, it should be). Google Fellow Amin Vadhat and Engineering VP Suzanne Frey will discuss the opportunity to build clouds securely from the ground up, incorporating lessons from decades of building secure distributed networks.

snippet.title: In the Wake of an Attack: Thoughts from a Seasoned CISO
snippet.description:
Hugh Thompson, Program Committee Chair, RSA Conference
Bob Lord, Chief Security Officer, DNC

Bob Lord has had a front-row seat, security-wise, at many high-profile organizations. And in the process, he’s learned much. This fireside chat will explore topics including secure by default, the CISO’s role (hint: it’s not cheerleader), the art of communication, and much more. He’ll also share how he’s helping would-be US presidentials to be secure, with sage recommendations that can be useful for all.

snippet.title: (Girl) Scouting for Talent: The Solution in the Next Generation
snippet.description:
Sylvia Acevedo, Chief Executive Officer, Girl Scouts of the USA

Girl Scouts taught this Brownie how to nourish her love of numbers and science, and she became one of the first Latinx to earn an engineering master’s from Stanford, a NASA rocket scientist, an accomplished entrepreneur and a White House education commissioner. Multiply this success times millions, and the positive future impact of diversity looks powerful. Learn how you can help lead the change.

snippet.title: Pushing Left with Tanya Janca
snippet.description:
Dr. Chenxi Wang, Founder, Rain Capital
Tanya Janca, Senior Cloud Developer Advocate, Microsoft

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

Tanya Janca (Shehackspurple) talks to Dr. Chenxi Wang about the importance of pushing left with application security. As a self-taught pen tester and an appsec community leader, Tanya advocates building application security early on in the development lifecycle.

snippet.title: Human Defense: The Next Frontier
snippet.description:
Dr. Chenxi Wang, Founder, Rain Capital
Masha Sedova, Co-founder, Elevate Security

Masha Sedova, co-founder of Elevate Security, talks to Dr. Chenxi Wang about the importance of human behavior change and how that can impact the security posture for the organization. As a behavioral scientist, Masha was responsible for security awareness programs at some of the largest enterprises. At her work with Elevate, Masha puts her learnings in practice to impact organizational and behavioral changes. 

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: Security for All; Not Just Infosec
snippet.description:
Dr. Chenxi Wang, Founder, Rain Capital
Hala Al-Adwan, VP of Technology, Signal Sciences Corp

Signal Sciences' Hala Al-Adwan sat down with Dr. Chenxi Wang to discuss the importance of infusing different talent streams into Cybersecurity. As an engineering leader, Hala came to security without being classically trained as a security engineer. She brings a different viewpoint into her security engineering work and advocates the importance of building security products not for infosec, but for its true end users.  

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: ICS Security & Women in Cyber
snippet.description:
Dr. Chenxi Wang, Founder, Rain Capital
Galina Antova, Co-Founder, Claroty

Co-founder and Chief business development officer of Claroty, Galina Antova, talks to Dr. Chenxi Wang, about the evolution of the ICS security landscape, and the need for attracting more diverse talents into the Cybersecurity market. 

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: A New Employer-Driven Model of Cyber-Workforce Development For Dell
snippet.description:
Simone Petrella, Chief Cyberstrategy Officer, CyberVista
John Scimone, Chief Security Officer, Dell

Today’s cybersecurity training landscape fails employers by producing over-credentialed, yet under-qualified, job candidates. Employers contribute to this problem by lacking clearly defined roles. This session will examine a use case where job role and skills assessments were applied to Dell Inc.’s core cyber-staff resulting in a more effective cybersecurity workforce development and training path.Learning Objectives:1: Learn to identify professional and career pathways for your company’s cybersecurity professionals.2: Glean how this new model can assist in recruiting and other talent strategies.3: Understand a starting point to assess cyber-employees’ skills and competencies.

snippet.title: Democratizing Cloud Security: Journey to Secure the Public Cloud
snippet.description:
Yunchao Liu, Sr Software Engineer, Symantec Corporation
hardeep singh, Senior  Principal Security Engineer, Symantec Corporation

As companies migrate their workloads from on-premise to public cloud platforms there are a number of new challenges in securely operating these environments. This talk will delve into the steps a security architect needs to take to secure the environment and services running in it, with special focus on individual operators role in monitoring, forensics and response.Learning Objectives:1: Gain an understanding of security implications of migrating to the cloud.2: Learn how to decentralize security operations and management.3: Learn how to monitor and react to security incidents across the fleet.Pre-Requisites:Someone who has already migrated or is thinking of migrating their service to the public cloud. They should have a basic understanding of environment and SDLC security.

snippet.title: CISO COMPASS: Cybersecurity Leadership Effectiveness Using the 7-S Framework
snippet.description:
Britta Glade, Director, Content and Curation, RSA Conference
Todd Fitzgerald, Managing Director/CISO, CISO Spotlight, LLC

How do we know if the CISO's security program has accounted for all the components to be effective? This interview introduces an innovative holistic approach to cybersecurity leadership presented in a RSA learning lab and new book entitled CISO COMPASS: Navigating Cybersecurity Leadership Challenges with Insights from Pioneers. The approach innovates by adapting the time-tested McKinsey 7-S Framework for organizational effectiveness to building and sustaining the cybersecurity program to ensure the CISO and cybersecurity leadership has accounted for strategy, structure, systems, skills, style, staff, and shared values. Over 75 top-rated CISOs and cybersecurity leaders contributed to this approach.

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: Threat Modeling in 2019
snippet.description:
Adam Shostack, President, Shostack & Associates

Attacks always get better, so your threat modeling needs to evolve. Learn what's new and important in threat modeling in 2019. Computers that are things are subject to different threats, and systems face new threats from voice cloning and computational propaganda and the growing importance of threats “at the human layer.” Take home actionable ways to ensure your security engineering is up to date.Learning Objectives:1: Use provided models to make sense of a fast changing world.2: Understand how threat modeling fits into the agile world we all live in.3: Learn about new and emergent threats that engineers must start to address.Pre-Requisites:Some exposure to threat modeling will be helpful.

snippet.title: Infecting the Embedded Supply Chain
snippet.description:
Zach Miller, Software Engineer, in8 Solutions

With a surge in the production of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, embedded development tools are becoming common and the software they run is often run in escalated modes. However, some of the embedded development tools on the market contain serious vulnerabilities that put users at risk. This talk will demonstrate this via the exploitation of a common embedded debugger.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the risk introduced by untested development tools.2: Find out the current state of development tools related to embedded development.3: Learn how to best proceed when tools cannot be trusted.Pre-Requisites:General understanding of the concepts behind IoT device development (the design of both hardware and software, familiarity with the concept of a debugger, etc.); general understanding of basic binary exploitation (e.g. stack-overflow, memory corruption, etc.).

snippet.title: Procuring IoT: Purchasing Guidance for Government Officials
snippet.description:
Daniel Kroese, Associate Director, National Risk Management Center Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, Department of Homeland Security

During this session, the Department of Homeland Security will provide a briefing on Internet of Things (IoT) purchasing guidance for government officials. This guidance, co-created by government and the tech industry, will assist those officials involved in the purchasing lifecycle in making risk-informed acquisition decisions and drive demand for secure IoT products and services.Learning Objectives:1: Learn about purchasing guidance for the IoT for government officials.2: Learn how the tech industry helps the government make risk-informed decisions.3: Learn how to make risk-informed acquisitions decisions.

snippet.title: 4G to 5G Evolution: In-Depth Security Perspective
snippet.description:
Anand Prasad, CISO, Rakuten Mobile Networks

In this talk we will present 4G security and issues identified recently followed by in-depth explanation of security enhancements in 5G. We will also cover potential security implications from usage of technologies such as virtualization in mobile networks. Finally we will summarize 5G related security activities expected in near future.Learning Objectives:1: Get a refresher on 4G security, security issues and solutions.2: Learn in-depth regarding 5G security.3: Find out considerations for end-to-end 5G network deployment.Pre-Requisites:Attendees should have some background in mobile networks and security, especially 4G will be beneficial. It is assumed that the attendees have good knowledge of information security.

snippet.title: Use Model to Deconstruct Threats: Detect Intrusion by Statistical Learning
snippet.description:
Tao Zhou, Senior Staff Algorithm Engineer, Alibaba Group

Machine learning has been widely discussed in various areas. However, there is not much discussion about intrusion detection in large scale enterprise networks. This talk will propose a method based on statistical learning. The main idea is to identify unknown threats by modeling behaviors at different attack stages, and some tricks in performing pre-filter data and conducting post-correlate alarms.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the basic information of the security operations in a large Internet company.2: Learn how to use statistical models to identify the unique patterns of post-exploitation attacks.3: Master the necessary skills in performing pre-filter data and conducting post-correlate alarms.Pre-Requisites:Have basic statistical knowledge, familiar with the popular attack techniques.

snippet.title: SOC Automation, Enterprise Blueprinting and Hunting Using Open-Source Tools
snippet.description:
Brian Baskin, Senior Threat Researcher, Carbon Black
John Holowczak, Senior Threat Analyst, Carbon Black

Visibility is the core component in any SOC, from continual monitoring to incident response. While having a simple interface helps to display data, sometimes advanced hunting requires moving beyond the interface and delving into data that’s likely never been documented. This presentation will focus on building a better understanding of environments and hunting for unknown threats that lie within.Learning Objectives:1: Learn about blueprint networks using native operating system tools and osquery.2: Learn how to reduce SOC fatigue by automating regular but critical tasks.3: Learn to hunt using properly collected and organized data.Pre-Requisites:Linux, Windows command line; ELK stack configuration, administration (or equivalent technology, i.e., Splunk); networking basics; networking configuration/engineering; software deployment; programming.

snippet.title: Phantom Menace, Episode I? The Attack That Undressed the Mexican Banks in ’18
snippet.description:
Josu loza, Information Security Advisor, Scotiabank

The presentation will show what happend inside the Mexican banks when the 2018 attacks occurred on the SPEI system (Interbanking Payment System in Mexico) for everybody to understand what happened in order to protect the institutions from a similar scenario, because Mexico ignored the similar attacks that occurred previously around the world.Learning Objectives:1: Understand what is SPEI system and how it works.2: Learn from how the 2018 attacks operated.3: Understand what minimum measures should be adopted in transfer payment systems or any application.

snippet.title: The New Gold Rush: How to Hack Your Own Best Mining Rig
snippet.description:
Roy Katmor, CEO and Co-Founder, enSilo
Udi Yavo, CTO and Co-Founder, enSilo

2018 is the year of malicious crypto-mining attacks, as threat actors turn from doubtful one-off payment disruption attacks to cryptojacking malware attacks, which almost guarantee a payday, with a negligible chance of being discovered. The new cryptocurrency mining attacks are relatively simple and secretly utilizing the processing power of the victim device to mine for the cryptocurrency.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the simplicity of crypto-mining attacks.2: Learn how to build a decentralized platform dedicated to crypto-mining.3: Learn about steps to take to protect digital assets and bank accounts.

snippet.title: Do You Know Your Organization’s Top 10 Security Risks?
snippet.description:
Min-Hwei Liu, Director, Information Security, Aetna

Maintaining focus in an ever-changing threat landscape: Global Security Top 10 Risks. How do we remain focused as a security organization in the ever-changing threat landscape? In this session Aetna will share the steps to the top 10 security risks, the key success factors and metrics, and the steps to kick off this program in your organization.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the importance of a top 10 security risks list to an organization.2: Develop a data driven top 10 security risks list.3: Learn how to leverage the data you are already collecting to generate a top 10 security risks list.Pre-Requisites:Individuals should have a broader understanding of a security organization, its diverse functions, operations and metrics. Enterprise view of a security organization is a plus, or outside-in view of a security function.

snippet.title: A Separate Network for Critical Infrastructure: Is It a Good Idea?
snippet.description:
Robert Knake, Senior Research Scientist, Northeastern University
Sharla Artz, Vice President, Government Affairs, Policy & Cybersecurity, UTC
Peter Fuhr, Distinguished Scientist, Director, Grid Security, Tech Director UAS Research Center, Oak Ridge National Laboratory
Samara Moore, Director, Cybersecurity, Exelon

In August of 2018, the National Infrastructure Advisory Council recommended exploring the creation of separate networks for critical infrastructure to move essential operations off the Internet. Is it practical? Would the cost exceed the value? Drawing on a yearlong study, three industry professionals from industry, government and academia will discuss the merits of the concept.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the feasibility of creating a separate network for critical infrastructure2: Identify the tradeoffs between pursuing segmentation and investing in other defenses.3: Explore government’s role in protecting critical infrastructure.Pre-Requisites:Basic familiarity with critical infrastructure, governments role in protecting it and an understanding of network security.

snippet.title: Five Secrets to Attract and Retain Top Tech Talent in Your Future Workplace
snippet.description:
Laurie Battaglia, CEO & Workplace Strategist, Aligned at Work

High demand and rising compensation have put the cybersecurity industry under increasing pressure to attract and retain high performers. Turnover can cost you money and high levels of risk. How can you prevent top talent from jumping to your competition? Leaders play a key role in keeping people satisfied and engaged. Learn proven ways to keep your professional team thriving at work.Learning Objectives:1: Learn five key areas where people focus when deciding to stay or go at their current employer.2: Know current statistics and stories that determine what people want in their workplace and career.3: Walk away with practical steps you the leader can take to connect and engage with team members.Pre-Requisites:This session will be impactful for any level of leader of people. Those currently leading people will benefit most.

snippet.title: Key Management and Protection: Evaluation of Hardware, Tokens, TEEs and MPC
snippet.description:
Nigel Smart, Professor, KU Leuven

One of the pillars of cryptography implementation is the secure storage and management of the keys used to perform cryptographic operations. This session will review the varied cryptographic key management and protection technologies available today, including new emerging solutions designed to enhance security and usability in a dispersed, connected digital IT environment.Learning Objectives:1: Review the varied cryptographic key management and protection technologies available today.2: Discuss key criteria for evaluating the security strength of key protection mechanisms.3: Provide a security and usability assessment of key protection models.Pre-Requisites:Basic knowledge of cryptography/key management.

snippet.title: Designing Effective Security UX: If It’s Not Usable, It’s Not Secure
snippet.description:
Ranjeet Kumar Tayi, User Experience Design Leader (Data Security Group), Informatica

User experience (UX) design plays a critical role in empowering people to protect their privacy by controlling their data. A human-centered design thinking approach to security can bring together what’s desirable to people, possibly with technology and regulatory context. If the security system is complex and not usable the user will never know the risk and today security needs the power of UX.Learning Objectives:1: Understand security challenges and complexity.2: Learn about user-centric and data-centric approaches to security.3: Learn how good UX can make security simplified and easy to use.Pre-Requisites:Basic knowledge of security products and be part of a product development organization.

snippet.title: Wireless Offense and Defense, Explained and Demonstrated!
snippet.description:
Rick Farina, Senior Product Manager, WLAN Software Security, Aruba
Rick Mellendick, Chief Security Officer, Process Improvement Achievers LLC

This session will discuss the use of radio frequency, often overlooked for network enumeration and attack. The techniques to be discuss are used to identify authorized and unauthorized signals in an organization. Without understanding the offensive attacks an organization can’t perform effective defense. The talk will explain and demonstrate how to enumerate and gain access to resources through RF signals.Learning Objectives:1: Understand that wireless doesn’t just mean WiFi.2: Understand that the Bluetooth protocol can allow for direct attacks against phones, PCs and other devices.3: Learn that other RF attacks are very difficult to detect, and gain an understanding of what they look like.Pre-Requisites:The biggest prerequisite for our talk is an open mind and the ability to understand risk, and after the talk to better assess risk on your environment.

snippet.title: Tales of a Teenage Security Supergirl
snippet.description:
Kyla Guru, Founder/Chief Executive Officer, Bits N’ Bytes Cybersecurity Education

In her keynote at RSA Conference, Kyla Guru will share her story of being a social entrepreneur in the cybersecurity industry, the challenges she has faced and what she believes should be the greater mission of all cybersecurity initiatives. Guru will use her unique perspective of going through the education system to talk about what she sees for the future of the industry, and, of course, how we can make radical change to our current state of cyber-insecurity.

snippet.title: Three Things the Security Industry Isn’t Talking About (but Should Be)
snippet.description:
Pat Gelsinger, Chief Executive Officer, VMware
Shannon Lietz, Director, Intuit

The biggest threat to security today is our hyper-focus on threats. Most innovations have centered on finding and dealing with attacks. By contrast, very little has been done in how we shrink the attack surface. That domain needs to be a topic to achieve big gains in security. Join VMware CEO Pat Gelsinger and Intuit DevSecOps Leader Shannon Lietz, as they unveil the three things the industry needs to talk about to reduce the attack surface and shift the advantage to the defenders.

snippet.title: Connecting the Dots for the Future
snippet.description:
Diane Brady, Award-Winning Writer, Author, Consultant
John T. Chambers, Founder and Chief Executive Officer, JC2 Ventures, Former Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Cisco

Diane Brady and John Chambers will discuss the process of how they co-wrote their new book, Connecting the Dots: Lessons for Leadership in a Startup World. They will also cover Chambers’s leadership roles serving as CEO and executive chairman at Cisco up through his current position as founder and CEO of JC2 Ventures, where he works with startups from all around the world. Chambers will speak to the importance of diverse teams in the development of a successful business and what he looks for when investing in startups.

snippet.title: Government Needs You
snippet.description:
Travis Moore, TechCongress
Hashim Mteuzi, Senior Manager, Network Talent Initiative, Code for America
Gigi Sohn, Distinguished Fellow, Georgetown Law Institute for Technology Law & Policy
Ashkan Soltani, Independent Consultant, Soltani LLC

Government needs technologists at all levels. We’re needed on legislative staffs and at regulatory agencies in order to make effective tech policy, but we’re also needed elsewhere to implement policy more broadly. We’re needed to advise courts, testify at hearings, and serve on advisory committees. At this session, you’ll hear how public-interest technologists are having an impact on government.

snippet.title: Working in Civil Society
snippet.description:
Sarah Aoun, Digital Security Technologist, Independent
Peter Eckersley, Partnership on AI
Harlo Holmes, Director of Newsroom Digital Security, Freedom of the Press Foundation
John Scott-Railton, Senior Researcher, Citizen Lab

Bringing a technological perspective into civil society can transform how organizations do their work. This session examines how this transformation can happen from a variety of perspectives: exposing government surveillance, protecting journalists world-wide, preserving a free and open Internet, bringing a security focus to artificial intelligence research, protecting NGO networks, and more.

snippet.title: The Future of Public-Interest Tech
snippet.description:
Jenny Toomey, Director, Internet Freedom, Ford Foundation
Bruce Schneier, Fellow and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School
Ben Wizner, ACLU

Creating an environment where public-interest tech can flourish will require a robust pipeline: more people wanting to go into this field, more places for them to go, and a better market that matches supply with demand. This closing session will sum up the day and discuss future directions for growing the field, funding trajectories, outstanding needs and gaps, and how you can get involved.

snippet.title: Changing Academia
snippet.description:
Deirdre Mulligan, Associate Professor, UC Berkeley Center for Long Term Cybersecurity
Latanya Sweeney, Harvard
Danny Weitzner, MIT CSAIL

Higher education needs to incorporate a public-interest perspective in technology departments and a tech perspective in public-policy departments. This could look like ethics courses for CS majors, programming for law students, or joint degrees that combine tech and social science. This session will look at some efforts to build these sorts of interdisciplinary classes, programs and institutes.

snippet.title: How Long to Boom: Understanding and Measuring ICS Hacker Maturity
snippet.description:
Sergio Caltagirone, Director, Threat Intelligence, Dragos

The industrial control system threat is growing quickly. But ICS hackers do not start by disrupting electric grids. Instead, they mature predictably leading them from things that go bad, to things that go boom. Using ICS threat intelligence we’ve developed an ICS hacker maturity model enabling us to determine how much risk a threat poses and predict how long until they reach maximum risk.Learning Objectives:1: Understand and differentiate between risks in industrial control and critical infrastructure threats.2: Learn the different levels of threat maturity and how to map them to environment risk.3: Know how to estimate how long a threat will take to reach future maturity levels.

snippet.title: Public-Interest Tech: Bruce Schneier Interviews John "JSR" Scott-Railton
snippet.description:
Bruce Schneier, Fellow and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School
John "JSR" Scott-Railton, Senior Researcher, Citizen Lab

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: The Future of Data Protection: Adapting to the Privacy Imperative
snippet.description:
J. Trevor Hughes, President & CEO, IAPP
Kalinda Raina, Senior Director, Head of Global Privacy, LinkedIn
Ruby Zefo, Chief Privacy Officer, Uber

Organizations are grappling with complex ethical and competitive imperatives associated with getting privacy right, impacted by competing global regulations and high-profile incidents that have made consumers reconsider how much data they want to share with businesses. This session will explore the future of privacy, in which personal data has become a currency, exploring who owns the data and who controls its flow and use.Learning Objectives:1: Explore and understand the responses to privacy from major organizations.2: Learn the management processes used to mitigate privacy risks.3: Learn what future privacy issues are likely to drive organizational behavior in the coming months.

snippet.title: Public-Interest Tech: Bruce Schneier Interviews Travis Moore
snippet.description:
Bruce Schneier, Fellow and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School
Travis Moore, Founder and Director, TechCongress

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: Public-Interest Tech: Bruce Schneier Interviews Sarah Aoun
snippet.description:
Bruce Schneier, Fellow and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School
Sarah Aoun, Digital Security Technologist

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: Public-Interest Tech: Bruce Schneier Interviews Matt Mitchell
snippet.description:
Bruce Schneier, Fellow and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School
Matt Mitchell, Director of Digital Safety & Privacy, Tactical Tech

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: Public-Interest Tech: Bruce Schneier Interviews Jon Callas
snippet.description:
Bruce Schneier, Fellow and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School
Jon Callas, Senior Technology Fellow, ACLU

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: Public-Interest Tech: Bruce Schneier Interviews Jenny Toomey
snippet.description:
Bruce Schneier, Fellow and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School
Jenny Toomey, International Director for Technology and Society, Ford Foundation

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: Public-Interest Tech: Bruce Schneier Interviews Dr. Kelley Misata
snippet.description:
Bruce Schneier, Fellow and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School
Dr. Kelley Misata, Founder and CEO, Sightline Security

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: Public-Interest Tech: Bruce Schneier Interviews Dierdre Mulligan
snippet.description:
Bruce Schneier, Fellow and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School
Dierdre Mulligan, Faculty Director, Berkeley Center for Law and Technology, University of California Berkeley

Recorded at Broadcast Alley, RSA Conference 2019

snippet.title: Stress, Burnout and You: Fireside Chat with Dr. Christina Maslach
snippet.description:
Josh Corman, CSO, PTC
Christina Maslach, Professor of Psychology, Emerita, University of California, Berkeley

More attention is focused ensuring a nearly infallible security posture, and little on security teams. Become hyperaware of the impact of stress, and the fallout that leads to profound industry issues like burnout and toxicity. Renowned expert Dr. Maslach provides an understanding of stress in other industries and applies it to cyber. And gives guidance on championing wellness in your organization.

snippet.title: Hacking Exposed: Hacking Macs
snippet.description:
Dmitri Alperovitch, Co-Founder & CTO, CrowdStrike
George Kurtz, CEO, CrowdStrike

Real-world case studies of advanced intrusions on MacOS systems, with detailed breakdown of TTPs and artifacts. In the typical raw Hacking Exposed style, the session will demonstrate these attacks and provide relevant countermeasures for detection and response. Reprising their appearance again this year are also the must-see Adversary Oscars.Learning Objectives:1: Learn what the different attacker TTPs are on MacOS systems.2: Understand how the macOS process visualization trees can be used for forensics.3: Understand how both static and behavioral indicators are relevant to intrusions.Pre-Requisites:Understand basic hacking tools and techniques.

snippet.title: Public-Interest Tech in Silicon Valley
snippet.description:
Mitchell Baker, Chairwoman, Mozilla Corporation
Cindy Cohn, Executive Director, Electronic Frontier Foundation
Shannon Vallor, AI Ethicist and Visiting Researcher, Google

Silicon Valley is at the epicenter of the ongoing technological transformation of human society. Here, code can dictate large-scale outcomes across privacy, security, and human health and wellbeing. What does it mean to do public interest tech work in Silicon Valley from both corporate and nonprofit perspectives? How can technologists become forces for the public interest within their own organizations?

snippet.title: How Public-Interest Technologists are Changing the World
snippet.description:
J. Bob Alotta, Astraea Foundation
Matt Mitchell, Tactical Tech
Bruce Schneier, Fellow and Lecturer, Harvard Kennedy School

Public-interest technologists apply technological expertise to further the public interest: by working on tech policy, working on a tech project with a public benefit, or as a traditional technologist for an organization with a public benefit. These people are already changing the world. In this session, we’ll talk about who and how – and what needs to be done in the future.

snippet.title: Investigating IoT Crime: The Value of IoT Crime Classification
snippet.description:
Evan Perez, Senior Justice Correspondent, CNN
Anthony J. Ferrante, Global Head of Cybersecurity and Senior Managing Director, FTI Consulting, Inc.
Jordan Kelly, Senior Managing Director, FTI Consulting

The Internet of Things (IoT) has increased quality of life for many. However, it has also enticed cybercriminals to commit fraud in new and novel ways. This presentation will focus on strategies implemented in the early stages of the investigation of IoT crimes. The first approach will be to consider the classification of the crime, the methods of collecting evidence and all relevant laws and regulations.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the evolving vulnerabilities posed from the advancement of IoT.2: Learn how to creatively use data from IoT devices in cybersecurity investigations.3: Prepare and respond to protect and fight against vulnerabilities posed from IoT.Pre-Requisites:Three to five years of security experience.

snippet.title: The Five Most Dangerous New Attack Techniques and How to Counter Them
snippet.description:
Alan Paller, Research Director and Founder, SANS Institute
Heather Mahalik, Director of Forensics Engineering  at ManTech  and Mobile Forensics Course Director, SANS Institute
Ed Skoudis, Instructor, SANS Institute
Johannes Ullrich, Dean of Research, SANS Technology Institute

Which are the most dangerous new attack techniques? How do they work? How can you stop them? What’s coming next and how can you prepare? This fast-paced briefing features the three people best positioned to provide answers and best able to communicate them: the nation’s top expert/teacher on mobile forensics, the director of the Internet Storm Center and the top hacker exploits expert/teacher in the US.  They also answer audience questions.

snippet.title: Change Your Approach to Get It Right
snippet.description:
Caleb Barlow, Vice President, IBM Security, X-Force Threat Intelligence
Mary O’Brien, General Manager, IBM Security

What if our approach to cybersecurity isn’t going to make us better…that despite all the advanced security technologies, we don’t have the right culture and approaches to combat this complex, chaotic problem. Mary O’Brien, general manager, and Caleb Barlow, VP of threat intelligence, both from IBM Security, share insights they have learned from running a large security business and a fully immersive cyber-range, that challenges our conventional thinking and offers new ways to empower our entire organizations and bring the industry together so we can become exponentially better.

snippet.title: Securing Intel PC for FIDO Support: Industry Standard to Remove Passwords
snippet.description:
Nitin Sarangdhar, Senior Principal Engineer, Intel Corporation

FIDO-enabled platforms replace password match on the relying party website with a passwordless experience of biometric authentication on a user device. This session will cover how PCs can be vulnerable to attacks on simple host OS-based FIDO authenticators and capabilities available in Intel HW to create a trusted execution environment–based FIDO Authenticator to address such vulnerabilities.Learning Objectives:1: Understand how FIDO is addressing the industry challenge of eliminating passwords.2: Learn pros and cons of host OS vs. trusted execution environment-based FIDO Authenticators.3: Find out how PCs and Intel are addressing this challenge along with its ecosystem partners.Pre-Requisites:Understanding the concept of trusted execution environments and vulnerability exposure in PC environments.

snippet.title: Kubernetes Runtime Security: What Happens if a Container Goes Bad?
snippet.description:
Jen Tong, Security Advocate, Google

Kubernetes security discussions often focus on safe configurations and deployments. This talk will focus on a different aspect: runtime security. Runtime security mitigates damage done by a compromise. It includes an overview of runtime security, how it changes as you move to containers and Kubernetes, and a demo of features and tools that help you respond to these risks.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the security differences between VMs and containers.2: Grasp the importance of container specific run-time security.3: Gather a list of options for addressing this need, including free open source options.Pre-Requisites:Basic understanding of containers.

snippet.title: Future Forests: Realistic Strategies for AD Security & “Red Forest” Architecture
snippet.description:
Katie Knowles, Security Consultant, MWR InfoSecurity

Microsoft’s Red Forest mitigates devastating Active Directory (AD) attacks like WannaCry. But the process isn’t easy...how can an enterprise domain move to this architecture? Answers on this journey integrate lessons learned from both attackers and defenders. From exact benefits to common weaknesses, this session will cover a clear strategy to implement Red Forest. Only you can prevent AD forest fires!Learning Objectives:1: Understand how Microsoft’s Red Forest architecture mitigates modern AD attacks.2: Create a plan to realistically implement the objectives of Red Forest within an organization.3: Identify common challenges and weaknesses in implementing these steps.Pre-Requisites:A base understanding of Active Directory. A passing knowledge of the current attacks used on Active Directory is beneficial, but not required.

snippet.title: Election Hacking is No Longer Theoretical: Russians are Pwning Our Votes
snippet.description:
James Foster, CEO, ZeroFOX
Avi Rubin, Professor, Johns Hopkins University

Facebook is not to blame for nearly every country’s lack of guidance, regulation or legal precedent on how to secure their sovereignty from election meddling and hacking. This talk will show how nation-state adversaries are targeting election systems, election system supply chains, regional populations, elected officials and the democratic state.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the history of election hacking and how the times are changing.2: Learn the multiple methods in which elections are being targeted and compromised.3: Understand what a protection framework must include to protect democratic elections.Pre-Requisites:An cursory knowledge of red teaming tactics and the complex nature of election systems would be useful.

snippet.title: Cryptojacking Meets IoT
snippet.description:
Sherri Davidoff, CEO, LMG Security
Matt Durrin, Security Consultant, LMG Security

Hackers have a new way to profit off your security cameras, smart lighting, and even your fancy new coffeepot: cryptojacking. This talk will show you screenshots and forensic artifacts from a real cryptojacking attack. Then, watch an infection of a popular security camera with the Mirai botnet, and use it to mine Monero coins. How can you detect and prevent IoT cryptojacking attacks? Find out!Learning Objectives:1: Watch a cryptojacking attack in action!2: Understand how cryptojacking can impact your physical devices.3: Learn strategies for detecting and preventing IoT cryptojackjing attacks.

snippet.title: Business Email Compromise: Operation Wire Wire and New Attack Vectors
snippet.description:
Anne Connell, Cybersecurity Engineer, CMU – SEI – CERT

The FBI (IC3) received 600,000 cybercrime and fraud complaints in 2017 with reported losses in excess of  $12.5 Billion, and BEC was the number one cause of loss. This talk will analyze “Operation Wire Wire” to detail how targets are identified, methods for obtaining information, the new attack vectors—beyond impersonation, invoices and social engineering—and offers new defense techniques.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the new attack vectors BEC scammers use.2: Know how the BEC targets are identified and the methods to obtain information.3: Learn how to defend against the new attack vectors of BEC and stop the wire transfer.Pre-Requisites:Understanding basic attack vectors and techniques, leveraging social engineering tactics to identify targets, and a grasp of the cost that BEC has to an organization.

snippet.title: How CTI Can Play a Key Role to Get Security on Board
snippet.description:
Jean-Yves Riverin, Cyber Threat Intelligence Senior Advisor, Desjardins

Jean-Yves Riverin is a cyberthreat intelligence senior advisor who works for the Desjardins group, the leading financial cooperative in Canada with total assets of 275 billion and over 45,000 employees. Riverin will go through the creation of Desjardins’ SOC eight years ago and all the ensuing steps accomplished over the years to improve its maturity and get the ongoing support of upper management.Learning Objectives:1: Describe the main steps to get a spot in the board’s multiple priorities to talk about security.2: Reach the level where security is no longer a show stopper, but a must-have in projects.3: Translate security risks into business risks... Security can be sexy.

snippet.title: Threat Hunting Using 16th-Century Math and Sesame Street
snippet.description:
Vernon Habersetzer, Sr. Enterprise Technical Expert, Walmart

With attacks always changing, threat hunting in a massive environment can be an overwhelming endeavor! This session will show how to hunt for threats in a way that transcends attack specifics, using the numbers to your advantage to uncover unique and unusual machine behaviors. This practical method that can be leveraged in almost any environment, and can be applied to network and endpoint data.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the challenge of threat hunting in a massive environment.2: Learn about the need for a hunting method that transcends attack specifics.3: Learn how to use the numbers to your advantage to hunt for threats.Pre-Requisites:Attendees should have a basic understanding of networking and security threats. Database experience would be beneficial, but not required. The session will be most relevant and beneficial to those in a threat hunting or incident response role.

snippet.title: What Makes a Good KRI? Using FAIR to Discover Meaningful Metrics
snippet.description:
Steve Reznik, Director, Operational Risk Management, ADP

In addition to risk assessments, many best practice guidelines specify continuous monitoring and metrics to drive effective governance. However, companies waste valuable resources and create noise by reporting on bad metrics. This session will review characteristics of a “good” metric and introduce a method to identify KRIs using sensitivity analysis.Learning Objectives:1: Learn a FAIR-based approach to identify more meaningful metrics.2: Understand the characteristics of a key risk indicator.3: See a case study of risk quantification sensitivity analysis.Pre-Requisites:Some experience with risk assessment and/or setting, tracking or reporting metrics.

snippet.title: What Sennacherib Taught Me About Security: How to Translate Cyber-speak
snippet.description:
Mary Ann Davidson, Chief Security Officer, Oracle Corporation

What do cuneiform and cybersecurity have in common? Both are “C” words and both are arcane languages. Cuneiform is the past; cybersecurity is the future as everything is connected. How do we de-geek our speak for the many who need to know? Learn how to use the communication weapons in your armory you didn’t know you had: stories, analogies, humor, sarcasm, economics, history, biology and more.Learning Objectives:1: Learn how humor, economics, military history and more can shed light on cybersecurity.2: Develop your own library of analogies to convey security issues and possible remedies.3: Discover how to explain a complex security issue to a nonexpert in less than 10 minutes.

snippet.title: Mushrooming Economic Inequality Menaces Security: Here’s How to Fix It
snippet.description:
Laura Koetzle, Vice President, Group Director, Forrester Research

Today, consumer data monopolies, automation and economic concentration combine to fuel economic inequality. Why is this a security and privacy problem?  Unchecked inequality means that top talent in our fields either: a) works for the top 1 percent of firms, or b) embraces the dark side. In this session, Forrester security research leader Laura Koetzle shows how we got here and five ways we can fix it.Learning Objectives:1: See why we're here: concentration fuels inequality, and we’re not using taxes and regulation to help.2: Find out why rising inequality particularly impacts information security and privacy.3: Learn five ways to help fix it, including via industry consortia and educating officials.

snippet.title: The Detrimental Nature of Proofs of Work, and Risks to Cryptocurrencies
snippet.description:
Guy Stewart, Co-founder and CTO, Egni Inc.

This session will analyze what cryptocurrency design aspects threaten to destabilize the marketplace and expose systems to hostile take-overs, and will describe why the reliance on PoW contributes heavily to a lack of robustness and how PoS based solutions can help strengthen systems. With greater robustness and an associated growth of the marketplace comes benefits, such as high-speed transaction support.Learning Objectives:1: Understand stability risks of cryptocurrencies.2: Learn to analyze robustness risks, using proofs of work as case study.3: Analyze the potential benefits of a shift towards proof of space.Pre-Requisites:General familiarity with how cryptocurrencies are constructed and work.

snippet.title: Cheaper by the Dozen: Application Security on a Limited Budget
snippet.description:
Christopher Romeo, CEO, Security Journey

Everyone wants to improve application security, but what if your company does not have one million dollars to spend? Learn which open source projects fit together to solve application security problems and receive advice on how to get started. Explore OWASP projects, including purpose, usage, risk rating and human resources. Reap enormous benefits and change organizational application security forever.Learning Objectives:1: Identify which open source projects fit together to solve your application security problems.2: Locate the right projects to match organizational application security needs.3: Recognize per project advice on how to use application security improvements for great success.Pre-Requisites:Foundational understanding of AppSec.

snippet.title: Container Security at the Speed of CI/CD
snippet.description:
Tim Chase, Director of Security, HealthStream

Containers are everywhere! But how do you deal with the security challenges of using containers? You have to secure the application, the code, the web server and the host itself. And how do you do this at the speed of DevOps? This session will talk about containers, why they are complex to secure and then walk away with an easy-to-implement container security solution.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the complexity of containers.2: Understand the security challenges with containers.3: Learn how to build an automated container security solution.Pre-Requisites:General understanding of containers.

snippet.title: RF Exploitation: IoT and OT Hacking with Software-Defined Radio
snippet.description:
Harshit Agrawal, Security Researcher, MIT Academy of Engineering, SPPU

Himanshu Mehta, Team Lead (Senior Threat Analysis Engineer), Symantec

Recent years have seen a flood of novel wireless exploits, from vulnerable medical devices to hacked OT devices, with exploitation moving beyond 802.11 and into more obscure standard and proprietary protocols. While other non-WiFi RF protocols remain a mystery to many security practitioners, exploiting them is easier than one might think. SDR is changing the game for both offense and defense.Learning Objectives:1: Become familiar with common security concerns and attack surfaces in a wireless communication system.2: Understand the ease and prevalence of wireless exploitation, with sophisticated examples.3: Learn to view IoT devices, security and privacy collectively.

snippet.title: Software Bill of Materials: Progress toward Transparency of Third-Party Code
snippet.description:
Allan Friedman, Director of Cybersecurity, NTIA / US Department of Commerce

A “software bill of materials” that lists third-party components can help both SW vendors and enterprise customers. In 2018, NTIA launched an open process of experts from many sectors to identify challenges in assembling, sharing and using this data. This talk will present progress and highlight successes in harmonizing standards as well as sector-specific use cases, including healthcare.Learning Objectives:1: Understand the value of software bill of materials, as well as challenges.2: Understand the progress of this government-convened process.3: Understand how to give input and participate across a range of sectors.

snippet.title: Manufacturers Approach towards Cybersecurity Threats Targeting Healthcare
snippet.description:
Jonathan Bagnall, Sr. Security Manager,  Product Security & Services Office (PSSO), Royal Philips
Phil Englert, Global Leader for Healthcare Technology, Deloitte
Roberta Hansen, Director, Product Cybersecurity, Abbott
Michael McNeil, Global Product Security & Services Officer, Royal Philips
