snippet.title: RSA Conference 2011 Keynote - Driving Security Down the Stack - George Kurtz
snippet.description:
Speaker: George Kurtz, Chief Technology Officer and Executive Vice President, McAfee, Inc.

The explosive growth of Internet and IP-enabled devices is reshaping communication, collaboration and commerce opportunities for individuals and organizations around the world. At the same time, miscreants are abusing the Internet's open and any-to-any communication architecture for malicious purposes, leaving many users at risk and the future of a secure Internet as an aspiration rather than a reality. The current cybersecurity model is reactive, disconnected and unable to keep pace with the seismic explosion in malware. Providing protection to a heterogeneous world of connected devices requires a new approach to security. McAfee CTO George Kurtz will show that incremental improvements can't bridge the opportunity gap and explain the required paradigm shift of driving security down the stack.

snippet.description:
Web-based malware silently waits between the user's machine and the malware distribution servers and is mostly used to mediate local machine infection. The number of infected websites is growing each year and the popular mantra of "browsing known websites is safe - threats come from pornographic and warez sites", is no longer true.

snippet.title: RSA Conference 2011 Keynote - The Future of Security in the Era of Cloud Computing -- On Twitter
snippet.description:
SPEAKERS:  Philippe Courtot, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Qualys, Inc.; Paul Saffo, Technology Futurist and Consulting Associate Professor Stanford University; Dave Cullinane Chief Information Security Officer, eBay Inc.

As cloud computing adoption accelerates, the security model is shifting from the network layer to focus more on the data and where it resides within global datacenters. This major shift in computing is forcing enterprises, vendors and security professionals to rethink their security model in order to make the data secure yet accessible everywhere. Technology futurist Paul Saffo will host a lively discussion on this topic with two cloud computing pioneers, Philippe Courtot of Qualys and Dave Cullinane of eBay/CSA, taking live questions from the audience via Twitter (#RSACcloud).

snippet.description:
As the threat facing our military networks and valued information evolves, the Department of Defense (DoD) is adapting its defenses in cyberspace and improving cybersecurity while safeguarding civil liberties and privacy. General Alexander will discuss key DoD cyber initiatives over the past year, including the establishment of U.S. Cyber Command, explain DOD's approach to active cyber defense, and introduce the concept of a Secure Zone.

snippet.description:
Tom Gillis, Vice President & General Manager, Security Technology Business Unit, Cisco

Enterprise security is built for a network that is quickly disappearing. With the disappearance of enterprise perimeters, the rise of mobile devices, the cloud, and always-connected workers changing the game, the need for a new security model is paramount. Tom Gillis discusses how a new fabric of trust over the global network will make security transparent for every user and safer for every administrator.

snippet.description:
Cloud computing's growth in popularity has been due to the lure of inexpensive and redundant storage, computation and services. This presentation provides an analysis of what happens when things go wrong, by looking at real-world cloud computing investigations and digital forensics. It proposes a set of technical and legal recommendations to reduce risk.

snippet.description:
Cloud storage of websites attracts a new kind of malware: well-behaved hooks that link to malware stored elsewhere. 
Conventional malware detection techniques don't find these. Learn how to force the adversary to hide in plain sight, to scan quickly and efficiently, and to write malware scanners your adversary can't buy off a shelf. Working knowledge of web application security helpful.

snippet.description:

snippet.description:

Starting with Saltzer and Schroeder, this talk explores the origins, evolution, and use of these activities and others. Throughout, we share deployment experience and relate the discussion to living standards, such as Microsoft SDL, OWASP Top 10, and PCI DSS.

snippet.description:

This session will examine how to analyze and reduce attack surface while still allowing developers to add new exciting and delighting features that users love. snippet.description:

snippet.description:
An applications transformation has begun, creating both challenges and opportunities: with users (consumers) demanding everything as a service, anywhere, how can enterprises secure critical corporate infrastructure assets and information? Building security into applications, assessing risk-- even before coding begins, and applying quality and operational management using ITIL concepts to the practice of security are key.

snippet.description:
Adopting the mythical "hacker's toolbox", we have become experts in many awkwardly specialized security disciplines, welding together an ever-growing collection of esoteric technology and spending a lot of money on security products; yet we still get hacked. This talk will explore ways to tie together today's silos of security data into a holistic view of system security.

snippet.description:

Director and Senior Fellow, Technology and Public Policy Program, Center for Strategic and International Studies

PANELISTS: Michael Chertoff , Former U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security; Mike McConnell, Executive Vice President, Booz Allen Hamilton; Bruce Schneier, Chief Technology Security Officer, BT

In this keynote panel, explore the complex and evolving issues tied to cybersecurity and conflict in cyberspace in the 21st Century from leading experts in the field. Moderated by Dr. James Lewis of the Center for Strategic and International Studies, this session will include discussion on thresholds for cyberwar, the often confusing terminology used for various types of cyber conflict, and what needs to be done in the international context to secure cyberspace while also deterring the possible escalation of various kinds of cyber attacks and conflict.

IT is being pulled in conflicting directions as users demand more choice over their devices and applications while management demands more security and control. The mission of IT is also growing much faster than resources. Symantec President and CEO Enrique Salem will give his perspective on resolving these conflicts through a new approach to IT architecture focused around people and information.

snippet.description:
Presented by Scott Charney, Corporate Vice President Trustworthy Computing, Microsoft

As people move more data and information into the Cloud, the need for secure, private and reliable services is growing from a technology concern within the industry, to a societal concern for citizens around the world. Microsoft Corporate Vice President for Trustworthy Computing, Scott Charney, will discuss how the growing alignment of social, economic, political and technical forces are creating a situation where the industry has the potential to make substantial security progress.

snippet.title: RSA Conference Webcast: State of SSL on the Internet - Ivan Ristić
snippet.description: The SSL (TLS) protocol is the security backbone of the Internet, but surprisingly little is known about how it is deployed in real life. This session will present the results of the first publicly available survey aimed at assessing the state of SSL on the Internet. It will also provide documentation and free tools to test and improve the configuration of SSL servers. Sponsored by Qualys, Global Platinum Sponsor. View more webcasts at http://www.rsaconference.com

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- The Seven Most Dangerous New Attack Techniques, and What's Coming Next
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Nation-states and organized crime groups are rapidly increasing the sophistication, virulence, and effectiveness of attack tools and techniques. In this session, three people in unique positions to see the newest attack patterns will share what they believe are the seven most dangerous new attack vectors and how they think attack tools and patterns will evolve over the coming year.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Cloudiquantanomidatumcon: The Infra/Info-Centric Debate in the Cloud
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

The advent of cloud computing introduces a paradigm shift in our data centers more akin to the transition from the Standard Model of physics to quantum mechanics or string theory than the boring "fortress/airport" metaphors. Come debate infrastructure vs. information-centric security as we deconstruct cloud computing showing practical security while building a foundation for the next 7-10 years.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Top Website Vulnerabilities: Trends, Business Effects and How to Fight Them
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Jeremiah Grossman will draw from the most recent WhiteHat Security Website Security Statistics Report -- a trove of information from over 1,600 websites -- to introduce the most prevalent vulnerabilities putting data at risk. This presentation will place special emphasis on separating historical trends from the current state of web application security.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Hacking Exposed - Exploiting the Cloud and Virtual Machines
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

In this enlightening session, industry heavyweights and "Hacking Exposed" co-authors, George Kurtz and Stuart McClure, will show you contemporary ways that hackers are exploiting the cloud and virtual machines to harm your business, along with common sense techniques you can employ to stop them in their tracks.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011--From White Hat to Black-Curious Case of Cybercrime Kingpin Max Vision
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

This session will detail the criminal innovations and industry vulnerabilities that spawned the explosive growth of computer intrusion as a for-profit criminal endeavor. Our roadmap will be the singular career of Max Vision, a former security researcher who turned to the dark side and became a leader in the billion-dollar credit card fraud underground.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- How to Recruit Spies on the Internet
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

The Internet, especially social networking, allows for sharing of information. This sharing is a gold mine for spies, who need to find people with access to sensitive information. This session will tell how spies identify and recruit people through social media and similar venues.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Advanced Persistent Threats: War Stories from the Front Lines
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Confused by the marketing hype that surrounds APT, the latest buzzword in security? APT is not a botnet, malware code or a new term for cybercrime. What is it? You will find out if you attend this panel of battle-hardened experts that have been facing this threat for years in government and enterprise networks. Hear their experiences and lessons learned for detecting and responding to APT attacks.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Misconceptions of Security
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Paul Kocher explores misconceptions about security, including those he has been guilty of. Fallacies discussed include categorizing security and insecurity as binary states, assuming that additional paperwork will improve security, dismissing TSA's screening as useless theater, and overestimating the human brain's ability to comprehend complex systems.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Extreme Makeover: Open Source Edition
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

In the spirit of ABC's reality TV show, Fortify's Brian Chess and Jacob West will bring their combined experience to bear on an open source project. They will lead a panel of security experts in a critique of the project's security. This lighthearted session is for newbies who want to watch a real live dissection take place and pros who need a dose of schadenfreude.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- The Dishonest Minority: Security as Society's Enabler
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Security systems divide into two types. In direct security there are distinct attackers and defenders. Societal security ensures we adhere to the social contract with no free riders - attackers and defenders are the same. We'll explore the uniquely human implications of societal security: how it follows the rise of society and civilization and protects us from the dishonest minority amongst us.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Cyber War: How We Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Cyber Bomb
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Cyber War is a controversial subject, with some experts arguing that the whole idea is overhyped while others argue that it is underappreciated. Who is right? This distinguished panel of experts, assembled by IEEE Security & Privacy magazine, will discuss cyber war. Where do these ideas come from? What do they mean to information security and risk management professionals?

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Public, Meet Private: Lessons Learned in Chasing Cyber Crooks
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Hear from law enforcement and security professionals on how they worked together on some of the biggest cybercrime cases to date. What made those collaborations succeed where others failed? Is it getting easier or harder for the public and private sectors to work together? What does each side need to learn from the other, and what emerging policies could improve the situation?

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Don't Teach Developers Security
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

The general message preached for the past couple of years is that developers need to learn security and training developers in security will give us vulnerability-free code. This presentation is will destroy that myth and put forth that this is the WRONG way of creating secure code. It's time to simplify the secure development process.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- DNSSEC: A Discussion with the Experts
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

The participants on the panel -- Jim Bidzos, Rod Beckstrom, Whit Diffie, Paul Mocakpetris and Dan Kaminsky -- will provide an update on the latest milestones in the adoption of DNSSEC and their thoughts on how the adoption of DNSSEC will help remediate risks in Internet security. The experts will discuss the potential impact of the full implementation of DNSSEC in .COM and its implication for the security community.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Encore: The Machinery of Cybercrime: Uncut and Uncensored!
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Slick front ends, a database build for performance, and good quality control: welcome to the new world of hacker tools developed by cybercriminals and terrorists. This session examines the tools of real hacking: command and control for botnets, spam management, encryption tools used by terrorists. See first-hand how advanced cyber crime has become. In your organization prepared for attack?

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- ENCORE: A Practical Approach to Risk Management
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

This talk will present a risk management framework that can be used to monitor compliance, evaluate risk, communicate with various levels of management and help drive business decisions that are in alignment with the business objectives and the risk tolerance of the organization. It will give attendees practical tools that they can take away and begin using immediately.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011--Encore: Risk and Resilience Considerations for Info Security Risk Assessment
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

The CERT Resilience Management Model (CERT-RMM) defines processes for managing operational resilience in complex risk-evolving environments. This presentation will discuss the concepts and principles of operational risk, link operational risk and operational resilience, present a framework for operational risk management, and introduce aspects of CERT-RMM.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011--Next 20 Years Interacting with Computers, Telecommunication, AI in the Future
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

What will computers and the internet look like in 20 years. The internet in our contact lens, computers controlled by the mind, nanobots attacking cancer cells. Dr. Michio Kaku will explore how artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, and quantum mechanics will play keys roles in the development of these and other innovations in the not so distant future, especially as Moore's Law begins to break down.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- "Who Are You?" When Security Hinges on Identity
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Each IT trend brings new security challenges. Today, consumerization challenges the control over which devices access networks. The Cloud challenges the control over applications and infrastructure. Collaboration challenges the control of information once it crosses enterprise boundaries. This discussion will explore how answering the most basic question-- "Who are you?" -- could be the key to navigating these trends.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Driving Security Down the Stack
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

The explosive growth of Internet and IP-enabled devices is reshaping communication, collaboration and commerce opportunities for individuals and organizations around the world. At the same time, miscreants are abusing the Internet's open and any-to-any communication architecture for malicious purposes, leaving many users at risk and the future of a secure Internet as an aspiration rather than a reality. The current cybersecurity model is reactive, disconnected and unable to keep pace with the seismic explosion in malware. Providing protection to a heterogeneous world of connected devices requires a new approach to security. McAfee CTO George Kurtz will show that incremental improvements can't bridge the opportunity gap and explain the required paradigm shift of driving security down the stack.

snippet.title: RSA®Conference 2011--Security in the Era of Cloud Computing--Live Discussion Twitter (#RSACcloud)
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

As cloud computing adoption accelerates, the security model is shifting from the network layer to focus more on the data and where it resides within global datacenters. This major shift in computing is forcing enterprises, vendors and security professionals to rethink their security model in order to make the data secure yet accessible everywhere. Technology futurist Paul Saffo will host a lively discussion on this topic with two cloud computing pioneers, Philippe Courtot of Qualys and Dave Cullinane of eBay/CSA, taking live questions from the audience via Twitter (#RSACcloud).

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- The Department of Defense, Active Cyber Defense, and the Secure Zone
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

As the threat facing our military networks and valued information evolves, the Department of Defense (DoD) is adapting its defenses in cyberspace and improving cybersecurity while safeguarding civil liberties and privacy. General Alexander will discuss key DoD cyber initiatives over the past year, including the establishment of U.S. Cyber Command, explain DOD's approach to active cyber defense, and introduce the concept of a Secure Zone.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- "The Murder Room": Breaking the Coldest Cases
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Bestselling author Michael Capuzzo reveals the inner workings of the mysterious Vidocq Society: celebrated forensic investigators tackling unsolved murder cases that have confounded conventional techniques. Michael will be joined by Vidocq Society members: William Fleisher and Richard Walter. The collaboration of these brilliant minds will set an inspiring example to the RSA Conference community.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Secure This: Every Device, Every Cloud, Every Moment
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Enterprise security is built for a network that is quickly disappearing. With the disappearance of enterprise perimeters, the rise of mobile devices, the cloud, and always-connected workers changing the game, the need for a new security model is paramount. Tom Gillis discusses how a new fabric of trust over the global network will make security transparent for every user and safer for every administrator.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Secure, Global Collaboration Made Possible
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Balancing the need to share critical information with the obligation to prevent it from falling into the wrong hands is one of the greatest challenges government and industry face today. Join CA Technologies and Transglobal Secure Collaboration Program members for a discussion of how aerospace and defense organizations are securely collaborating on projects across international borders.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Securing the Enterprise in a Changing World
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

An applications transformation has begun, creating both challenges and opportunities: with users (consumers) demanding everything as a service, anywhere, how can enterprises secure critical corporate infrastructure assets and information? Building security into applications, assessing risk-- even before coding begins, and applying quality and operational management using ITIL concepts to the practice of security are key.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Letting Go and Keeping Control: Beyond the PC and Data Center
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

IT is being pulled in conflicting directions as users demand more choice over their devices and applications while management demands more security and control. The mission of IT is also growing much faster than resources. Symantec President and CEO Enrique Salem will give his perspective on resolving these conflicts through a new approach to IT architecture focused around people and information.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Defending a New Domain: The Pentagon's Cyber Strategy
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Digital networks undergird nearly every facet of U.S. military operations. The Pentagon recognizes the serious threat to its cyber security, and is partnering with allied governments and private companies to defend this new domain of war. Secretary Lynn will characterize the threat, describe the Pentagon's strategy, and call on industry to develop new technologies that reverse the present advantage held by those seeking to penetrate computer networks.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- The Cryptographers' Panel
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Join the founders of the field for an engaging discussion about the latest advances in cryptography, research areas to watch in 2011 and practical insights that continue to be drawn from lessons learned over the last three decades.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Collective Defense: Collaborating to Create a Safer Internet
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

As people move more data and information into the Cloud, the need for secure, private and reliable services is growing from a technology concern within the industry, to a societal concern for citizens around the world. Microsoft Corporate Vice President for Trustworthy Computing, Scott Charney, will discuss how the growing alignment of social, economic, political and technical forces are creating a situation where the industry has the potential to make substantial security progress.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- The Hugh Thompson Show
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Internet security guru and author Dr. Herbert "Hugh" Thompson has seen it all -- hacked voting machines, airline computer insecurities, e-commerce vulnerabilities and cell phone exploits. For the fifth year running, Thompson brings a lifetime of security expertise and a wide-eyed enthusiasm to "The Hugh Thompson Show" at this year's RSA Conference. Become part of the action as Thompson takes center stage, interviewing some very special guests.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Cyberwar, Cybersecurity, and the Challenges Ahead
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

In this keynote panel, explore the complex and evolving issues tied to cybersecurity and conflict in cyberspace in the 21st Century from leading experts in the field. Moderated by Dr. James Lewis of the Center for Strategic and International Studies, this session will include discussion on thresholds for cyber war, the often confusing terminology used for various types of cyber conflict, and what needs to be done in the international context to secure cyberspace while also deterring the possible escalation of various kinds of cyber attacks and conflict.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Trust in the Cloud: Proof Not Promises
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Organizations worldwide have high hopes for the cloud. Hope in its potential to transform IT infrastructures, applications, and information management and in its ability to revolutionize business. But before we can trust that the cloud is safe for real business, we need a secure foundation of dynamic controls and trustworthy measurement. Art Coviello and Richard McAniff unveil innovative advances toward a trusted cloud.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Is it Time to Put HIPS in the Recycle Bin?
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Host Intrusion Prevention System technology is intended to prevent malicious software from running. Unfortunately, it is proving to be problematic, resulting in excessive support costs, high false positives and labor-intensive behavioral rules. In this session, Eric Ogren of the Ogren Group will do a side-by-side comparison of behavioral HIPS to Application Whitelisting.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Awareness for the ADD and ADHD Society
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Using Web 2.0 technologies, this fast-paced seminar will demonstrate unusual but effective methods to enhance and expand your enterprise security awareness program. Audio, video, subliminal messages, Twitter, blogs, Wikis, webinars, RSS feeds, Facebook and LinkedIn communities will demonstrate effective and evolving methods to engage your organization while significantly improving your program.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Trends in Mobile Authentication and Fraud Deterrence
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Authentication on handsets has become critically important as these devices become more capable and more connected. However, passwords are frustrating on handsets, which makes users take insecure shortcuts. This calls for a redesign of mobile authentication. We describe some recent results on when and how to authenticate, and show concretely how to apply the results of this research.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Loose Lips Sink Networks Is Social Networking Making Your Network Insecure?
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Social networks pose a number of threats to companies and organizations. We will explore how these threats manifest, how hackers use social networks to increase the effectiveness of social engineering and other attacks, and how organizational policy can limit these threats. Additionally, we will discuss a number of attacks that have been seen in the wild that used social networks to propagate.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011--What Happens in Vegas Goes on YouTube Security & Corporate Social Networks
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Social networks simultaneously offer huge business benefits and unheard-of security risks. How can enterprises effectively use social networks, while not putting their security and data at risk? This presentation will discuss these issues.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Government Information Security: The State of the Union
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

This session draws insights from Information Security Media Group's inaugural Government Information Security Today survey to review the top trends, threats and solutions for federal, state and local government agencies. Topics include cybersecurity policy, regulatory compliance, cloud computing and other emerging technologies.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- PKI, Lemon Markets and Lemonade
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

While much attention has been given to PKI and PKI technology, very little is usually said about its actual, rather than claimed, effectiveness as an overall security measure. This session examines PKI's shortcomings -- copiously illustrated with examples ranging from the trivial, to the scary, to the comical -- as well as what works in the real world.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Rethinking Passwords
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Traditional password advice and rules are seldom appropriate for today's threats, yet we labor with the password rules and servers of yesteryear. Strong passwords are weakening our security, and it is time to fix that. There are numerous proposals for new password solutions. This session will present a few half-baked ideas, but there are good solutions available now. We ought to get this easy stuff right!

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- The Manchurian Device Problem
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

How do we protect U.S. critical infrastructure for a cyber attack when most, if not all, of the control equipment is manufactured overseas? In this presentation, you will see a simple, practical infrastructure that allows devices manufactured in an untrusted environment to be made highly trustworthy.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- The Machinery of Cybercrime: Uncut and Uncensored!
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Slick front ends, a database build for performance, and good quality control: welcome to the new world of hacker tools developed by cybercriminals and terrorists. This session examines the tools of real hacking: command and control for botnets, spam management, encryption tools used by terrorists. See first-hand how advanced cyber crime has become. In your organization prepared for attack?

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011--U.S. Cyber Challenge Developing the Next Generation of Cyber Guardians
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Where will the nation get the 20,000 technical security experts the military and industry need to protect their systems and to fight in cyberspace? The U.S. Cyber Challenge is the most promising answer. Thousands of young people have participated in competitions and dozens have attended intensive summer cyber camps in CA, DE, and NY. This year all states will be eligible.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Ethical Considerations Involving the Use of Force in Cyberspace
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Unclassified discussions of offensive activities in cyberspace have begun to occur, though the ethics remain murky. Greater open dialogue must occur about the policy implications and practical realities around the "use of force" and acts of war in cyberspace. This session will look at the ethical issues that arise in these areas and stimulate debate about how such techniques should be used.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- How Malware Authors Are Winning the War
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Unclassified discussions of offensive activities in cyberspace have begun to occur, though the ethics remain murky. Greater open dialogue must occur about the policy implications and practical realities around the "use of force" and acts of war in cyberspace. This session will look at the ethical issues that arise in these areas and stimulate debate about how such techniques should be used.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Drive By Downloads: How to Avoid Getting a Cap Popped in Your App
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

This talk will present state-of-the-art web-based malware attacks and describe how the techniques used have evolved over time. Learn how today's attackers use additional mechanisms to inject malicious code, conduct multiple injections into a single web page, use multi-DOM node injections, foil first generation web-based malware scanners and rely on social engineering technologies.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- A Study on The State of Web Security
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

It's 2010. Why are we still dealing with drive-by downloads? This session combines telemetry data from two web security products with millions of users to answer some of today's top questions. Where are the malicious payloads hosted? How are criminals infecting legitimate sites? Do we really want to block the unintentionally malicious sites? Use these answers to optimize your web security efforts.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- BlackBerry Security FUD Free
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

As mobile computing devices proliferate the enterprise, more people are raising flags about mobile device security. One device that is dominant in the enterprise mobile computing world is the ubiquitous BlackBerry®, which has quite a bit of Fear, Uncertainty, and Doubt surrounding its security controls. This presentation aims to set the facts straight by going to the source - literally.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Lightning Round: Mobile Security the Ugly Truth
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

106A: Why Mobile and Security Don't Mix -- Yet
106B: Profiting from Mobile Malware, Russian Style

The first session sets the stage and the challenges for both mobile carriers and security companies to prevent data breaches or enterprise IT attacks. The second session illustrates how Russian cybercriminals are utilizing mobile malware to generate profits and take advantage of Russian laws.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- TLS Renegotiation Vulnerability
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

The TLS renegotiation vulnerability, discovered in late 2009, is a serious security issue that has real-world attack scenarios for many SSL and TLS deployments. What steps can be taken to protect from these attack scenarios? Which vendors have fixes in place and how many 'secure' websites are still vulnerable?

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Combat IT Sabotage: Technical Solutions from the CERT Insider Threat Lab
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

CERT has developed strategies to help organizations combat insider threat, based on a database of over 400 actual cases and with over nine years of research. To test these proposed strategies, CERT created the Insider Threat Lab to simulate events from actual cases. This panel will present three of these simulations and demonstrate how to best deploy countermeasures against malicious insider IT sabotage activities.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Aspire to a Network Free of Malicious Programs
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Aspire of Western New York serves people with intellectual and neurological impairments through nearly 50 group homes and field offices. Aspire system administrator, Dave Compton, and Webroot CTO, Gerhard Eschelbeck, will present how the virus "Sality" infected Aspire's network and impacted its operations in 2009, and how Aspire secured its network, patients, students and employees after the attack.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Why Johnny Can't Navigate Away from this iFrame: A PHP Malware Primer
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

The past several years have seen a boom in the sheer volume of malicious applications for the Windows platform, but there has been a more secretive, parallel growth spurt in a different form of malicious code: PHP-based scripts, hosted on hijacked or compromised web servers. We'll provide an overview of the malware landscape in this largely undiscussed, but growing, problem.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Wireless Vulnerabilities in the Wild: View from the Trenches
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Today, it is well known that wireless is indeed a threat to enterprise network security. However, empirical data that provides insights into the degree of wireless threats in an enterprise is still lacking. This session presents what we believe to be the first-ever empirical analysis of enterprise wireless threat space based on customer deployments.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Browsing Known Sites is Safe -- True or False?
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Web-based malware silently waits between the user's machine and the malware distribution servers and is mostly used to mediate local machine infection. The number of infected websites is growing each year and the popular mantra of "browsing known websites is safe - threats come from pornographic and warez sites", is no longer true.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Building a Global Privacy Program Leveraging Binding Corporate Rules
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

This session will cover a sample approach for developing a global privacy program based on binding corporate rules, including key activities, critical success factors, and program accelerators.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Red Pill, Blue Pill -- Prescriptions for Curing Compliance Complexity
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

You take the blue pill - the story ends, you wake up in your bed and believe whatever you want to believe. You take the red pill - you stay in Wonderland and I show you how deep the rabbit hole goes. This session will include practical lessons from industry experts on slashing the cost and risk in complex compliance environments.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Mapping an Organization's DNA Using Social Media
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

This session will depict a detailed research into the social media presence of a random sample of 20 businesses and their employees who are active on social networks. The objective is to map out the DNA of the organization, and demonstrate the relative ease with which applications such as Twitter and Facebook can be leveraged to gather advanced business intelligence.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Payment Data in 2011 and Beyond: Investigating Updates to the PCI Standards
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

The Council has completed a series of key initiatives in recent months including the launch of PTS 3.0, DSS 2.0, PA-DSS 2.0, and guidance on emerging technologies. This session will provide practical insights on how security executives can use PCI standards and payment card industry tools to protect their customers' data and develop a comprehensive security strategy.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Metrics are Bunk!?: The Zombie Apocalypse, Baseball, and Security Metrics
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Metrics are BUNK! No, metrics will save us! Two smart guys debate both sides. In a zombie apocalypse, it's a game of survival. As IT security matures and crawls out of the primordial ooze, we look to metrics to lift us from chaos. The desire is rational, but is it tangible? Amidst constant change, which metrics matter? Which don't? What are the limits? Can they ever keep up with rates of change?

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- A Practical Approach to Risk Management
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

This talk will present a risk management framework that can be used to monitor compliance, evaluate risk, communicate with various levels of management and help drive business decisions that are in alignment with the business objectives and the risk tolerance of the organization. It will give attendees practical tools that they can take away and begin using immediately.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Security Metrics: A Beginner's Guide
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

In today's economic environment, limited resources for information security programs have become even more constrained. CISOs must pick the right metrics and align with business goals to justify funding for information security priorities. This session discusses the importance and benefits of measuring security, and offers practical advice for practitioners looking to build or improve a security metrics program.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- The Psychology of Risk: Why Understanding Human Behavior is Essential
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

This session examines empirical studies around common assumptions associated with risk and risk mitigation. The presentation will challenge common risk mitigation strategies of utilizing technical solutions, awareness training, and sanctions policies. A major surprise is that empirical studies find many common mitigation strategies are, at best, ineffective—and, at worse, counterproductive!

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Overlooked Security Threats of Data Recovery Operations
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

79% of IT security and support practitioners reported that their organizations have used, or will continue to use, a third-party data recovery service. As use of data recovery services grows, so does the threat of a data breach -- often due to a vendor's lack of data security protocols. Panelists review security threats, and actual breach events and outline recommended protocols.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2010 -- Thirty Thousand Records, Four Weeks, and No Time to Lose
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

EMC is one of the world's leading providers of infrastructure information systems and services. A global sweep of enterprise data revealed 30,000 unprotected records. This session will reveal how EMC designed and executed a data remediation exercise that secured all these records within a 30-day time frame rather than the four to five months it typically takes for a project of this size.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2010 -- Behind the Verizon Business 2010 Data Breach Investigations Report
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Every year, Verizon Business publishes the Data Breach Investigations Report (DBIR), which presents a unique view into how victims get breached, as well as how to prevent data breaches. This session will examine this data, culled from forensic investigations carried out by Verizon Business and the U.S. Secret Service.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About DLP
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

From technology and process to real-world experiences, this session will cover everything you need to know to evaluate, implement and succeed with data loss prevention. This session will detail the technology fundamentals, selection process, pragmatic implementation strategies, ongoing management, and even a few use cases.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Trusted IaaS
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) is an essential component of cloud computing, yet there are concerns about security: data protection, integrity and compliance. This session covers in depth the capabilities that meet this need, including service identity, platform trust, audit and service partitioning, shared storage, and policy-driven management.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Cloud Investigations and Forensics
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Cloud computing's growth in popularity has been due to the lure of inexpensive and redundant storage, computation and services. This presentation provides an analysis of what happens when things go wrong, by looking at real-world cloud computing investigations and digital forensics. It proposes a set of technical and legal recommendations to reduce risk.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Scanning the Ten Petabyte Cloud: Finding the Malware that Isn't There
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Cloud storage of websites attracts a new kind of malware: well-behaved hooks that link to malware stored elsewhere.
Conventional malware detection techniques don't find these. Learn how to force the adversary to hide in plain sight, to scan quickly and efficiently, and to write malware scanners your adversary can't buy off a shelf. Working knowledge of web application security helpful.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- A Changing Industry: The 2011 Global Information Security Workforce Study
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

A panel of top information security industry experts will discuss the results of the 2011 Global Information Security Workforce Study, based on the world's largest survey of professionals. Released exclusively at RSA Conference 2011, the study will cover current threats and challenges, technology solutions, in-demand job skills, security budgets, hiring outlook, training requirements, current salaries, and more.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Security Business Cases: Fact and Fiction in Selling Security
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Many CISOs dread the budget cycle, frustrated for lack of a persuasive business case. This updated session for RSA Conference 2011 looks at key parts of an infosec business case. The objections will be flushed out and neutralized, the needed alliances will be forged, and success will be yours. Attendees take away a useful template to craft business cases for the key elements of their information security programs.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Making Security Decisions Disappear into the User's Workflow
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Security dialog boxes are annoying and largely incomprehensible. A lot of research is being done to make them more understandable. We wondered if people understand them at all. We have developed a set of design principles that let us unambiguously infer the user's security decisions from actions they take to get their work done.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Agile Development, Security Fail
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Transition from Waterfall to Agile always leaves some tasks behind, and secure code development is one of the casualties. Focusing on the efficient delivery of features, textbook implementations of Agile come at the expense of secure software development, and push security verification and services outside of the software. This session will examine this issue.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Intelligence on the Intractable Problem of Insecure Software
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

On an almost daily basis, news of data breaches and cyber threats remind us that the security of our critical financial and public services software infrastructure is inadequate. Software is the very fabric of how the world communicates and conducts business. This session offers actionable information designed to protect organizations from the very real and costly impact of insecure software.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- Innovation in Application Security
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Since today's applications are made up of multiple pre-compiled components, libraries and open source, organizations need to establish an application portfolio risk management process to protect themselves from the inherent security threats. While no software will ever be perfectly secure, there are steps you can take to mitigate your organization's risk. This talk will show you how.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 -- The Evolution of Software Security Assurance and its Relevance Today
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Secure software means threat modeling, code review, penetration testing, and a plethora of other activities we take for granted. Right? Starting with Saltzer and Schroeder, this talk explores the origins, evolution, and use of these activities and others. Throughout, we share deployment experience and relate the discussion to living standards, such as Microsoft SDL, OWASP Top 10, and PCI DSS.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011-Stop Exposing Yourself: Principles of Attack Surface Analysis and Reduction
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Reducing your application's attack surface is one of the most effective ways to improve its security. This session will examine how to analyze and reduce attack surface while still allowing developers to add new exciting and delighting features that users love. This session will also include demonstrations of new tools to help find hidden attack surface in your applications before attackers find it for you.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011- Luring Your Prey:The Art of Effectively Communicating with a Cyber Predator
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Engaging an online predator requires strategic communication skills. Unlike face-to-face communication where body language, voice qualities and language patterns are easily accessible, online communication demonstrates unique challenges. If your intention is to engage, communicate, draw-out and stop an online cyber predator, this presentation is for you.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 - Software Security: The Big Picture
snippet.description:
Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference

Adopting the mythical "hacker's toolbox", we have become experts in many awkwardly specialized security disciplines, welding together an ever-growing collection of esoteric technology and spending a lot of money on security products; yet we still get hacked. This talk will explore ways to tie together today's silos of security data into a holistic view of system security.

snippet.title: RSA® Conference 2011 Pecha Kucha Night - Uri Rivner
snippet.description: Visit http://www.rsaconference.com for more information about the RSA® Conference
